title: What is Life All About?
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: In this program Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that the world's biggest problem is neither war, disease nor poverty but that people do not know who they are, mistaking the body they see in a mirror for the self. He distinguishes body from soul, calls the body a garment worn for fifty or a hundred years, and observes that people feed the body three meals a day while giving the real person nothing, describing the soul as literally a piece of the breath God breathed into Adam and claiming it can grow to immense size when nourished. He says the nourishment is a specific method rather than vague spirituality or ordinary supplication: five daily contacts with God following what he compares to the numerical combination of a safe, with fasting as a further practice, and he offers newly obtained mathematically coded evidence as his authority. Citing the Barbara Hutton story and Eddie Murphy's interview with Barbara Walters as cases of wealth without happiness, he closes by inviting viewers to examine the physical evidence free of charge, giving an address on East 6th Street in Tucson and a telephone number.

title: Who is GOD?
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that idol worship persists because people do not grasp the greatness of God, and devotes the sermon to establishing that scale from what he presents as established scientific facts. He works outward from the solar system, whose sunlight reaches Earth in four minutes and whose span runs to billions of miles, to the Milky Way, which light would take a hundred thousand years to cross, to a neighboring galaxy two million light years away, to a universe of a billion galaxies and a billion trillion stars measuring some 26 billion light years across, pausing to calculate that merely counting a quintillion stars at one per second would take 32 billion years. He then states, on the authority of the Quran and its mathematical code, that this universe is the smallest and innermost of seven, so that no number can express the circumference of the outermost, and cites Sura 39:67 on the heavens held in God's hand as an allegory for that greatness. He concludes that against this scale it is blasphemous to attribute to God a son, wife or mother, or to idolize Muhammad, Jesus, Mary or a saint, asking what role any of them played in setting the synchronized rotation of the moon or the precision of the orbits. Recording date: this is the Friday sermon of 4 August 1988. It was also uploaded separately as a dated Friday sermon, and that upload was the only place the date was stated; the two were proven to be one recording by a flat timestamp offset across sixteen minutes, so the duplicate entry was merged into this one and its dating carried over. This transcript is the fuller of the two, being the only one to include the opening takbirs from 00:01:19.

title: Witness a Miracle
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Recorded in January 1986, this program opens from Carl Sagan's novel Contact, quoting its account of a decoded message from outer space and Sagan's own hope that the book would be made obsolete by real scientific discovery, which Dr. Rashad Khalifa claims has now happened. He traces one message delivered through Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, David, Jesus and Muhammad, all mathematically coded in their original languages, cites Studies in Jewish Mysticism and Rabbi Judah the Pious on a numerical harmony in the prayer text and on nineteen occurrences of the divine name in the morning prayer, and presents the Quran as the only original scripture still intact. He walks through the counts of the Quranic initials, Q in chapters 50 and 42, N in chapter 68, Y and S in chapter 36, and explains that 19 is the numerical value of the Arabic word for one. The program closes with the scale of the universe, the seven universes he says the Quran describes as held in God's hand, and his Tucson address and telephone number for questions.

title: Mathematical Miracle of Quran
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa narrates how he came to the Quran's mathematical code and then walks through the findings one by one with a printed Quran in hand. He recounts arriving in the United States in 1968, disliking every English translation he read, and beginning his own for his children with a pledge not to pass a verse until he understood it, which stopped him at the initials A.L.M. of Sura 2; finding no scholar who could explain them, he entered the whole Quran into a computer and after four years of counting found 19 binding all fourteen sets of initials. The body of the program presents the counts in sequence: nineteen letters in the opening verse, 114 chapters, the first revelation positioned above the last nineteen chapters with nineteen words and 76 letters, the four words of the Bismillah occurring 19, 2698, 57 and 114 times, the missing Bismillah of Sura 9 restored by an extra one in Sura 27 exactly nineteen chapters later whose numbers total 342, matching the count of words between them, 6346 verses in all, and 5263 verses between the first and last initials. He continues through the words for Quran, for God being one, and for the five pillars, then the individual initial groups, Q in Suras 50 and 42, N in Sura 68, Saad across three chapters, Ya Seen in Sura 36, the seven H.M. chapters totalling 2147, and the A.L.M. and A.L.R. groups. The program closes with his answer to why the number is 19: that it is the numerical value of the Arabic word for one, in the system where alphabet letters served as numerals before Arabic numbers existed.

title: Essentials of Submission (Islam)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: A compilation program in which Dr. Rashad Khalifa sets out the essentials of Islam as he understands them, followed by three shorter appended segments. He presents Islam as beginning with Adam, with Abraham as the founder who delivered every religious practice and Muhammad contributing only the Quran, which he says was placed in the prophet's heart in one night and released over twenty-three years to aid memorization. He then goes through the five pillars: the shahada of Sura 3:18 with no name added beside God's, the five contact prayers and their units, the fasting of Ramadan whose movement through the seasons he reads as a test that sifts out those who will only fast on short cool days, the zakat of 2.5 percent of net worth following the Quran's order of recipients, and the hajj, whose steps he lists while advising against the visit to Medina and against going before one's faith is settled. The program covers the prohibitions, four forbidden meats, intoxicants and gambling, and closes with three appended segments: a correction to how zakat is timed, an emphasis on the Dawn Prayer, and a 1987 appeal to form Universal Unity through devotion to God alone by rising above the human figures that divide believers who all already believe in God. Related recordings: the zakat and Dawn Prayer segments also appear in "45 - Friday Sermon Purpose of Messengers, The Advent of the Pure Quran (03-17-1989)" and "43 - Friday Sermon Revelation of Quran to Revelation of Miracle, Importance of Dawn Prayer (02-03-1989)"; the Universal Unity appeal is developed in "23 - Friday Sermon Universal Unity Through Devotion to GOD Alone."

segments.text: The second pillar of Islam is the Contact Prayers [Specified actions and words]
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: There are 5 Contact Prayers per day, Morning, Noon, Afternoon, Sunset, and the Night Contact.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: These are the daily meals for the soul to nourish the real person [That's you].
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The third pillar of Islam is fasting, in
Arabic, SIYAM.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
God commands us to fast during one
month of the year, and it is the ninth
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
month of the lunar calendar.
Now, I'm smiling because there is a
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
tremendous test in this system, where the
lunar year is shorter than the solar year,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and this makes the month of Ramadan
move about 10 to 15 days every year.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, it comes in the winter sometimes when
the day is nice and short and fasting is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
very easy, and moves to the summer where
the days are very long, 16 hours or more
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
sometimes, and the day is hot and you
can't eat or drink during this long
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
period. And a lot of people will drop out.
They will... they will not fast even though
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
nobody dies by not eating or
drinking for 24 hours. But some people
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
will drop out and you can see that the
system is designed to show who will fast
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and would obey God's commandment, no matter
how long the day is.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
This changing of the day from short and
cold to long and hot days will show
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
us who are the dropouts, who will fast
only if the day is short and nice and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
cold. So, this is the second pillar of
Islam, fasting during the month of
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Ramadan, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The third pillar of Islam is Fasting during one month [Ramadan].
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: From dawn to sunset, Muslims do not eat or drink or have any sexual activity [during Ramadan]
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
As you see, the fasting of Ramadan is
also designed to tame the wild horse,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
your body. See, your body wants to eat and
drink,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and you, the real person or the soul,
dictates on the body saying "no, you're
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
not going to eat or drink until sunset."
Because the fasting consists of not
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
eating or drinking or engaging in intercourse,
sexual intercourse from dawn
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
to sunset. Dawn means about two hours
before sunrise to sunset, no eating, no
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
drinking, no sex. And this is control of
your wild horse.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You are taming the wild horse, your body.
And you can see that God is training you,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
is teaching you to be a person of a
strong will,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and preparing you for the eternal life
of the Hereafter, the real life.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Because in the real life that comes after this
life, God wants the people who are strong,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
who practice and exercise and know
how to control themselves, I mean, their
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
their bodies. This also causes your soul to
feed, grow and develop.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Fasting makes you the boss, not your "body" ... The soul commands the body to control itself.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Fasting prepares us for a position of prominence and leadership in the real life [Hereafter].
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The fourth pillar of Islam is charity, in
Arabic, ZAKAT. There is an obligatory
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: charity where you sit down and you calculate exactly what you possess, what
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: your possessions are, and you give away a portion,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: a fixed portion of your net worth. You do this once a year.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: You pick out a specific day in the year, the last day of Ramadan, the first day of Ramadan,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: or the first day of January, one day, one fixed day in the year.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And you sit down on that day and you calculate how much you are worth.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: This means you add up the market value of your house, your car, your clothes,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: anything that you posses if you sell it all today. How much will it be worth?
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The fair market value, not the new... the price of the new thing, no, the present
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: market value of everything you posses. And then you give away 2.5% of that.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: See? It's a small percentage. And you do it once a year.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And it goes to specific people.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The Quran lists them in this priority:
first your parents.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
If your parents are rich...
and these are the recipients of your
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
charity. If your parents are rich, the
second in the list are you relatives.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You give this 2.5%, you
give it to your relatives. If they're all rich,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
then you find some orphans, people who do
not have support, parental support, a father
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
support or something. And you give
this charity to them.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
After the orphans, you give to the alien,
somebody who's traveling and is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: stranded and doesn't have the money or the bus fare to go to his home town,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: you help that person. So, the order in the Quran is: the parents, the relatives,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the orphans, the traveling alien, the poor
the beggars and so on. So, there is a
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
specific order for giving these
charities. However, there is also
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
a general charity called "Sadaqa" and
this is an on-the-spot charity. You're
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
walking in the street and you see a poor
person and you want to help, then you
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
help that person and this is called
"Sadaqa" or charity. You're supposed to be
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
charitable the whole year, all the time.
You must be charitable. But the ZAKAT
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
is the obligatory charity where you give
it to someone you personally know.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You personally know that this fellow is poor
and needs help and you give your 2.5%
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
to these people that
you personally know. You cannot consider
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the taxes, for example, as ZAKAT charity,
because you don't know where the taxes
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
will go. They can go to fix the street or
something, or to the army or something.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But the idea behind ZAKAT is that you
give it to the people that you
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
personally know are in need. And the
Quran, as I said, lists the parents first,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the relatives, your own - you start with
your own people then you go to
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: other strangers in that order.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The fourth pillar of Islam is Zakat charity.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Zakat is obligatory once a year and is 2.5% of your net worth at the time..
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Quran specifies the recipients as people you know, beginning with your parents
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The fifth pillar of Islam is Hajj
pilgrimage to the Holy Land in Mecca.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And this is only, of course, for the
people who can afford it. When you can
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
afford it, you go to Mecca and you
observe Hajj, and this is commemoration of
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the prophet Abraham,
not the man Abraham but his
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
exemplary submission to God.
He thought... he saw a dream one time and he thought
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
that God was commanding him to sacrifice
his only son, Ismail.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And he proceeded to carry out this
command even though God did not order
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
him to do it. He just thought in a dream that
God was ordering him to do it. But he was
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
willing to sacrifice his own son in
submission to God, and of course, God
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
intervened to save Ismail and Abraham
from this tragedy. And God
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
substituted a sheep to be sacrificed
instead of Ismail. And this is what you
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
do when you go to Hajj. So, and Hajj
consists of arriving in Mecca dressed
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: only in untailored clothes, just a sheet or something.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: and seamless shoes or sandals, seamless
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
clothes and seamless sandal. The women
dress in a regular dress that is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
simple. So, you cannot tell the rich from
the poor.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The fifth pillar of Islam is pilgrimage Hajj to Mecca.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: To observe Hajj, you go to
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Mecca dressed in seamless clothes and
seamless sandals. This is for the men.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The women dress modestly in regular
modest dress, all white dress, for
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
example, so you cannot tell the rich from
the poor. You get to Mecca and you go
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
around the Ka‘bah in Mecca seven times.
Then, you go between Safa and Marwah, the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: knolls of Safa and Marwah seven times. Then, you go to 'Arafat, Mount 'Arafat and you
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
stand there the whole day, which is the
10th day of the twelfth, the last month in
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the Islamic calendar. The tenth day of
the Hijr. You spend that whole day on
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Mount 'Arafat commemorating God,
worshiping and praying. And then, you go to
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Mina, it's a little town near Mecca.
You go to Mina for two or three days.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Then, you go back to the Ka‘bah, go around
it seven times, which is called the farewell
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
circumambulation around the Ka‘bah,
and this is it. Now, my advice to you is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
never to go to Medina because people go
to Medina and they ruin their Hajj. They
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
go to the Prophet Muhammad's tomb,
mausoleum, and they idolize the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
prophet and this ruins everything, ruins
the whole religion not just Hajj. So, Hajj
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
must be done only in Mecca where you go
around the Ka‘bah seven times, between
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Safa and Marwah seven times, you go to 'Arafat for one day and to Mina for two or
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
three days, and this is it. These are
specific steps that are mentioned in the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Quran. And by the way,
all these duties in Islam came to us
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
through the prophet Abraham. If you look
at Sura 22, the last verse, number 78,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you will see that Abraham is the source, is
the father of Islam and the father of
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Muslims. And if you look at Sura number
16 verse 123, you see that the prophet
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Muhammad followed the religion of
Abraham. Islam is the religion of
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Abraham. He's the founder of Islam. And
all the duties of Islam came from
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
IBRAHIM, not the prophet Muhammad.
Muhammad brought the Quran. God brought the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Quran through Muhammad. So, this is why
some people become confused when you
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
tell them that God says that the Quran
is complete, perfect and fully detailed.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Because some of the old traditionalists will say "ok, where is the number of Raka's
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
for the Noon prayer in the Quran?" See,
they forget that the contact prayers, the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
fasting of Ramadan, the ZAKAT charity, and
the Hajj pilgrimage, all these duties
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
came to us from Abraham, and the Quran
says so. If you look at Sura 21
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
verse 73, it tells you that Abraham
started the Salat and the Zakat. And in
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Sura 22 entitled Hajj, you see that
Abraham is the source of Hajj and so on.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The Quran says clearly that all duties
and obligations came to us through the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
prophet Abraham, and tells us in Sura  22
verse 78 that this is the religion
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
of Abraham. The prophet Muhammad simply
contributed the Quran. And the Quran
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
is God's words that came through Muhammad.
So, watch for this point and don't let anyone
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
trick you into thinking that the Quran
is not complete. The most important
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
principle in Islam is God ALONE. You must
be devoted to God alone. You do
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
not idolize the prophet Muhammad like
the Christians did with the prophet
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Jesus. You devote yourself completely to
God alone, and you follow the word of God
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
alone, the Quran alone, no other
sources. If you do,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you'll nullify all your work, as we see in
Sura 39 where God says if you fall
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
in idol worship, all your works are
nullified. You may do the Salat, the Zakat,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the charity, the Hajj, the fasting and all
this and it will be all in vain unless
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you are devoted to God alone. And you
will declare your SHAHADA
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
"Ash-hadu Alla Elaha Ella Allah." This is it.
So, these are the basic essentials of Islam.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: All our work would be nullified if we practice idol-worship. We must be devoted to God Alone.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The prohibitions are also
important. There are four meats that you
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
cannot eat, for example. And these are
number one, animals that die of
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
themselves without human interference.
Number two, pork, the meat of pigs. Number
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: three, running blood, running blood that you can put in a glass and cook or drink.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Number four, animals dedicated to other
than God that are specifically dedicated
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: to Muhammad or Jesus or Ali or somebody. These are forbidden. So, if you go to the market,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you go to Safeway Market, for example,
and you look at the meat, if you want to know
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
if it is HALAL, permitted or HARAM,
prohibited, you ask yourself these four
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
questions. Is this meat pork?
The answer is "no", then did these animals
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
die of themselves without human
interference? The answer is "no." Is this
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
running blood? The answer is "no." Was this
meat dedicated to Jesus or to anyone else or
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Saint Francis? The answer is "no." Therefore,
this meat is HALAL. It's ok. You can eat
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
it. If you make it HARAM, if you
prohibit it, then you are following some
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
other religion. You're not a Muslim
when you do that. So, it is very important
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
to follow specifically what the Quran
prohibits. If you prohibit anything else...
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
some people go to funny lengths like
prohibiting soaps and brushes and shoes
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and things like that, and of course, this
is a religion that is not Islam, has
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: nothing to do with Islam.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Four Prohibited Meats
1. Dead Animals.
2. Running Blood.
3. Meat of Pigs.
4. Dedicated to Idols
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Prohibitions not specifically mentioned in Quran belong to another religion.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Also prohibited are all intoxicants: alcohol,
marijuana, anything that will affect your
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
mind. All intoxicants, anything that
affects your capacity to think and to
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
have a healthy brain. So, all intoxicating
drugs, weeds and alcohol, all these are
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
prohibited. Also, gambling is prohibited.
Don't play the lottery. Believe me, it
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
will cost you more than... even if you win
the jackpot, you will end up a loser.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Believe me for this is God is in control
and He prohibited gambling, games of
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: chance of any kind.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Of course, the major prohibitions are
listed in the Quran: adultery is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
prohibited, murder, stealing, cheating,
lying. God wants you to be a perfect
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
person, a nice person. Even breaking the
promise is prohibited. You must be a
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
person of your word. You must be a man of
your word, or a woman of your word. When
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you say something, you do it and people
must know you as such. This is what a
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Muslim is all about.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: All intoxicants are prohibited: Alcohol, Marijuana, LSD, etc. Anything that alters your mind.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Islam is proven to be the best way to fight drug and alcohol abuse.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Now, some people are
fascinated by Hajj pilgrimage and they
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
just want to do it right away. You know,
they're fascinated by the exotic country,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you know, Saudi Arabia and the trip and
all that. But my advice to you is to
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
perfect your religion first. Believe me,
it is not a very pleasant trip. There's a
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
million and a half or two million people
making pilgrimage and it is a, an
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: exacting trial instead of enjoyment. You're not going as a tourist. It is a difficult
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
process and some people may become
disillusioned when they go too
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
early, before the faith is strong enough.
So, be sure you perfect your religion
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: first and then make the Hajj pilgrimage.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: One needs to perfect the religion before going to Hajj. About 10 good years of prep'n needed.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Performing Hajj too early, often leads to opposite results. Arrogance..... and loss of faith.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Another thing to guard against with
regard to Hajj is that some people go and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
do the Hajj pilgrimage like I said
before their faith is strong enough
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: and they come back puffed up and thinking "you know, I'm perfect now. You know, I'm
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
cool, and nobody is like me. I did Hajj, you
know." And it goes to their head.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And it brings the reverse result.
They become worse Muslims than
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
better Muslims. So, you want to go and do
Hajj pilgrimage after you perfect your
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
religion and this must make you humble,
more humble.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:

title: Principles of Contact Prayers Salat
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents an instructional program on the Contact Prayers (Salat), explaining that the word derives from an Arabic root meaning connection and locating all five daily prayer times in the Quran through Suras 11:114, 17:78, 2:238 and 24:58. He argues that the practices of Islam originated with Abraham rather than Muhammad, which is why the Quran does not specify the number of units, and describes the prayers as five daily meals that nourish the soul and make the real person master over the body. The second half removes what he identifies as later innovations from the Azan, the ablution and the prayer itself, insisting on four ablution steps, the recitation of Al-Fatehah alone, and the mention of no name besides God. The program closes with word-by-word transliteration of the Arabic, guidance on menstruation, group prayer and missed prayers, and filmed demonstrations of the morning, four-unit and sunset prayers. Related recording: the companion tape on the Friday congregational prayer is "18 - Principles of Friday Prayer" in this collection.

segments.text:
Allahu akbar; Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar;
Allahu akbar, La elaha ella Allah, there is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: no god except the one God, which is the message of all God’s messengers to the world.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
There's really one message from all the messengers
that God sent to us. And this message is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
la elaha ella allah, there is no god except
the God, Allah.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: So the Azaan consists of: Allahu akbar, 4 times, followed by la elaha ella Allah.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
This Azaan that has been approved by the prophet
consisting of Allahu akbar 4 times,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
then la elaha ella Allah, with time, it
got so long that in my lifetime, in 1953, the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Minister of Religious Affairs in Egypt issued
a law to reduce the Azaan. It got so long
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: and so ridiculous, it took 10 to 15 minutes to deliver the Azaan.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And it had foolish things praising the prophet
and his red cheeks and these silly things. I mean,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the Azaan got really ridiculous.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
After a few years, some people added to the
Azaan “Ash-hadu an la elaha ella Allah
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: wa ash-hadu anna Muḥammadan rasūlu Allah.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: This was added to the original Azaan.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Some years later, they added the expression
“ḥayya ʿalā ṣ-ṣalāh” which supposedly
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
means “come to the prayer”, but it really
doesn't mean that. Apparently, some new
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
foreign Muslims, that is non Arab Muslims,
added that expression “ḥayya ʿalā ṣ-ṣalāh”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
which is not a typical. The Arabic should
have been “ḥayya ʿilā ṣalāt”, but
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: they said “ḥayya ʿalā ṣ-ṣalā.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Then many years later, somebody added “ḥayya
ʿala l-falāḥ” which supposedly means
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: “come to the success.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And some other people added “ash-hadu anna alīyyan walīyyu Allah.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: in some parts of the Muslim world.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And until now, they use these... all these
additions are being used in different parts
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: of the Muslim world.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Later on, some people added the ” ash-hadu anna ahlul bayt hojato Allāh” and so on.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, the Azaan kept getting longer and longer,
as I told you, until the Minister of Religious
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Affairs in Egypt issued a law reducing the
Azaan to its present form in the Muslim world.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But here at Masjid Tuscon, and hopefully you
will go back to the original Azaan that the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
prophet Muhammad approved. Allahu akbar, Allahu
akbar, Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar, la elaha ella Allah.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
This is the Azaan that we use here in Masjid
Tuscon, and hopefully it will spread all over
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the world.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
We have it done like this in many mosques
around the world
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
that have seen the light and decided to take
the Azaan and the prayers to the original
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Azaan and prayer of the prophet Muhammad.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: You know the same thing is true with the Wuḍū.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Wuḍū is the ablution or the preparation
for Salat.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
When people hear the Azaan or the call to
the Contact Prayer, they prepare for the prayer,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And they do this by observing ablution. And
ablution is decreed in the Quran in Sura number 5
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: verse number 6.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And it is very specific. It gives you 4 steps. Remember that, 4 steps of ablution.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The average Muslim today has 8 or 9 or 10 steps
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
which constitutes actually in reality some
other god that added these steps, because
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
they do it religiously, and it constitutes
idolatry.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, please be careful, and observe what the
Quran says, the Quran, the whole Quran
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: and nothing but the Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And the Quran gives us 4 steps.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The first step is washing your face. The second
step is washing your arms to the elbow.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The third step is to wipe your hair. And the fourth step is to wash your feet.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
These are the 4 steps decreed in the
Quran, and it is actually a gross transgression
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
to add anything to the 4 steps, or
reduce anything.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Some people will say “what is wrong with washing my nose and my mouth and my neck and all the... my ears and so on?"
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Of course, there's nothing wrong with extra
cleanliness. Go take a bath or a shower if you want to.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: But when it comes to religious practices, we must adhere to what our creator dictated exactly.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
We cannot increase it, reduce it, or increase
it by anything.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, it is very crucial that we follow what
our creator said in the Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
These are the words that came out of the prophet
Muhammad’s mouth.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Ironically, those people think that they are
following the prophet Muhammad by increasing
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the number of steps in ablution. And you
and I know that the prophet Muhammad could never disobey God.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, if God said 4 steps, this is it.
The ablution is 4 steps.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: So, now let us go to show you, demonstrate for you the 4 steps of ablution, the Wuḍū.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: We find this commandment in Sura number 5, verse number 6.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And I will quote the verse for you. It says “O you who believe, when you get up for
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the Salat prayer, you shall wash your face,
your arms to the elbows, wipe your hair,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: and wash your feet.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
4 steps, and these are the words that
came out of the prophet Muhammad’s mouth.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: These are the words of God.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And God is saying "you shall observe the ablution 4 steps."
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Washing the face, arms to the elbows, wipe
your head, and wash your feet.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
These are the 4 steps as dictated in
Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
However, like everything else, innovations,
superstitions, traditions crept into God’s
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: commandment and Satan distorted the commandment.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Now, the vast majority of Muslims observe something
like 9 or 10 steps in ablution.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And this is very serious because it simply
means that there is some other god who told them
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
to do the ablution 9 steps. They wash
their hands, their mouth, their nose, their
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
face, their ears, their neck. They have all
kinds of innovations and additions.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And I would like to warn you that you must
never increase the steps or decrease them,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the steps of ablution. You must obey exactly
what God told you in Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
If you want to wash more, you might as well take
a shower or do whatever you want, but outside
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the ablution.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
If you are taking a shower or a bath, you
can do the ablution after the shower or the bath
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: while you are still in the shower.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But you have to go through the motions of
ablution as I will show you now.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, let me show you, demonstrate to you
how to do the ablution.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
First of all, you roll your sleeves so you
can wash your arms to the elbows.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: There we go. We are now demonstrating the ablution.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You go to the faucet, and the first step in
Quran is wash your face. So, you wash your face.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Here we go. Bism Allah Al-rahman Al-raheem.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Okay, let me stop right here and remind you of something.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You should make an intention, that is you
say “I intend to observe the Wuḍū, or the ablution.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Before you do that and you say “Bism Allah Al-rahman Al-raheem.” And you commemorate God
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
in any way you want. You say “Alhamdu
Lillah”, “Subḥān Allāh”,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
“Allahu akbar”, anything you want
to commemorate God.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: But if you want to say it in Arabic, the intention should be;
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: “nawayatu al-wuḍū, Bism Allah Al-rahman Al-raheem.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, here we go. “Bism Allah Al-rahman Al-raheem,
nawayatu al-Wuḍū.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Then the first step, you wash your face.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Okay, I washed my face twice, and I feel like
I did a good job. So, this is good enough.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: There is no set number of washing your face.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The second step, the arms to the elbows. So,
here we go,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: washing the arm to the elbow. Right arm and then the left arm, the same thing.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And this takes care of the second step.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: The third step is you wipe your hair. So, what I will do is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
I wet my hands and then I wipe my hair, my
head, like this. And this is the third step.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The final step is wash your
feet to the ankles. So, you put your foot there
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
wash it thoroughly. And this
takes care of the right foot.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And then the left foot.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: That's it. There you have it, the 4 steps of Wuḍū, very simple.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Don’t add any more steps, and don’t reduce
the steps.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Now that you finished the 4 steps
of Wuḍū, wash your face, your arms to the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: elbows, wipe your head and wash your feet, you are ready for the Salat Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: So, now let's go back to the masjid and show you how to observe the Salat Prayers, all 5 of them.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The innovations, superstitions, prejudices,
customs, and traditions did not hit the Azaan
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and the Wuḍū only, brothers and sisters,
it also hit the Salat itself, the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
There's so much garbage that we have to remove
from the Contact Prayers to make it pure,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and make it exactly the Contact Prayers that the
prophet Muhammad preached and practiced.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, what I'm going to present to you is the
pure Contact Prayer without any innovations
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: or additions that happened in the last 1400 years.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
We are trying to take the Salat, the Contact
Prayers, all the way to the prophet Muhammad,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the way he preached it, and the way he practiced it.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And the most important point, please pay attention,
the most important point is never to mention
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
any name other than the name of Allah, the
name of God, in your Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: This is dictated upon us in the Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But you probably know that the average Muslim
today adds the names of Muhammad and his family,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Abraham and his family, and so on in the
Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And this nullifies the Contact Prayer and makes
it absolutely useless, if not harmful.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, you must be very careful. And this is my
responsibility to tell you that.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You must be very careful never to mention
any name other than the name of Allah, the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: name of God, in the Contact Prayers.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: We see this in the Quran in Sura 72, AYA or verse number 18,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
where it says “the places of worship belong
to God, do not mention any other name besides
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the name of God.” This is a Quranic commandment.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And in Sura 20, verse 15,
we see the commandment
(20:14) أَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
“observe the Contact Prayers
to commemorate Me” singular. God
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
is telling us that we must commemorate Him
alone in the Salat, in the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, I will give you the details of the Contact
Prayers and we will go the mosque now and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: give you a demonstration.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But before I do this, I want to clarify that
the TASHAHUD or the recitation while sitting down
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
should be only “Ash-hadu Alla Elaha
Ella Allah Wahdahu La Shareeka Lah”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
or just “Ash-hadu Alla Elaha Ella Allah”,
or just “La Elaha Ella Allah.” This is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
enough. “There is no god except the one
God.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And forget about all these names, Muhammad
and his family, Abraham and his family.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Muhammad and Abraham will be the first people
to denounce this use of their name in the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And you know something, all the Imams of Sunni
and Shia, all of them, unanimously agree that
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
this mentioning of Muhammad and his family,
Abraham and his family while sitting down
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
in the Contact Prayer, is not an obligatory
part of the prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You heard me right. Unanimously, they agreed
that this is just a desirable, they think,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
a desirable part, but it is not. It actually
kills your Contact Prayer, makes it useless
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and actually does harm to you. Because God will be offended
to have other names mentioned besides Him
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
in the daily worship. You're worshiping God
alone. So, just be careful.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And this by the way led to the conclusion
that you must recite only Al-Fãtehah, the opening
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Sura of the Quran while standing up in the
Contact Prayers.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Do not recite any Quran after the Al-Fãtehah.
And on the surface, this looks like abandoning
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: the Quran, it is not. It's the exact opposite. Because in the Contact Prayers, a lot of people end up memorizing
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the short Suras: “qul huwa Allahu ahad”, and “qul
a’uzu…”, and that’s it. And they think
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: they know Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But I must tell you to read Quran every day.
You must read the Quran every day. This is
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
a commandment from our creator to read His
message, the Quran, every day, the whole Quran,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: not just the short Suras.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But in the Contact Prayers, please, you only
need recite Al-Fãtehah.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And this is a unifying force of all the Muslims
in the world.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
I was praying in Mecca one time and the Imam
read Al-Fãtehah and then he read the whole
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Sura number 32, Sura Al-Sajdah
after Al-Fãtehah.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And I was thinking, you know, there are a few
thousands of people in there around the Ka‘bah
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
praying behind this Imam, and the vast majority
of them didn’t know any Arabic.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
What is their point? They just stand through all
this recitation in Arabic that they do not understand.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: What is required is only recite Al-Fãtehah.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And this will unify all the Muslims of the
world. They will do the same thing in all
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the prayer. In Japan, they know Al-Fãtehah.
They read it in the Contact Prayer. In Sweden,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
in America, in Canada, in Australia, in Mecca,
in Pakistan, all the Muslims of the world
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: will do the same thing.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But this business of reciting long portions
of the Quran is wrong. It actually ruins the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Contact Prayer. God wants things to be easy
for us, but Satan wants to make things difficult
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
for us. So, he adds all things. Besides,
when you recite the Quran, you mention Moses and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Jesus and Muhammad and Pharaoh and the
devil and all these things.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You'll mention other names besides the name of
God in the prayer, and this is forbidden by
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: commandment from God.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: We are not to mention any name.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
When you recite the Quran in the mosque and
you mention other names, it's because God says
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
so in the Quran. It says
(19:16) وَٱذْكُرْ فِى ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ مَرْيَمَ
for example. This is God’s commandment.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You can mention the name of Mary in the Quran
in order to learn from the lessons of previous
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: prophets, messengers, and so on.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And it is a commandment from God to mention. So, when we read the Quran, we mention these
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
names only because God commanded us to do
so.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
But in the Contact Prayers, in the Salat,
we are commanded never to mention any other
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: name but the name of Allah, the name of God.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
After you have done the Wuḍū and you are
ready for the prayer, you go to a nice clean
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
place. You don’t necessarily need the
prayer rug. This is one of those innovations.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You can pray in any clean place, even bare
ground as long as it is dry and clean.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, you go to a nice clean place and you find
the direction of Mecca, the direction of the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Sacred Mosque, because this is
a commandment in Quran that you must face.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
This is an organizational point. There
is no other significance to it, except organizational.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You can imagine people going in a mosque and
facing in different directions, it'll be a mess.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
One of the most important points is that
there is a myth among the average Muslims
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
that a woman who has her period or menstruation
cannot pray.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Now, this has to be from Satan because Satan
is the one who does not want you, the Muslim
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: woman, to pray.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
God did not say in the Quran at all “do
not pray during menstruation.”
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: There is nothing in the Quran that says that.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Even the Hadith... we learn from Hadith that
the prophet’s wives used to pray during
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: their menstruation.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
One Hadith even says "they put a bucket
under one of his wives as she prayed."
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Ridiculous as this may be, but it demonstrates
that the Muslim woman should pray during her
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: menstruation.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
If a Muslim woman does not pray, during menstruation,
this means one week in the month without prayer,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: and this is like 4 years every 10 years, 4 years without any
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: prayer, imagine that.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, this will be a satanic innovation to stop
the women from praying during menstruation.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, please, menstruation or not, the Contact
Prayer, the Salat prayer is the only worship
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
that must go on. There is absolutely no excuse
for not doing the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:

or riding in a car, or riding in a plane,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
or in a bus, or even if a person is very sick,
very ill, cannot move, that person can pray
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
with his or her eyelids, or even
mentally.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:

cannot find a place to pray, you can pray
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:

through the motions and the words.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, there is absolutely no excuse for missing
any Contact Prayer.

segments.text:

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

or during menstruation, or the after birth bleeding,

segments.text:
stops your from performing, observing the

segments.text: after the imam.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Remember, all that is required in the Contact
Prayer is the Al-Fãtehah, the first Sura of Quran.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, you just mentally follow the imam as he
recites Al-Fãtehah during the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And then of course in Ruku', the bowing position,
you say “Subhaana Rabbiya Al-‘Azeem” as usual.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And in the Sujood or prostration, you say “Subhaana
Rabbiya Al-A‘alaa”, as usual.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: So, you only listen to the imam when he recites Al-Fãtehah in the standing position.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
If a person comes late, and finds the Jama’a,
the group, already did one or two or three
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Rak’as, units, you just – if you come
late, you just join the group in whatever
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
position they are in, and then after they
finish, when they say “Al-Salaamu ‘Alaykum”,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
the first one, you stand up and you complete
the part that you missed.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, this is how you make up for missing units,
or missing Rak’as when you join a group.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
What happens if you miss one of the prayers,
one of the Contact Prayers?
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
You're supposed to do all five Contact Prayers
during each one of the five periods, the Morning
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: Contact before sunrise, the Noon between around 12:00 and four (16:00), the Afternoon
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
between four (16:00) and sunset, the Sunset
Contact immediately after sunset, and the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Night Prayer after all the twilight disappears
from the horizon, about two hours after sunset.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Now what happens if you miss one of these
prayers?
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
There is a myth that you can make it up or
combine prayers and it is just an innovation.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: You cannot make up missed prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
If you miss the Noon Prayer in any day, you
just cannot bring yesterday back.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: You missed it and it is too bad.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, you just ask God for forgiveness, repent
and promise God that you will never, to the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
best of your ability, miss anymore prayers,
and you just go on doing the prayers.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
See, the idea of the Contact Prayer is to contact
our creator within a certain period of every day.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And when you miss that, it is gone. You
cannot bring it back, and you cannot make
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: it up, but you can ask forgives and repent.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: And now the best way to describe the Contact Prayers to you is to demonstrate exactly how it is done.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, now I will demonstrate for you the Morning
Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Do you remember the first thing you have to
do in order to observe the Contact Prayers?
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
That’s right, the intention. You declare
your intention, in Arabic “NIYYA."
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, since this is the morning prayer, I will make
the intention for the Morning Contact Prayer,
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: in English then in Arabic.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Then, I will proceed with the prayer and you
just watch everything I'm doing and this
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
is – this should be the correct way for
observing the Contact Prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
So, here I am facing the direction of Mecca,
and I'm going to make my intention.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
I intend to do the Morning Contact Prayer, Nawaytu
Salat Al-Subh.

segments.text: all the way from Abraham exactly this way.

And you notice in my prayer, I didn’t look

segments.text: And now I will do the Noon Prayer.

segments.text: Now, the Noon Prayer, the Afternoon Prayer, and the Night Contact Prayer are all identical, exactly the same.

title: Principles of Friday Prayer
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa explains the procedure for the Friday congregational prayer, citing Sura 62:9 as an obligation on both men and women, and walks through each required element: an Azan mentioning God's name alone, two sermons that each open with "Alhamdu Lillah, La Elaha Ella Allah," a pause for repentance after the first, the closing call "Aqem Al-Salah," and a two-unit prayer in place of the usual four. The second half of the tape presents sample sermons, the first on seeking God's kingship, which opens from Luke 12:29-31 and covers religious priorities, the order of Zakat recipients, Hajj, and God as Al-Razaq the provider who gifts the prayers themselves to the believer. A further sermon treats marriage in Islam, which he says requires love built on real acquaintance and a dowry serving as the wife's security, then extends into self-discipline, the soul's strength over the body, polygamy in light of Muhammad's long monogamous marriage, and the argument that God hates divorce and protects the rights of women. Related recordings: the two sample sermons in the second half of this tape also appear separately as "32 - Friday Sermon Seek GOD's Kingship Over You and Everything Else Follows (03-25-1988)" and "33 - Friday Sermon Marriage Importance of Love, Muhammad's Example (04-08-1988)"; the companion tape on the five daily prayers referred to here is "17 - Principles of Contact Prayers Salat."

BISMI ALLAH AL-RAHMAN AL-RAHIM. In the name
of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Brothers and sisters AL-Salãmu ‘Alaykum.
The Friday congregational prayer is an
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
obligatory duty upon every Muslim man
and woman. This is a social function
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
decreed by God Almighty for the Muslims
to get together and to know each other
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
and to be familiar with their problems
and their joys. And we find in SURA
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
number 62 verse number 9, the commandment
from God says "o you who believe when the
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
contact prayers, the SALAT for Friday, is
announced, you shall go to the mosque and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
observe the SALAT prayer,
and drop all business. This is better for
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
you if you only knew." So, if anyone is
afraid that he or she may lose some
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
business during the Friday prayer, God is
saying "this should be better for you"
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
God will make it up to you.
God runs the world and He is the only
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
provider and He guarantees you doing
better if you go to the Friday prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
And notice that the commandment said "o
you who believe."
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: It didn't say "o you believing men or o you believing women." It says "o you who
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
believe when the contact prayer on
Friday is called for, you shall go and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: drop all business." It is very important. I'm emphasizing the role of the women
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
because this is also an educational
meeting where people sit down and
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
listen to a sermon and the Muslim woman
must be the best educated because she
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
teaches the children.
Women are our mothers and they teach
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
us as we grow up and it is essential
that they are educated, not ignorant.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
The traditional customary Muslims of the
Middle East, they kept the women away
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
from the mosque and this kept the
children ignorant because the mothers
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
are ignorant as far as the religion is
concerned. So, it is very important to
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
emphasize this fact that Muslim men and
women are required. It is an obligatory
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text: duty for them to go to the Friday prayer.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
Now, there are certain conditions for the
Friday prayer. The people dress nicely as
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
commanded in the Quran, and they go for
the noon prayer on Friday to the mosque.

traditions or duties that came to us all

Now, the AZAN should be

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

I said the first sermon,

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

The prayer itself consists of two RAKATs,
instead of four. The customary noon prayer

segments.text:
consists of four RAKATs or four
units but on Friday, it is only two
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
RAKATs or two units and this is because
the two sermons compensate for two
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.text:
RAKATs or two units. So, the first sermon
and also the second sermon, they must

segments.text:
begin by stating ALHAMDU LILLAH, praise
be to God, followed by the SHAHADA.
segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

each sermon the first one and the second
one by saying ALHAMDU LILLAH. La Elaha Ella Allah.

the subject in any language that he wishes.

The sermon also deals with the
local conditions of the local community.

Tooboo Ela Allah.

title: Old Message, New Messenger
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: A compilation of two 1988 sermons on Dr. Rashad Khalifa's claim to messengership, each opening with a recitation of Sura 36. The first announces the commission he says he had known of since 1980 and avoided declaring for eight years, and argues from Sura 18, Sura 39:65, Sura 21:28 and Sura 49:13 that a messenger holds no rank, is not guaranteed Heaven and takes no money, then from Sura 33:40, Sura 3:81 and Sura 7:35 that messengers can follow Muhammad; the signs he offers include the mathematical code, the root rashada appearing nineteen times in a Quran index printed the year before his birth, the verse numbers containing the word Allah totalling 118123, and the names Abraham, Muhammad and Rashad totalling 855. The second sermon gives his detailed account of the night in April when he repeatedly opened the Quran at random, across several copies and by pointing a letter opener into a stack, and each time read that he was fired and doomed for cowardice, until he wept, prostrated and resolved to announce regardless of cost, after which the same procedure began returning messages of forgiveness. It closes with corrections he proposes to zakat under Sura 6:141, to fasting and to hajj, and with the argument from the mention of Joseph in Sura 40 that people have wrongly declared each messenger to be the last. Related recordings: these two sermons also appear separately in this collection as "34 - Friday Sermon Proclaiming Messengership, Abraham's Religion (04-15-1988)" and "35 - Friday Sermon Rashad Explains His Messengership Details (05-16-1988)." Note also that the segment on zakat, fasting and hajj is repeated a second time in the closing minutes of this recording.

title: The Great Debate: Dr. Rashad Khalifa vs Dr. Abdel Rahman
displayTitle: The Great Debate: Dr. Rashad Khalifa vs Dr. Abdel Rahman
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: A 1987 televised interview and debate between Dr. Rashad Khalifa and his host Abdel Rahman Salem, opening with a recitation of Sura 36 and an introduction to the mathematical code. Khalifa argues that the code is the first indisputable, physical miracle of the Quran and lists the five purposes he reads in Sura 74, after which the exchange turns adversarial as Abdel Rahman presses him on rejecting hadith and on omitting Muhammad's name from the shahada and the call to prayer. Khalifa answers from Sura 3:18 that God's own testimony contains no other name, from Sura 2:285 that no distinction may be made among messengers, and from Sura 75:16-19, Sura 69:38-47 and Sura 5:99 that the prophet was forbidden to explain the Quran and charged only with delivering it, holding that hadith was attributed to Muhammad rather than spoken by him and first recorded some 250 years after his death. The middle of the debate covers his claim that two verses at the end of Sura 9 are human additions, which he supports from the printed Quran's own note that the chapter is Medinan except its final two verses, from the single witness named in the collection account, and from the counts of the words for God being thrown off by one, while maintaining that God's promise of preservation holds precisely because the errors are detectable. The closing section measures his practices against Abdel Rahman's, four steps of ablution against eight, audible rather than silent prayer, the words said in the sitting position, and zakat paid on receipt rather than annually, and ends with his claim to messengership, the root rashada occurring nineteen times in a Quran index, and his statement that Islam as practiced has nothing to do with the prophet Muhammad.

title: In Defense of the Bible
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that the Bible is the word of God but that human interference has injected contradictions which drive intelligent readers away from it. He opens with the discrepancy Carl Sagan notes on page 30 of Contact, between Matthew's 28 generations from David to Jesus and Luke's 43, and treats the deification of Jesus as the largest distortion, reading the cry from the cross in Matthew 27:46 as incompatible both with Jesus being God and with the doctrine that he came to die for sins. He reads at length from The Myth of God Incarnate, naming its seven contributing theologians and their posts at Cambridge, Oxford and Birmingham and their thesis that Jesus was a man approved by God, as in Acts 2:21, and that the incarnation is a poetic rather than a literal claim. Estimating that ninety percent of the printed Bible is divine truth which readers abandon on account of the remainder, he presents the Quran as a mathematically composed final edition with four functions: exposing the injected contradictions, confirming the Bible's genuine content, settling controversies such as the crucifixion, which he says was inflicted on Jesus' body after the soul had been raised, and confirming earlier miracles such as the parting of the Red Sea. He illustrates the crucifixion argument with the case of artificial-heart recipient Bill Schroeder and closes by giving his Tucson address and telephone number for questions.

description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa, a biochemist, examines the evolution-creation debate as it reached the Supreme Court in 1987, arguing that mathematics can settle which events are probable. He summarizes Darwin's proposal and the modifications science has since imposed on it, punctuated equilibrium replacing gradual evolution and the abandonment of Lamarck, and offers the navel orange as an instance of real evolution within a kind. He then develops a probability argument from five cubes yielding 120 permutations up to 84 cubes, where the chance of one specific arrangement is effectively zero, and applies it to the 30 billion nucleotides of the human genome, the complexity of the so-called simple cell, and the eye, asking what told the dragonfly to stop at 30,000 lenses. Turning to creation, he argues that a mathematically coded message would constitute proof, quotes Duane Gish conceding that creation cannot be tested, cites Rabbi Judah the Pious on nineteen occurrences in the morning prayer, and describes putting the Quran into a computer and finding 19 across the initialed chapters and the four words of the opening statement, noting the finding's mention in Scientific American in September 1981. He concludes that the document confirms life beginning in water and presents evolution as a divinely guided process still underway, so that science and religion need not conflict, while correcting popular creationist claims about the age of the Earth, Noah's ark and the extent of the flood, which he blames for Darwin's own loss of faith.

formed, then this cell split and

millions of years were required for some

and evolve all the way to human beings.

theory.

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

original theory of evolution as written

new established facts.

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

So, this was the first major modification of

let me give you the correct expression here -

segments.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

title: King of Chaos
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: The second in a series of programs, in which Dr. Rashad Khalifa addresses why a world governed by a loving God contains famine, disease and war. He first establishes scale, working from the 93 million miles between Earth and the Sun through the Milky Way, a universe of a billion galaxies spanning 26 billion light years, and the seven nested universes he says the Quran describes as held in God's hand. He then narrates the origin of the arrangement: angels created with immense powers, one of them, Satan, concluding privately that he could be a god in his own right; God choosing to expose him rather than destroy him by creating Adam from mud and commanding the angels to prostrate; and then granting Satan the planet Earth as a dominion, with those humans who accept his view that God alone is not enough serving as his constituents. On this account the misery in the world is the visible result of Satan's incompetence, while those who side with God's view belong to a kingdom he describes as free of illness, financial trouble and even headaches. He sets out how to switch, citing Sura 29:2 on being tested and the trial of Job, distinguishes four kinds of disaster, admission tests, educational disasters, blessings in disguise and retributive disaster, and closes on repentance turning past sins into credits, the suffering of children, and idolatry as the one sin unforgivable at death.
