title: Friday Sermon: Knowing GOD: GOD is Doing Everything (06/05/1987)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Knowing GOD: GOD is Doing Everything (06/05/1987)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa delivers what he calls the most important sermon he has given, arguing that belief in God is not sufficient because the Quran repeatedly states that the majority of believers will go to Hell. Drawing on Sura 12:106, Sura 23:84-90 and Sura 29:61-63, he contends that real belief requires recognizing that God runs everything, and he prescribes a new zikr, the constant repetition of "God is running everything," to be kept up throughout the day. He illustrates the point with Joseph's dream preceding his brothers' apparent decision, his own recent trip to Egypt, a printing error at the Muslim Perspective, and an analogy of foreknowledge as travel in time, concluding that to think anyone else acts independently is shirk. The second sermon warns that anger, complaint and even private suspicion backfire because they amount to objecting to God, and closes with reflections on moderation in eating and on the scale of a universe containing a billion trillion stars.

title: Friday Sermon: GOD is Doing Everything, Rearranging Our Priorities (07/1987 No. 2)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: GOD is Doing Everything, Rearranging Our Priorities (07/1987 No. 2)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa continues the previous sermon's conclusion that God is doing everything and turns to the rearranging of priorities, diagramming the human being as a body that lasts perhaps a hundred years and a soul that lasts forever. He argues that people devote schooling, careers and money to the vanishing body while starving the real person, citing Rock Hudson and Liberace as cases of fame and wealth that left the soul undeveloped, and reads Sura 18:45-47 on this world as vegetation turning to hay and on money and children as its adornments. The second sermon contrasts a believer's morning with a neighbor's and stresses commemorating God throughout the day, then presents a passage he asks the congregation to identify, which argues that no letter of a prayer text may be added or omitted because any change destroys an inherent numerical harmony. He applies that argument to the addition of "Amen" to Al-Fatehah and to the Quranic warning addressed to those who are heedless of their prayers.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Quran vs Bible Code, End of the World Revealed 2280AD (07/1987)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa contrasts the Quran's mathematical structure with a computer study of the Torah conducted at the Hebrew University, playing a clip in which Professor Richard Elliott Friedman dismisses that work on Larry King as statistically bogus because the letter interval was chosen by trial until a word appeared. He argues that the Quran's case is different because its initials were fixed in the text, walking through counts of Q, N and Saad, the seven H.M. chapters, ALM in Sura 2 and the five initials of Sura 19, each a multiple of 19, and notes that he has offered to abandon the entire finding if a single error is produced. The second sermon defends his claim that the Quran dates the end of the world, deriving 1709 years from the numerical total of the fourteen initial sets in light of the "seven pairs" mentioned in Sura 15, corresponding to 1710 AH and 2280 AD, and citing the 309 years of the people of the cave in Sura 18 as confirmation. He stresses that this dating is a piece of information rather than a condition of salvation, since he reads the Quran's minimum requirements as belief in God, belief in the Hereafter and a righteous life under any religious name.

title: Friday Sermon: Universal Unity Through Devotion to GOD Alone
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Universal Unity Through Devotion to GOD Alone
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa introduces an idea he calls Universal Unity through Devotion to God Alone, arguing that Protestants and Catholics, Jews and Muslims, Hindus and Sikhs, Sunnis and Shias all share belief in God and are divided only by human figures such as Jesus, Mary, Muhammad, Martin Luther and Joseph Smith. He announces a video program on the theme and a change to the mosque's sign from submission to devotion, reasoning that a person can submit to something while hating it. The first sermon then turns to polygamy, which he treats as a permitted law being abused among Muslims in the United States, offering Muhammad's twenty-five years of monogamy with Khadija and his later marriages to widows as the standard and proposing that the test is whether a marriage alleviates or creates sorrow. The second sermon takes up a statement he attributes to Jesus that people do not know God, and reviews the scale of the solar system, a billion trillion stars across a billion galaxies, and the seven nested universes of the Quran to argue both God's greatness and God's capacity to attend to every individual creature. Related recording: the video program on Universal Unity that Khalifa announces in this sermon appears to be the August 1987 segment appended to "16 - Essentials of Submission (Islam)" in this collection. The two are separate recordings covering the same theme, not the same talk.

title: Friday Sermon: The Mathematical Miracle Proves the Quran to be the Word of GOD (10/16/1987)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: The Mathematical Miracle Proves the Quran to be the Word of GOD (10/16/1987)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that his generation is uniquely fortunate because the mathematical composition of scripture supplies tangible proof for statements earlier generations could only take on faith, such as Moses' staff becoming a snake or Jesus reviving the dead. He reviews the evidence in ascending order, including the nineteen letters of the opening verse, the 114 chapters, the 57 occurrences of Q in each of the two Q-initialed chapters, and the 2147 H.M. letters across seven chapters, noting that a hostile reviewer has now conceded several of the counts while still calling them coincidence. The center of the sermon is a discovery he credits to Lisa: that between the first Quranic initial in Sura 2 and the last in Sura 68 the verses number 5263 and the chapters fall into nineteen alternating groups, that the word Allah occurs 57 times outside that span, and that the sura and verse numbers of those occurrences total 2432, while Sura 68 itself does not contain the word at all. He closes by reading Psalm 91, which he holds to be mathematically authenticated as well, and applies its promise of angelic protection to the believer's confidence that God controls every outcome.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Evidence is Increasing, This Life is a School for the Eternal Life (11/1987)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa reviews the latest issue of the Muslim Perspective and the accumulating numerical findings it reports, opening with an account of a Saudi visitor who disputed that Bismillah contains nineteen letters by counting letters not written on the page, and with the two different spellings of bism in the first revelation. He restates the findings credited to Lisa concerning the 5263 verses between the first and last Quranic initials, the nineteen alternating groups of chapters, and the occurrences of the word Allah, arguing that these confirm the verse numbers, chapter numbers and chapter sequence as divinely fixed rather than editorial. He then presents work by Ihsan on the refrain "which of God's marvels can you deny" in Sura 55, its patterning across odd and even verse numbers, and the related occurrences in Suras 7 and 53, whose chapter and verse numbers and letter counts he reports as multiples of 19. The second sermon turns to Sura 38:67 on the momentous event people disregard, describing the Day of Resurrection as a universal conference at which an eternal rank is assigned and this life as a school in which credits are accumulated through the Friday and daily prayers, credits he says begin paying off in the present as an inner happiness only God controls.

title: Friday Sermon: Quran is the Only Book in the World That is Mathematically Composed (11/1987)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Quran is the Only Book in the World That is Mathematically Composed (11/1987)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa argues that the mathematical composition of literature is an idea belonging to God alone, noting that no book in a library is composed this way and that the Quran is the only intact example, and illustrates what he means by imagining an instruction to write a chapter containing exactly 500 occurrences of one letter. Delivering the sermon on behalf of Ihsan Ramadan, he presents her findings on whether the numbers assigned to Quranic verses are man-made: the chapter and verse numbers where the word salat occurs total 4674, the verses containing the word Quran total 2660, the word itself appears 57 times once a verse in Sura 10 referring to a different quran is set aside, and adding the 38 chapters involved gives 2698, the same as the number of occurrences of the word Allah. Along the way he treats the contact prayer as the connection lost by the generations described in Sura 19, comparing it to a combination to a safe and to ropes that keep a person out of a sizzling pan. The second half relays two illustrations from Ihsan, a driver who stops at a changing light only because a police car is present and a machine that issues tickets whether or not police are watching, applies this to living in the knowledge that God is nearer than the jugular vein, notes a verse in Sura 68 about those unable to prostrate hereafter because they would not prostrate here, and closes by reading Psalm 62.

author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa returns to the basics of the mathematical miracle, explaining that 19 carries the meaning "God is One" because the letters of wahid served as numerals in the era before Arabic numbers existed. He then reports new counts tied to the pillars of Islam: the word wahid appearing nineteen times in reference to God, the chapter and verse numbers of those occurrences totaling 1425, the five occurrences of wahdahu totaling 361, and the mentions of salat, zakat, siyam and hajj summing to 114. He notes that the chapter-and-verse totals for salat and siyam are multiples of 19 while zakat is one above and hajj one below, and reads this as a message that every Muslim prays and fasts while only some pay zakat or perform hajj. The sermon closes with a finding in Sura Qaf whose verse total yields 19 times 42, the number of the only other Q-initialed chapter, a note that Jesus and Adam are each named 25 times alongside Sura 3:59, and a recommendation to memorize the supplication of Sura 23:97-98 as protection against satanic suggestion.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: The Muhammadans Worship Muhammad, Discoveries by Atef and Lisa (12/04/1987)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens by describing a shift in the reception of the God Alone message from religious leaders to academic researchers, then recounts a visit from the vice president of a Saudi Islamic university who objected to the mosque's sign bearing God's name without Muhammad's beside it. Taking this as an illustration of what he calls the worship of Muhammad, he reads at length from a devotional text describing a pre-existent light of Muhammad from whose sweat the angels, the throne and the prophets are said to have been made, and which assigns trades and religions according to which part of Muhammad's form each soul beheld. The remainder of the sermon reports numerical findings: the word Quran occurring 57 times once a disputed instance is set aside, the word messenger 114 times, and, credited to Lisa Spray, the nineteen chapters spanning the missing Bismillah of Sura 9 and the extra one in Sura 27, whose numbers total 342 and match the count of words between them. He closes with totals involving the unnumbered Bismillahs and 6346 verses, and with a prediction he published in 1986 that governments in the region would change at a rate of three every two years, which he reads as fulfilled by changes of government in Sudan, Yemen and Tunisia.

title: Friday Sermon: The Power of Repentance, The Secret of Happiness (01/01/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: The Power of Repentance, The Secret of Happiness (01/01/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Delivered on January 1, 1988, this sermon presents repentance as a means of starting over and then sets out what Dr. Rashad Khalifa calls the secret of happiness, reading the theme he has written for his new Quran translation: that happiness is a quality of the soul rather than the body. He cites Eddie Murphy's interview with Barbara Walters and a televised account of Barbara Hutton's life as cases of wealth and fame without happiness, and describes the utterances Bismillah, Ma Sha Allah, Alhamdu Lillah, Subhan Allah and In Sha Allah as snacks for the soul, with the five daily contact prayers as its full nourishment. Reading Sura 21:1-3 on a reckoning that approaches while people remain heedless, he contrasts this with the previous night's New Year celebrations, and draws on Sura 56 to describe a crowded lower Heaven and an uncrowded first class in which his own generation, as witnesses of the miracle, will be numerous. He closes with a new zikr, the visualization that God is present in the room and hears one's secrets, and with plans for a language-neutral video and a set of flashcards presenting the numerical facts of the code.

title: Friday Sermon: GOD is Doing Everything, Story About Ahmed Subhy Mansour (1/22/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: GOD is Doing Everything, Story About Ahmed Subhy Mansour (1/22/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa restates his central claim that God is doing everything, citing Sura 8:17 on a battle in which God rather than the believers did the killing, and Sura 51:56 on worship as the purpose of creation. He presents the variation in sunrise times and in the length of fasting days as a mechanism by which God removes excuses and sorts people by rank, then applies the same logic to the arrival in Tucson of Dr. Ahmed Subhy Mansour, an Al-Azhar graduate whose doctorate argued that the prophet will not intercede on the Day of Judgment, which he reads as God answering the charge that he himself is merely an unqualified chemist. He recounts Mansour's imprisonment in Egypt, the telegrams and recitations of Al-Fatehah he credits with the release, and the Egyptian press campaign calling for the degree to be revoked, along with plans to answer an Al-Azhar editorial by turning the label "rejector of Sunna" back on its authors as "rejector of Quran." The second half reports on a trip to Vancouver, including the five-day visa requirement for Egyptians, a meeting missed at the Seattle airport, a visa obtained through a shared Lancashire dialect, and well-attended gatherings at which former objectors did not appear.

title: Friday Sermon: Our Purpose, GOD's Kingdom vs Satan's Kingdom, Abraham's Dream (03/04/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Our Purpose, GOD's Kingdom vs Satan's Kingdom, Abraham's Dream (03/04/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa frames the purpose of human existence as a distinction between God's kingdom, which he describes as free of problems, and Satan's kingdom, permitted on Earth to demonstrate Satan's incompetence to be a god. He explains that entry into God's kingdom comes through following the commandments and nourishing the soul, that showing off or yielding to peer pressure over prayer is self-deception, and that recognizing God as the doer of everything is the decisive condition, then leads the congregation in a collective covenant of irrevocable repentance drawn from the Quranic command tooboo ela Allah. The second sermon dwells on God's mercy, citing the forty years he says a person is granted to make up their mind and the law of equivalence in Sura 2:178, which he reads as restricting capital punishment and leaning toward compensation against the harsher instincts of his listeners. He closes by arguing that God never commanded Abraham to sacrifice his son, since Sura 7:28 states that God does not enjoin vice and Sura 37:102 has Abraham acting on a dream, and that God intervened to save the son, treating the traditional reading as an idolization of prophets whose dreams are held to be true.

title: Friday Sermon: Seek GOD's Kingship Over You and Everything Else Follows (03/25/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Seek GOD's Kingship Over You and Everything Else Follows (03/25/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens from Luke 12:29-31, which he treats as expressing a Quranic idea, and explains what it means to seek God's kingship: giving priority to the five contact prayers and the Friday prayer, attending Quranic study, calculating and distributing the 2.5 percent zakat in the order of recipients the Quran specifies, eventually observing hajj, and keeping the prohibitions. The second sermon identifies the secret of happiness as a nourished soul, citing Eddie Murphy's interview with Barbara Walters as a case of wealth without contentment, then examines God's name Al-Razaq, arguing from Sura 7:43, Sura 10:9 and Sura 49:17 that guidance and the prayers themselves are God's provision rather than a favor done to God. He notes Abraham's prayer in Sura 14:40 to be made an observer of the contact prayers, contrasts this with the sins provided in Satan's kingdom, and repeats that Sura 7:28 rules out God having commanded the sacrifice of Abraham's son. He closes by arguing that mentioning any name besides God's in the prayer nullifies it under Sura 72:18, and that a completed prayer is a gift worth congratulating. Related recording: these two sermons also appear as the sample sermons in the second half of "18 - Principles of Friday Prayer" in this collection.

title: Friday Sermon: Marriage Importance of Love, Muhammad's Example (04/08/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Marriage Importance of Love, Muhammad's Example (04/08/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents the Quranic law of marriage as resting on two requirements: love, which he grounds in Sura 4:24 and Sura 30:21 and says cannot exist without a real period of acquaintance, and a dowry, whose purpose he identifies as security for the wife. He extends the security argument to divorce, citing Sura 2:240-241 on alimony and Sura 65:1 on the prohibition against turning a wife out of the house, and describes the Middle Eastern practice of an official marriage followed by a long interval before consummation as one way of satisfying the first requirement. The second sermon treats self-discipline as the foundation of all religious practice, invoking Sura 7:179 on people who become worse than animals, contrasting the televangelists Jimmy Swaggart and Jim Bakker with a believer whose soul is stronger than the body, and offering his own experience at scientific conferences as illustration. He closes on polygamy, which he says the Quran permits under many conditions while Muhammad's twenty-five years with one wife and his later marriages to widows set the example, and on divorce, which he says God hates and hedges with protections for women drawn from Sura 28:5. Related recording: this sermon also appears as a sample sermon in the second half of "18 - Principles of Friday Prayer" in this collection.

title: Friday Sermon: Proclaiming Messengership, Abraham's Religion (04/15/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Proclaiming Messengership, Abraham's Religion (04/15/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: In this sermon Dr. Rashad Khalifa publicly announces that he has been commissioned a messenger of God, something he says he had known since 1980 and had avoided declaring for eight years. Anticipating resentment, he argues from Sura 18:60-82, Sura 39:65, Sura 21:28 and Sura 49:13 that a messenger is not necessarily better than anyone in the congregation, is not guaranteed Heaven, and serves only as a vehicle for information, and he states that he will not accept money for religious work. He then argues from the distinction between prophet and messenger in Sura 33:40, the covenant of Sura 3:81 and Sura 7:35 that messengers can come after Muhammad, and presents the signs he offers as authorization: the mathematical code of the Quran, the root rashada appearing nineteen times in a Quran index printed the year before his birth, the verse numbers containing the word Allah totaling 118123, and numerical totals linking the names Abraham, Muhammad and Rashad to 855, which he connects with his age of 45 in 1980. The sermon closes with a revised understanding of zakat drawn from Sura 6:141, which he says should be paid at 2.5 percent from each paycheck rather than once a year, and with his account of weeping and prostrating before he accepted making the announcement. Related recording: this sermon also appears as the first part of the compilation "05 - Old Message, New Messenger" in this collection.

description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa gives a detailed account of the night in April 1988 that led to his announcement of messengership, describing how he repeatedly opened the Quran at random, across several copies and even by pointing a letter opener into a stack of them, and each time read that he was fired, doomed and unfit because he had been a coward. He says that only after he wept, prostrated and resolved to make the announcement even at the cost of his children and friends did the same procedure begin returning messages of forgiveness, which is why he now speaks without hedging. He restates that messengership carries no rank, since Sura 18 shows Moses as a poor student, Sura 39 warns that even a messenger's work is nullified by idolatry, and Sura 49:13 makes righteousness the only criterion, and he insists on the shahada of Sura 3:18 with no name added to God's. The sermon reviews his own chronology, the 1973 publications on the Quranic initials and the number 19, the year 1400 as a turning point, and the "seven pairs" of Sura 15 read as fourteen centuries, then closes with corrections he proposes to zakat under Sura 6:141, to fasting and to hajj, and with the argument from Sura 33:40, Sura 7:35 and the mention of Joseph in Sura 40 that Muhammad was not the last messenger. Related recording: this sermon also appears as the second part of the compilation "05 - Old Message, New Messenger" in this collection.

title: Friday Sermon: Natural Instinct - Who is The Real You? How to Find Perfect Happiness (05/27/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Natural Instinct - Who is The Real You? How to Find Perfect Happiness (05/27/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa offers a summary overview of the message as he understands it, addressed partly to guests, beginning with the claim that this generation is the first to receive a divine message supported by tangible physical evidence. He describes a covenant taken before creation in which all human beings bore witness that God alone is their Lord, which he identifies as the natural instinct each person is born with, and then answers what he presents as the questions most people cannot answer: who we are, given that a person consists of a body and a soul; why we are here; and what we actually need. The second sermon traces the arrangement back to Satan's claim that he could be a god, which God tested by granting him the planet Earth as a dominion and those humans who choose him as constituents, so that every person stands in one of two kingdoms, one free of problems and one full of them. He closes with the mechanism he offers for perfect happiness, the nourishment of the soul through the Friday and five daily prayers, charity taken from what the body loves, fasting as mastery over the body, and pilgrimage commemorating Abraham, noting that some earlier scriptures also carry the mathematical code.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: The Meaning of Life, Discovering the Miracle (07/15/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa recounts a cosmology in which Satan's claim to be a god was tested by granting him the planet Earth as a dominion and, as constituents, those descendants of Adam who share his view that God alone is not enough, with every human being consulted beforehand and agreeing to take the test. He describes the instinctive knowledge and the messengers given on one side and, on the other, a jinn born alongside each person to whisper Satan's argument, and reads the surrounding universe of a billion galaxies as Satan's prison cell, too small for him to leave. The second sermon argues that Satan's method is to capture leaders rather than followers, naming the Pope, the imams of jurisprudence and students at Al-Azhar and the Islamic University in Medina, and inserts a newly reported finding that the distinct numbers appearing in the Quran sum to a multiple of 19. He closes with an account of how the discovery came about: a six-month computer course at Monsanto that coincided with his curiosity about the Quranic initials, and a move to the food research department of Anheuser-Busch where the work was completed, which he reads as the miracle having been hidden in Satan's own pocket and as evidence that Satan's knowledge is limited.

title: Friday Sermon: Who is Your GOD? Majority of Believers Are Going to Hell (10/28/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Who is Your GOD? Majority of Believers Are Going to Hell (10/28/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa asks the congregation to examine the question "who is your god," noting that the Quran repeatedly describes people who identify God as creator yet are destined for Hell. His answer is that whatever preoccupies a person's mind for the majority of the day is that person's god, supported from Sura 25:43 on one whose god is his own self, Sura 33:41-42 on commemorating God without limit, Sura 3:191, Sura 2:165 and 2:200, and Sura 63:9 and 64:14-15 on money, spouses and children as distractions and tests. He proposes dividing the day into a hundred units to measure how many are spent thinking of God, warns from Sura 18:42 and Sura 7:190 that whatever is idolized will eventually be lost, and gives practical means of remembrance: the first words spoken on waking, the five prayers as concentrated remembrance, Bismillah before eating, and Ma Sha Allah or Subhan Allah at any occasion. The sermon closes by answering students who ask why they do not get straight A's, arguing that God grants victory where it counts, illustrated with a broadcast recording of Sammy Khalifa's final at-bat of the season.

title: Friday Sermon: Classification of Creatures, Loving GOD, Hell is not Enough (12/09/1988)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Classification of Creatures, Loving GOD, Hell is not Enough (12/09/1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Speaking without prepared notes, Dr. Rashad Khalifa asks why believers should love God most, and answers by reconstructing an account in which unclassified creatures divided when Satan claimed he could be a god: those who accepted God's absolute authority without question became angels, Satan became a jinn, and those who agreed with him mentally became human beings. He says that when God offered these humans a second chance on Earth, the angels of Sura 2 asked whether God would place corrupters there, which he reads as a call to send them straight to Hell, and he finds parallel traces in Romans 3:23, Romans 6:23 and Hebrews 1:3. The second sermon argues that the human race remains bad enough to justify that judgment, pointing to mosques he says violate Sura 72:18 and churches that call Jesus God, and then explains why he believes two false verses in Sura 9 were allowed to stand for fourteen centuries: a proposal during Uthman's committee to add praise of the prophet, which he says Ali opposed, leading to fifty years of war, the killing of the prophet's family at Karbala, and Marwan burning the original copy. He closes with the retribution described in Sura 22:19-22, an account of a Los Angeles meeting where Muslim attendees attacked his presentation rather than a professor who had called the Quran a hallucination, and the point that summing the Quran's numbers leaves no room for disputes about letter counts.

author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa, working on the final pages of his new translation, takes up the recurring question of what becomes of earlier generations who lacked the complete message, recalling Pharaoh's question to Moses. He answers with a population estimate: about 6 billion people have lived from Adam until 1989, against some 75 billion still to come before the end of the world in 2280, so that the vast majority of humanity will receive the message intact. He revisits the classification of creatures into angels who never doubted God's absolute authority, jinns who accepted Satan's claim, and humans who remained undecided, and argues from Sura 19:71-72, Sura 21:101 and Sura 7:32 that this world is itself a mild or halfway Hell, defined as the absence of God's physical presence and distinguished from the eternal Hell by the fact that God still provides for believer and disbeliever alike, as in Sura 2:126. The second sermon previews a finding credited to Abdullah that stringing together the chapter and verse numbers of the Quran, stopping Sura 9 at verse 127, yields a number miles long that is a multiple of 19, and that the same holds for the units of the five prayers, then reads Malachi 3 on the Messenger of the Covenant and disputes the Christian identification of that figure with John the Baptist.

displayTitle: United Submitters International Conference: Explaining the Fulfillment of the Covenant (1988)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Answering a question at a 1988 United Submitters International conference, Dr. Rashad Khalifa recounts an experience during his pilgrimage in Mecca. Listening to the reciter Sheikh Al-Banna on Cairo radio on a Tuesday morning after the dawn prayer, he says that during the recitation of Sura 55 he was taken somewhere in the universe and shown all the prophets in turn, each appearing as in an oval portrait and nodding approvingly, with only Abraham identified to him by name, and that he was told at the time it was not his concern. He says the meaning was explained to him four months before this conference as the fulfilment of Sura 3:81, the prophets affirming a pledge to support a messenger who would confirm their messages. He then argues from Sura 16:2 and from Sura 22:75, which he stresses is in the present tense, that God continues to choose messengers, that everyone present who calls people to worship God alone is a messenger and a witness under Sura 22:78, and that his own role differs only in being specific. The session closes with a telegram from Ahmad Deedat addressing him by an Arabic epithet he locates in Suras 38 and 54, and with questions about the prophecy in Suras 9 and 48 that the message will prevail, the nineteen words of Sura 110, and the message reaching Japan and Latin America.

description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens with a finding he credits to Mahmood, that placing the numerical values of the letters of La Elaha Ella Allah side by side produces a multiple of 19, and connects it to counts he associates with the bones of the body and the length of gestation. The main sermon is an examination of conscience built around the question "who was your god last week," walking the congregation through an ordinary Saturday, waking with Bismillah, praying before sunrise, and pausing over the milk drawn from blood, the grain, the fruit, the clothing, the heater, the car and the traffic light, asking at each point whether God was actually in mind. He returns to Luke 12:29-31 and the argument that God runs everything, leaving a person only the choice between two kingdoms, and reassures listeners that the habit will take months to form. The second sermon divides humanity into submitters, who accept whatever God does and are therefore always happy, and objectors, who are always miserable, then asks why God named the longest chapter of the Quran after a cow, answering that the Israelites' haggling over which cow to sacrifice illustrates the arguing that total submission excludes, as with disputes over the four steps of ablution.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Revelation of Quran to Revelation of Miracle, Importance of Dawn Prayer (02/03/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Prompted by a question relayed from Canada about the interval between the revelation of the Quran and the revelation of its mathematical code, Dr. Rashad Khalifa traces the early history of Islam: the Quran placed in the prophet's heart in one night of Ramadan, its gradual release through Gabriel, three years of secret preaching, a boycott outside Mecca, Omar's conversion, and the Hijra thirteen years later. He dates his own identification of 19 as the code's common denominator to January 1974, corresponding to the close of 1393 after the Hijra, and reports that adding the Christian and Hijra figures gives 1406, or 19 times 74, the number of the chapter in which 19 is mentioned, which he reads as evidence that this history was predestined. The second sermon urges attention to the Dawn Prayer, arguing that the Quran's own name for it requires it before sunrise, that rising for it lubricates the joints and strengthens the soul against the body, and that varying sunrise times work as a sifting process which gradually reduces the number who keep it. He also defends a previous week's khutba by Mahmood Abib, citing Abraham's request to have his heart assured, and returns to his own eight years of resistance to announcing his messengership, the test he now reads in Sura 17:94, and the case of Kassim Ahmad in Malaysia as a believer who accepted everything else but not the announcement. Related recording: the Dawn Prayer segment also appears appended to "16 - Essentials of Submission (Islam)" in this collection.

title: Friday Sermon: Original Sin, Only GOD Guides, Majority of Believers Are Going to Hell (03/03/1989)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Original Sin, Only GOD Guides, Majority of Believers Are Going to Hell (03/03/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa returns to the account of a crime committed billions of years ago in which creatures failed to uphold God's absolute authority, and to the angels' suggestion in Sura 38 that all such creatures be sent to Hell. Drawing on Sura 12:103 and 12:106, he argues that this explains why most people will not believe and why most who do believe will still idolize something, so that the whole universe exists for the redemption of a small minority, a fortune he compares to matching every number on a lottery ticket with a million numbers. The core of the sermon is his reading of Sura 21:51 on Abraham given his guidance because God already knew him, Sura 12 on Joseph diverted from sin, and Sura 28:68-69 on God creating and choosing, which he takes to mean that each person arrives already marked for the High Heaven, the lower Heaven or Hell, and that this explains the circumstances which brought each listener to the mosque. The second sermon notes that only a few years earlier they too were praying wrongly, restates that people who name God as creator can still be destined for Hell because they do not know God, and criticizes those who invoke God's will as an excuse for idolatry or for prohibiting what God did not prohibit.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Purpose of Messengers, The Advent of the Pure Quran (03/17/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Marking one year since his announcement, Dr. Rashad Khalifa devotes the sermon to the question posed by the May 1989 Muslim Perspective: why God would send a messenger now. He grounds the answer in Sura 2:151 and the three modes of divine communication described in Sura 43, then sets out his reasons, beginning with the projection that some 70 billion people are still to come against 6 billion who have lived so far, and the claim that the pure Quran God intends has never existed, since Uthman's committee arranged the chapters from the prophet's chronological copy and two verses were added at the end. The bulk of the sermon catalogues practices he says Muslims perform wrongly, the Azan, the nine steps of ablution, names added to the salat, zakat delayed a year rather than paid on receipt, the timing of Ramadan, a hajj compressed into a single day, and visits to the prophet's tomb, alongside a critique of laws prescribing execution and of contemporary events including the Pan Am bombing and Khomeini's suppression of free expression. The second sermon promises a gentler second year, reads Sura 43:21, Sura 23:44 and Sura 40 on messengers rejected in succession and on belief that arrives too late, and closes with the nineteen-word chapter of victory and his sense that this message has reached more people in a messenger's lifetime than any before it. Related recording: the segment arguing that zakat is due on receipt rather than annually also appears in "16 - Essentials of Submission (Islam)" in this collection.

title: Friday Sermon: Why Announce Messengership? (08/11/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa addresses a question he says friends keep putting to him: why announce messengership at all rather than simply worship God alone. His answer is that worshipping God alone entails believing everything God says, including the statements he reads in Sura 2:285, Sura 33:40 and Sura 3:81 that Muhammad was the last prophet but not the last messenger and that a consolidating messenger would follow, so that Sura 49:15-16 makes real belief depend on believing in God and His messenger without doubt. He grants that doubt is permissible for a submitter but must be overcome, warns from Sura 57:14 of hypocrites who will one day ask believers "were we not with you," and identifies the ego of Sura 45:23 as the reason some drop out, noting that the root rashada occurs nineteen times in a Quran index printed the year before his birth, a finding he credits to Edip. The second half offers three questions to put to one's jinn companion when doubts arise: what the claimant advocates, whether he possesses real physical proof, and whether he makes money from the message, and he states that he arranges matters so that more goes out of his pocket on printing than comes in from sales.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Proving Every Verse, Word, Letter, with Irrefutable Evidence (11/09/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa presents what he describes as two new mathematical findings received after a conference, both concerning the numbering rather than the wording of the Quran. The first extends a display already on the mosque wall, in which the chapter and verse numbers of the whole Quran are written as one long number, by inserting a zero for every unnumbered Bismillah at the head of a chapter, with none inserted for Sura 9, which has none, yielding a number of 13,038 digits that remains divisible by 19; he credits the suggestion to Ali Fazeli and the computation to Abdullah. He distinguishes these structural findings from the literary side of the code, the counts of the Quranic initials and of words such as Allah and Quran, and argues from Sura 17:81 that what cannot be imitated is this composition rather than the prose. The second finding gives each verse both its number within its chapter and its sequential number in the whole Quran, 6346 in total, and strings all of these together with the chapter numbers into a number of 37,088 digits, with both the digit count and the number itself multiples of 19, a result he says collapses entirely if the two verses he regards as false at the end of Sura 9 are included.

title: Friday Sermon: The Heavenly Feud, The Importance of Killing the Ego (11/29/1989)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: The Heavenly Feud, The Importance of Killing the Ego (11/29/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens with a finding he credits to Edip concerning Sura 1: that writing the chapter number followed by its verse numbers, and again followed by the letter counts of each verse, yields multiples of 19, as does the sequence of units in the five daily prayers, which he takes as confirmation that only Al-Fatehah is recited in the contact prayer. The main sermon has two themes, how bad human beings are and how fortunate his congregation is, developed through an account of the heavenly feud in Sura 38:69 in which Satan's ego led a minority of creatures to withhold assent to God's absolute authority, after which most of that minority accepted a second offer and came as animals, stars and trees, which he reads as the sense of Sura 22:18 and Sura 55:6 on their prostration. Humans and jinns, he argues, refused that offer out of ego, unwilling to arrive as a horse that submits to any rider, which is why Sura 2:54 commands killing the ego and why he believes ego alone explains those who rejected his announcement without producing a single reason against it. The sermon closes with the World Conference on the Finality of Prophethood convened in Chicago, a flyer he notes contains neither God's name nor the Quran, the nineteen questions he intends to have put to its organizers, and the text of the letter he sent them inviting them to examine his evidence. Related recording: the Sura 1 and prayer-unit finding presented here is reviewed and extended in "50 - Friday Sermon Miracle of Miracles - Al-Fatiha, Proving the Five Salat (12-08-1989)" in this collection.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Proving Salat al-Jummah, The Righteous Go Straight to Heaven (11/26/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: After noting evidence presented the previous week that the Friday prayer and its two sermons form part of the mathematical code, Dr. Rashad Khalifa contrasts the submitter, who accepts new knowledge from God, with those who follow only what their parents taught, then reads Malachi 3, Luke 17:22-36, Matthew 24:27 and Sura 3:81 as announcements of the Messenger of the Covenant. Prompted by birthday wishes, he observes that November 19 is the only date in the year whose day-number, 323, is itself a multiple of 19, and reports a finding by Azhar Khan that the numerical values of the Arabic letters up to 1000 sum to a multiple of 19, which he offers as validating the claim that 19 is the value of the word for one. The second sermon presents what he calls great news, that the righteous go straight to Heaven at the moment of death, building the case from verses describing angels seizing the souls of disbelievers against verses describing the righteous being invited. He draws on Sura 2:25, 2:154, 3:169 and 22:58 on the dead being alive and provided for, on Sura 44:56 concerning tasting no death beyond the first, and on the man of Sura 36:20-27 who is told to enter Paradise and wishes his people on Earth could know.

displayTitle: Friday Sermon: Miracle of Miracles - Al-Fatiha, Proving the Five Salat (12/08/1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa devotes the first sermon to numerical findings contributed by three people. He reviews what he calls the miracle of miracles, in which the units of the five daily prayers written alongside representations of Sura 1, including its verse count, letter counts and numerical values, produce multiples of 19 even when the order is reversed; presents Saeed Talari's tally of the Fatehahs, bowings, prostrations and tashahuds in each prayer; and adds Edip Yuksel's observation that the lips meet exactly nineteen times when Al-Fatehah is recited, together with Soad's finding that the letter-position values of Noah, Abraham and Muhammad match the verse counts of the chapters bearing their names. In the second sermon he speaks about his mother's death, which he learned of days after preaching that the righteous do not die but go straight to Heaven, and reads the sequence of events as an assurance of the kind promised in Sura 41:30. He describes a mocking telephone call that preceded the news, the circumstances of her death while waiting for a cup of tea, the funeral prayer in Egypt led unexpectedly by a believer who opened the Quran to the example of Pharaoh's wife, and contrasts his grief at his father's death, which he believes came in disbelief, with his present happiness. Related recording: the Sura 1 and prayer-unit finding reviewed at the start was first presented in "48 - Friday Sermon The Heavenly Feud, The Importance of Killing the Ego (11-29-1989)" in this collection.

title: Friday Sermon: United Submitters International Conference (1989)
displayTitle: Friday Sermon: United Submitters International Conference (1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Delivered at the opening of a United Submitters International conference, this unprepared sermon doubles as Dr. Rashad Khalifa's welcome to the attendees, whom he calls the most important people on Earth and the elite of the elite described in Sura 56. He reads Sura 3:26 on God as possessor of all kingship and Sura 53 on God alone making a person rich or poor, happy or miserable, and argues that any intelligent creature would therefore attach itself to God alone. He warns that those present are the primary target of Satan, cites Sura 29:2 on believers being tested, and describes people who recently failed such tests, before addressing the accusation that his followers follow him rather than God, insisting that his own opinions carry no authority. The second sermon argues that since idolatry is the only offense unforgivable at death, any suspicion of it should be avoided, and that the shahada God states in Sura 3:18 and Sura 47:19 carries no name besides God's; he closes by telling conference attendees to measure every view they hear during the week against the Quran alone, since even a small doubt keeps a person at the lowest rank of submission.

title: United Submitters International Conference: Final Speech by Dr. Rashad Khalifa (1989)
displayTitle: United Submitters International Conference: Final Speech by Dr. Rashad Khalifa (1989)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa's closing address to the 1989 United Submitters International conference, delivered without notes and turning partway through into a series of direct confrontations. He frames this world as a remedial school and congratulates the audience for passing what he calls the hardest test, accepting that a human being like themselves is a messenger of God, a test he says took him eight years. Answering the persistent curiosity of Edip Yuksel and Feroz Karmally, he describes how revelation reaches him: not as a visible Gabriel, as with Mary in the Quran, but as his mind being taken over by a single piece of information, which he first dismissed as satanic, and he corrects an earlier impression by saying he was never ordered to announce, only told. He recounts the near-disclosure at the previous San Francisco conference, Ismail Barakat's determination to ask him point-blank and his own prayer that no one would, followed by the anticlimax of friends replying that they had known all along. The address then names individuals, challenging Christie of Vancouver over what she said privately, Sophie and Raymond over hosting people he regards as opponents, and Susan Ray over telling others that his translation contains mistakes, invoking Sura 58 on not befriending those who oppose God and His messenger, rejecting "do not judge" as a satanic principle, and closing with Sura 49 on believers who harbor no doubt and Sura 57:13-14 on hypocrites who ask "were we not with you."

author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Excerpts from a radio debate between Dr. Rashad Khalifa, a biochemist arguing for creation, and Professor Jeff Clark, an anthropologist at Arizona State University who holds that creationism is not a science and does not belong in science classrooms. Khalifa accepts the premise that science is how truth is established and argues that mathematics is the most rigorous of the sciences, then claims to possess a mathematically coded message from the Creator, comparing it to the fictional signal in Carl Sagan's Contact and offering to show the evidence as soon as the program ends. Clark treats Genesis as an origin myth no greater or lesser than any other, presses Khalifa on his relation to Henry Morris and the Institute for Creation Research, and states that gods have no existence apart from the societies that create them. A caller asks whether some vast thinking entity in the cosmos might account for creation without resembling the conventional picture of God.

title: The Creators Signature
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: A documentary-style program narrated by Bill Buck, with contributions from Dr. Rashad Khalifa, presenting the Quran's mathematical code as what it calls the ultimate miracle. The first half argues that modern people cannot be convinced by the localized miracles of earlier ages and need something perpetual, physical and verifiable, then surveys passages the program reads as anticipating modern science: embryology confirmed by Dr. Moore of the University of Toronto, the three veils of darkness, the Big Bang, the preserved body of Pharaoh, the moon as a reflector rather than a source of light, an egg-shaped Earth, the atmosphere as a protective ceiling, water as a requisite of every living thing, honey from the bee's belly, milk formed between urine and blood, plants created in pairs, moving mountains, mountains as stakes, and fingerprints, citing Maurice Bucaille's assessment that a fourteen-hundred-year-old text could not contain such ideas. The second half explains the code itself, using "Jack and Jill went up the hill" to show how hard it is to alter a sentence's letter counts while keeping its meaning, then reports the counts of the Quranic initials, the nineteen letters and four words of the opening statement with their totals of 19, 2698, 57 and 114, and the 6346 verses across 114 chapters. It closes with 19 as a signature the program finds in the 209 bones of the body and the 266 days of gestation, explains that 19 is the numerical value of the Arabic word for one, and argues that the code authenticates the earlier miracles of Moses and Jesus.

title: Arabic Language Lessons By Dr. Rashad Khalifa
displayTitle: Arabic Language Lessons By Dr. Rashad Khalifa
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa teaches a beginner's course in reading and writing Arabic, starting from the assumption that the viewer knows nothing of the language. He works through the full alphabet letter by letter, stressing the role of the dots and the pronunciation of sounds with no English equivalent such as Ha, Kh, Daad, 'Ain and Ghain, then covers the vowel signs Fat-ha, Kasrah, Dammah, Sukoon and Shaddah along with the long vowels formed by Alef, Ya and Wow. He shows how each letter changes shape at the beginning, middle and end of a word, identifies the six letters that cannot connect on the left, and demonstrates the rule by which the article Al falls silent between joined words. The tape closes with a grammar section built on root words including kataba, qara'a, akala and hamada, and a verse-by-verse reading of Sura Al-Fatehah directly from a printed Quran.

author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: A 1987 debate in Arabic, presented here in English translation, between Dr. Rashad Khalifa and a group of Sunni scholars. Both sides agree at the outset that every messenger called to the worship of God alone, but divide over the means: the scholars hold that the Quran states some matters in general terms and that the messenger's Sunna supplies the detail, citing Sura 16:44 on proclaiming to the people, Sura 59:7 and Sura 4:80 on obeying the messenger, and hadiths about being given "the Quran and something like it alongside it." Khalifa answers from Sura 6:114 and Sura 7:52 that the Quran is fully detailed, that Sura 5:99 limits the messenger's role to delivery, and that the number of prayer units and the rites of hajj and zakat reached Muhammad already established through the religion of Abraham, offering an analogy about a product already on the market and attributing his own knowledge of them to mass transmission and to the universal agreement of Muslims. The exchange, pressed hard from both sides and briefly interrupted by a dispute over a camera at the window, moves to the shahada, with Khalifa arguing from Sura 3:18, Sura 2:285 and Sura 72:18 that adding Muhammad's name beside God's in the testimony and the call to prayer is an innovation and a distinction among messengers, while the scholars insist the testimony is Quranic and press him on whether he denies that Muhammad is the messenger of God.

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> ما عرفنا هذا الا منك اليوم

segments_ar.text: الغنائم ولكني انا حق اتكم الرسول فاخذوه

segments_ar.text: >> وما يطع الرسول فقد اطاع الله اي نعم هل
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> هذا فيه حيده

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> ما اتاكم الرسول فخذوه وما نحكم عنه فخذوه
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> الشيء المؤكد اللي احنا عارفين انه خرج من

segments_ar.text: فم الرسول هو القران صح

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: في قضيه فيه امور لا نعرفها الا من السنه

segments_ar.text: وال القران نص على طاعه الرسول وما اتاكم

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: مثل ما ذكرنا الان وغير هذه تحتاج لبيان
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: وايضاح والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال الا
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: اني اوتيت القران ومثل
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> طب هل نستعمل علينا ونشوف هذا الكلام

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> من مزايا الاسلام انه لا يمنع العقل

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: ولا قال له نحفظ القران والسنه

segments_ar.text: >> فاما اما ابو بكر وعمر عصوا الرسول اما ان

segments_ar.text: هذا الحديث لم يحدث
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> لا لان ابو بكر وعمر لم يحفظوا الكتاب

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> كتاب الله وسنته شيئين اثنين مهمين لابد

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الذكر وانا له لحفظ فهو محفوظ وكما تذكر
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: قضايا الشرائع السابقه قبل الاسلام لان
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الاسلام جاء ناس يقول لها وقضيه التوافق
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: في البعض لا يقتضي ان نرتقي لناخذ ممن سبق
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: فنحن لنا رسول نتبعه بقي قضيه تفاصيل
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: السنه هل تتوقع هداك الله ووفقك الى
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الصواب ان الناس في هذه القرون الماضيه
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: ولا سما القرن الاول والثاني والثالث ا ما
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: كانوا على حق لما اخذوا بالسنه ودونوا
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: السنه عندك الخلفاء الاربعه ما رايك فيهم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> لا انا اسالت عن رايك العلم عند الله انا

>> ما علم من الجمع الانحد
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

>> لابد ان نختار واحده من اثنين
>> اطوع الناس للعمل بما جاء في الكتاب
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: والسنه لم يعصوا وما فرطوا وكانوا ي

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: صلى الله عليه وسلم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> وصلى الله عليه وسلم وجد عبد الله بن عمرو
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: بن العاص كان يكتب فقالت له قريش ان رسول
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الله بشر يتكلم في الرضا وفي الغضب فقال
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: له اكتب والذي نفسي بيده ما خرج من هذا
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الا حق وكتب الى الملوك والرؤساء يدعوهم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الى الدخول في الاسلام وكتب بعض الاحكام
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: كما قال اكتبوا لابي شاه فثبتت كتابه بعض

segments_ar.text: الاشياء وبعضها حفظ في صدور الرجال
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: يعني بحمد الله عز وجل تم تدوين السنه
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: وحفظها وكتابتها من خلال هذا التسلسل من
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: عهد الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والصحابه
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: لانه كان فيما اشكل عليهم شيء اتوا الى
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فاستفتوه فابان
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: لهم بعد ذلك ا يعني جمعت السنه وحفظت
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: وكتبت ودونت و فهي محفوظه في صدور الرجال
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

>> وفقك الله واهداك وفتح على قلبك اريد جواب

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: اربع وثلاث واثنتين
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> ولا تختلف معنا فيها اثنين اربعه

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> وكيف عرفتها
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: سابقا لا لان العالم كله بيصلونا الصبح
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> هذا العالم الاسلامي ولا غير الاسلامي
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> العالم كله المسلمين يعني
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> غير المسلمين مش هيصل هيصل
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> اذا انا اسالك الان
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: قبلنا كيف عرف
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> مثلا الشيء اللي حصل فيها اختلاف زي
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: الوضوء مثلا
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> انا بسالك سؤال وصدق انت رجل ان شاء الله
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: يتوسم فيك ان يكون نهايه للخير اصدق هل
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: انت تؤمن بهذا تقو لنفسك شيء
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> كلام ايه
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> يعني
>> عالم الايمان بالسنه يبدو لي انك متى مؤمن
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الاحاديث والسنه
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> نعم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> فهل انت في قراره نفسك تعتقد صحه هذا ولا
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: لا اصدق انت رجل ان شاء اللهقد
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> باذن الله ستكون نهايك خير ان شاء الله
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> الله سبحانه وتعالى انا اصدق ما قاله الله
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: سبحانه وتعالى ان كامل وتامصل
>> هذا صحيح
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> بس
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> باقي شيء اخر ان هذا لن تفهمه انت وانت
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: مولد في اللغه العربيه بمجرد هذا وحتى
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: الذين لم يولدوا فيعاد النبي صلى الله
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: عليه وسلم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: ما كانوا يستغنون بالكتاب بل فيه ايضاح
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: امور شرعيه لانك اذا اخذت بهذا المعنى
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: لغويا فحسب فالصلاه دعاء وخذ اي دعاء
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: وتمشي تقولني صلي الزكاه
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: اركعوا واسجدوا
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> واي ركوع وسجود افعل هل مجرد ما يفعله
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: من ركوع او سجود او البوذيين او غيرهم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

>> الله سبحانه وتعالى
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> انا اتوقع انك رجل ذكي بيهديك الله
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> نعم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> وانت بتاخذ بالسنه كما اخذت بالقران وان
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: في قلبك شيء مما تق الان قسمات وجهك

segments_ar.text: وحركاتك تنبئ بشيء في الخير ان شاء الله
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: قلبك يبد فيه الشيء غير
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

segments_ar.text: >> هو الخير الخير هو في تصديق الله سبحانه
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: وتعالى حد الله سبحانه وتعالى لا نختلف في
هذا اللي يتحدى الله كافر

segments_ar.text: >> لا هو اللي حصل المسلمين يتحدون الله
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: بيقول القران مش كامل القران
segments_ar.speaker: Dr. Rashad Khalifa

segments_ar.text: >> ما قالوا كذا من المسلم
segments_ar.speaker: Sunni Scholars

>> لا ما قلت كذا

segments_ar.text: فاهم
>> ربنا قال ان القران فصلنا انا وانت عشنا
في وقت ما اللغه ليست فطره عندنا وكما قلت

id: quran-study/01 Quran Study From Azhar 1 Sura 72;19 28 & Sura 73 By Kathryn Jinns 05 26 1989
title: Quran Study 01 — Surah 72:19-28 & 73 — Jinns (Catherine)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Catherine leads a study of Sura 72 (verses 19-28) and Sura 73 (verses 1-20), reading from Dr. Rashad Khalifa's upcoming translation of the Quran. She discusses the reaction of disbelievers when God alone is advocated, noting how their hearts shrink in aversion due to their egos. Dr. Khalifa explains the purpose of human existence as a chance to redeem ourselves after siding with Satan in the heavenly society. He argues that the true size of a believer's soul in the Hereafter is massive, while disbelievers shrink to the size of cats or ants. Edip Yuksel raises a question about the number of guards in Hell, leading to a debate with Dr. Khalifa over whether Sura 74:30 refers to nineteen angels or a general mathematical code. Dr. Khalifa asserts that Sura 72 contains no references to the Prophet Muhammad and points to mathematical patterns in the text discovered by Edip. Catherine continues with Sura 73, detailing the spiritual benefits of night meditation and the importance of choosing God as one's sole advocate. A discussion on self-defense and anger ensues, with contributions from Douglas, Hamid, and Robert on the ethics of fighting versus ignoring provocation. Dr. Khalifa emphasizes the absolute necessity of the Dawn (Fajr) prayer and explains that missing it is only excused under extreme circumstances like travel or exhaustive business. The session concludes with Dr. Khalifa announcing a new appendix on virginity and leading the group in reciting Al-Fatiha for several members' birthdays.

title: Quran Study 02 — Surah 95 & 96 — Quran Is Not Ink & Paper (Sabahi)
displayTitle: Quran Study 02 — Surah 95 & 96 — Quran Is Not Ink & Paper (Sabahi)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens with a warning about Satan targeting believers on the straight path before introducing Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi to lead the study of Sura 95 (Al-Tin) and Sura 96 (Al-Alaq), assisted by Dan, Ali, and Amir. Sabahi categorizes twelve suras where God swears by natural phenomena and plants, prompting Khalifa to explain the symbolic connections between the fig (Adam), olive (Jesus), Mount Sinai (Moses), and Mecca (Abraham and Muhammad). Hamid and Khalifa detail botanical and nutritional aspects of figs and olive oil, including cholesterol reduction and alternate crop bearing. Khalifa uses a jar and human balance mechanisms to illustrate divine physical design in 95:4, while Sabahi and Dan discuss the spiritual descent into the "lowliest of the lowly" (95:5). Addressing a printing omission of verse 5, Khalifa presents mathematical evidence based on the number 19 to argue that the Quran's preservation rests in the heart rather than physical paper. Sabahi draws on his background in organic chemistry to explain plant molecular synthesis, anti-cancer compounds, and chemical chirality using a hand glove metaphor. Robert questions why God created human beings knowing most would choose Hell, which Khalifa answers by asserting that Earth serves as a second chance to nullify excuses. Turning to Sura 96, Sabahi outlines traditional accounts of Gabriel's first revelation to Muhammad, which Khalifa rejects as untrue. David, Lisa, Douglas, and Ali debate whether 'alaq in 96:2 should be translated as 'embryo' or 'clot,' with Khalifa citing Maurice Bucaille to reject 'clot.' Sabahi and Ali reflect on human transgression through wealth (96:6–7) and mandatory versus forbidden prayer, citing experiences in post-revolutionary Iran. Khalifa concludes with administrative updates and leads the recitation of Al-Fatiha.

title: Quran Study 03 — Surah 10:79-92 & 73 & 3:110-117 (Rashad)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa leads a Friday gathering and study circle in Tucson, Arizona, opening with informal conversation alongside Ismail Barakat, Behrouz, and Mahmoud Abib regarding Iranian political culture and jokes about public grief versus private behavior. Khalifa recites Sura 10:79–92, drawing lessons on divine timing from the Red Sea crossing—rebutting a geologist's naturalistic explanation—and asserting that Pharaoh died a genuine believer whose late repentance failed to save his soul due to a lack of spiritual development. He shares anecdotes about the mummies at the Cairo Museum, a joke concerning Hosni Mubarak, and suspicions that a former acquaintance named Eric was a Saudi spy based on phone records. After reading Sura 23:1–14, Khalifa details the mathematical structure of the daily Contact Prayers (Salat) and discusses embryonic development stages described in verse 14. He and Mahmoud Abib present mathematical proofs centered on the occurrence of the word "God" in the Quran, including divisible verse totals, initialed sections, Abdullah's count of chapter and verse sums across 85 suras, and verse distances between 3:81 and 33:7 regarding the Messenger of the Covenant. In a sermon segment, Khalifa stresses prioritizing soul development through Salat over physical labor. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi then leads a study of Sura 3:110–117, addressing social responsibilities, the dual covenants with God and society, historical lessons from Sura 2:60–61, and a CBS 60 Minutes report on drug addiction in Zurich to illustrate moral decline in affluent secular nations.

title: Quran Study 04 — Surah 37 & 3:118-129 — Asteroid (Rashad)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Shakira Karipineni, Ismail Barakat, Mahmoud Abib, and Dr. Rashad Khalifa begin with lighthearted conversation about cholesterol and newspaper allegations against Khalifa before turning to Sura 37 (Al-Saffat). Khalifa, Abib, and Barakat humorously categorize hypothetical methods disbelievers use to force their way into Hell—such as storming gates, tunneling under fences, pole vaulting, and hang gliding—to explain why heavenly residents feel no sadness for the damned. Khalifa and Karipineni share childhood memories of climbing high fences to sneak into Egyptian soccer matches and Indian grape orchards. Exegetical commentary covers Sura 37's descriptions of angels as "arrangers" and "blamers," the cosmological meaning of "Lord of the easts" (interpreted as the rising of planets and stars), creation from wet mud as evidence of divinely guided evolution, and the rejection of Lā Elāha Ella Allāh by arrogant leaders. Khalifa references a video critique by Bilal Philips and contrasts the Qur'anic Shahada (3:18) with traditional Sunni formulas. Following readings of Sura 10:43–54, Abib shares a news report on H. Jay Melosh's theory regarding asteroid impacts and global firestorms, which Khalifa connects to the smoke prophesied in Sura 44. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi leads a study of Sura 3:118–129, analyzing the psychological state of hypocrites who bite their fingers in rage, a habit cross-referenced by Douglas to Sura 25:27. Commentary from Edip Yüksel, Abdullah, and Khalifa stresses severing close ties with hostile outsiders before Sabahi and Khalifa conclude with the historical context of the Battle of Badr and divine angelic assistance.

id: quran-study/05 Quran Study From Azhar 5 Sura 56;75 & Sura 57 By Lisa 02 17 1989
title: Quran Study 05 — Surah 56:75 & 57 (Lisa)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Lisa opens the study of Sura 56, verse 75, emphasizing the vast scale of the universe by citing galaxy counts, light-year distances across the Milky Way, and Psalm 8:3–4 to illustrate the gravity of God swearing by the positions of the stars. Reading verses 77 through 80, she contends that the phrase stating none can touch the Quran except the righteous refers to spiritual understanding and the discovery of its mathematical miracle. Addressing an audience question regarding the word "touch," Dr. Rashad Khalifa reads the study footnote to reject traditional ablution rules as a satanic plot, asserting that comprehension is granted exclusively by God. Khalifa hands out a summary sheet of the 19-based miracle, listing contributors such as Abdullah, Mahmood, Ihsan, Lisa, Feroz, Ismail, and Gatut, and demonstrates multi-thousand-digit numbers derived from verse and sura counts. Responding to Farhad Mo'ini's inquiry on number divisibility and a caller from Louisville, Kentucky, Khalifa argues that every Quranic verse is divine except two verses in Sura 9. Turning to verses 88 through 96, Lisa describes the allegorical nature of High Heaven, Lower Heaven, and Hell. Khalifa maintains that those who die before age 40, citing Malcolm X and Martin Luther King Jr., are granted Lower Heaven by divine mercy, drawing parallels to Abraham's understanding and Joseph's protection from sin in Sura 12:24. In Q&A, Catherine asks about generations of believers, and Hussein asks about age forty. Moving to Sura 57:1–5, Lisa discusses divine control over all matter and human hearts, before a group of children and a woman perform a devotional song on remembering God.

title: Quran Study 06 — Surah 59 — PRA, Invisible Giants, Hypocrites (Donna)
displayTitle: Quran Study 06 — Surah 59 — PRA, Invisible Giants, Hypocrites (Donna)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Donna opens a study circle session on Sura 59, discussing verses 5 through 10 regarding divine control over disbelievers' actions, angelic protection, and the equitable distribution of war spoils to prevent monopolization by the rich, which she compares to Hitler's plunder in World War II. Dr. Rashad Khalifa elaborates on verse 6, asserting that believers are accompanied by invisible angelic guardians and presenting local community events—including emergency financial aid collected for Emily and Lori surviving a rollover car crash unharmed—as empirical evidence. Donna and Dr. Khalifa address Sura 59:7–10, condemning sectarian abuses of verse 7 by Sunni and Shia sects while citing Sura 6:159 and Sura 3:103 to stress believer unity. Following audience questions regarding hypocrites, Dr. Khalifa defines hypocrisy as ego-worship and an inability to utter the shahada without adding Muhammad, referencing Sura 39:45 and Sura 4 while discussing political repression in Iran alongside Hamid and Parivash Ettefagh. Continuing with Sura 59:18–20, Donna discusses daily soul-nourishment, leading Dr. Khalifa to frame righteous deeds as deposits into a "Post Retirement Account" (PRA) for eternity, contrasting medical school preparation with eternal life. Reviewing Sura 59:21–24, Donna and Dr. Khalifa discuss the awesomeness of the Quran and divine attributes, supported by Abdullah's observations on mathematical coding, Dr. Khalifa's reflection on human physical design, Robert's inquiry on hypocrites citing Sura 12:103, and Farhad Mo'ini's questions about Quranic compilation history and Sura 53. The session ends with a group recitation of Sura 1 (Al-Fatiha) for Matt's birthday.

author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Dr. Rashad Khalifa opens the session with a significant announcement regarding the upcoming publication of a new, purified Quran translation, which he intends to release during Ramadan. He explains the historical corruption of the Quranic text, asserting that the original chronological order was altered by the Umayyads to include two verses in Sura 9 that idolize the Prophet Muhammad. He argues that this corruption, alongside the distortion of religious practices like the Azan and the ritual prayer, resulted in the loss of the pure Quran for centuries. Following this, Kathryn leads a study of Sura 62 and 63, focusing on the nature of God’s unlimited grace and the metaphor of the donkey carrying books to describe those who possess scripture but fail to understand it. The group discusses the concept of being "God's chosen," with Dr. Khalifa clarifying that this status is not an exclusive guarantee of salvation but a responsibility that many have distorted through arrogance. The conversation shifts to the importance of the Friday Prayer, which Dr. Khalifa emphasizes as a divine commandment that transcends cultural or gender-based restrictions often imposed by Hadith. The session concludes with a discussion on the hypocrites described in Sura 63, the nature of intercession, and the group reciting Al-Fatiha for various personal requests, including academic success for community members and the continued presence of a guest.

title: Quran Study 08 — Surah 65 & 66 — Enjoin Kids To Do Salat, Hamid Argues (Lori)
displayTitle: Quran Study 08 — Surah 65 & 66 — Enjoin Kids To Do Salat, Hamid Argues (Lori)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Lori leads a study of Sura 65 (Al-Talaq, 10–12) and Sura 66 (Al-Tahreem, 1–12), analyzing human creation, marital duties, and prophetic fallibility. Discussing 65:10–11, she explains that humans possess sufficient intelligence to believe rather than totally disbelieving like jinns, and that messengers serve to lead existing believers out of darkness. Dr. Rashad Khalifa addresses divorce laws, explaining alimony provisions and nursing mother allowances in 65:6–7. He argues that evolution within species is a divinely guided scientific fact, contrasting it with Darwinian natural selection and atheist evolution. He asserts that six other uninhabited Earths exist to prove on the Day of Judgment that life did not randomly evolve from chemical conditions. After an unedited manuscript typo found by Poopak is addressed, a participant questions how divorce arbitration functions in practice; Dr. Khalifa states that Quranic guidelines rely on conscience and mutual consultation. Transitioning to 66:1–7, Lori highlights Muhammad's human fallibility and the rejection of prophetic idolization. Hamid raises concerns regarding how far parents should force children to observe Salat, prompting Dr. Khalifa and Lori to cite 20:132 on persistent exhortation without compulsion. Beth offers personal testimony about her upbringing, noting that forcing children breeds resentment. Concluding with 66:8–12, Lori discusses sincere repentance, the struggle against hypocrites, and how the wives of Noah, Lot, Pharaoh, and Mary disprove the doctrine of intercession. The session ends with two recitations of Al-Fatiha for group members.

title: Quran Study 09 — Surah 70 — Chastity, Worry, Edip's Translation Request (Edip)
displayTitle: Quran Study 09 — Surah 70 — Chastity, Worry, Edip's Translation Request (Edip)
author: Dr. Rashad Khalifa
description: Edip Yuksel leads a study of Sura 70 (Al-Ma'arij), opening with Dr. Rashad Khalifa citing Sura 26 regarding reading the Quran in non-native languages. Edip discusses the relativity of time in 70:4, comparing human standards of age to flies and dogs—prompted by Lydia—while Khalifa references Carl Sagan's novel and Einstein's relativity theory to explain light speed and Prophet Muhammad's ascension. Examining 70:19–34, Edip addresses the passive creation of human anxiety, while Khalifa recounts an anecdote about his father's teacher debating mullahs over worry and despondency. Khalifa presents 70:29 as a command for chastity, citing a Joe Sobran column on sexual consequences and health risks like AIDS and cervical cancer mentioned by Naghmeh, while contrasting university condom giveaways with parental duties. On 70:30, Khalifa argues that "what is legally theirs" includes common law and non-traditional marital arrangements, responding to queries from Farhad Mo'ini, Parivash Ettefagh, and Douglas. Edip shares a personal story of a Turkish printing mix-up between 29:45 and 39:45 after neglecting his contact prayers. Dr. Mahmoud Sabahi, Robert, Martha, and Naghmeh ask questions regarding marital obligations, wealth as a virtue via Sura 16, verse order preservation through Gabriel, the historical Umayyad conflict following Uthman's era, and Behruz Mofidi Shirazi's Farsi translation project.
