segments.text: ISLAM: Its Mission in the World by Professor M. Farid Wajdi ISLAM: Its Mission in the World 1. UNITY OF RELIGIOUS BELIEF Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam. One of the great human aspects which lends immortality to Islam and establishes for it an historical right to intercourse with all people, is the inculcation of religious unity in so far as the source of religions is one and the same. The plurality and difference of religions were due to the addition, deletion and corruption which took place in the first and original faith.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: This notion of religious unity would have been regarded as an intellectual impossibility were it conceived in the olden days on account of the fundamental differences which existed between religions. Indeed, it is still regarded by the sociologists of today who are unacquainted with Islam, as a far-off hope because of the intermingling of religions with national and racial affairs. The efforts they made were therefore to exclude all religions from the field of human activities and to counteract its effect in society so that humanity may attain the universal peace and understanding for which it strives with nothing to obstruct its way.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: Yet, should those who study human affairs contemplate the principles on which Islam has established this unity and the historical facts on which it has relied, they would soon realize that these principles are by far more effectual than all the means employed by them. The beneficial effect of those principles had been amply shown in the uniting of nations in the early days of Islam despite the great influence which racial distinctions have had over their minds at the time. But these distinctions are fast disappearing today so much so that they have come to be regarded as purely theoretical.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: This has been due to the spread of philosophic and scientific ideas among nations, and to return today to Islam's principle of uniting them on a religious basis, would have more effect than it ever had before on the primitive nations which were devoid of all intellectual enlightenment. 57 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1): 57-62 نور الإسلام
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD Here someone may contend that the civilized nations of today do not depend on religion for their ascendancy or progress and even though we granted that they answered the call of Islam and adopted one religion, they have the economic problems which may overwhelm them and bring them into conflict. What advantage would the call to unity of religion avail so long as nations remain subject to social and economic factors? We should say Yes!
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: But does not our critic agree that these nations have come to realize that war is an abominable means to settle differences and that it weakens both victor and vanquished alike particularly when their interests in the economic field have become so intricate that the least trouble that upsets the one is bound to affect the other, and that for this reason they are looking for an effectual means to abolish it once and for all? If to these world-wide efforts the inculcation of the idea of one religion be added, would it not be to the good of the world? Would it not contribute to the unity of nations and help to overcome the destructive forces of disunion? Let us now consider the principles on which Islam has founded the unity of religious belief and the historical facts on which it has relied to render this idea acceptable to the minds: 1.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: Islam has proclaimed that the religion of God is one and the same for all times, that it was revealed to the first apostle sent to mankind and that the Lord has continued its revelation to His apostles from time to time of the world history to renew the signs which have been obliterated, elucidate its principles and rectify the corruption which took place. In this connection the Lord says: [Arabic text] God has ordained to you the religion which He commanded unto Noah, and which I revealed to thee and which I commanded unto Abraham, Moses and Jesus: Observe thou this religion by true belief and obedience, and divide not into sects concerning it. The worship of one God to which thou callest them is intolerable unto the disbelievers. God will choose to that Faith whomsoever he pleaseth, and will guide thereunto whomsoever shall turn unto Him (42:13). 2.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: Religion is a divine instinct which the Lord has implanted in human nature and no human soul is devoid thereof. In this respect it is undeniably a natural instinct and the Lord says: شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ الدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِ نُوحًا وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ ۖ أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ ۚ كَبُرَ عَلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ ۚ اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إِلَيْهِ مَن يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: M. Farid Wajdi [Arabic text] Wherefore set thou thy face towards the true Faith deviating not therefrom: the law of God to which men are created and are naturally disposed. No one could change the creation of God. This is the true Faith but the greater part of men know it not (30:30). 3. Islam has established pure reason to be a guiding beacon in all differences in the light of divine revelation. 4. The cause of all differences in religion which leads to division therein, is the tendency to iniquity, disregard of reason and blind imitation. In this connection the Lord says: [Arabic text] Nor were the past generations divided among themselves, through enmity and mutual jealousy, till after the knowledge of truth had come to them (42:14).
segments.label: page

segments.text: The Lord also says: [Arabic text] And they shall say, "If we had but hearkened to the discourse of the apostles or had rightly considered it, we should not have been among the dwellers of burning fire" (67:10). And: [Arabic text] And when it is said unto the believers, "Follow ye what the Lord has sent down," they say, "Nay, but we will follow only that which our fathers practiced." What! will they do so even though their fathers were utterly ignorant and were not guided to the truth? (2:170). 5. Islam which God had revealed to the seal of His prophets Muhammad (on whom be peace) was the first and initial Faith with which the Lord had sent him to mankind in its entirety to announce unto them these facts and to settle the differences which their passions have provoked.
segments.label: page

segments.text: In this connection the Lord says: ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1) 59 فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ الَّتِي فَطَرَ النَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ الدِّينُ الْقَيِّمُ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ وَمَا تَفَرَّقُوا إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ وَقَالُوا لَوْ كُنَّا نَسْمَعُ أَوْ نَعْقِلُ مَا كُنَّا فِي أَصْحَابِ السَّعِيرِ وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ
segments.label: page

segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD Verily the true Religion with God is submission to Him (Islam) and none other is acceptable unto Him; and those who were given the Scriptures differed not concerning it until after the knowledge of its truth had come to them, through mutual jealousy and desire for supremacy; and whomsoever believeth not in the signs of God, verily God is prompt in reckoning with him [3:19]. And: Do the unbelievers seek a religion other than God's, and to Him had everyone in heavens and earth submitted, willingly or unwillingly, and unto Him shall they return? [3:83].
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: In order to give this religious unity the highest consideration in the minds of men, it was included in the Qur'an in a purposely detailed verse so that no doubt may assail it: Say ye believers: We believe in God and that which has been sent down to us, and that which has been sent down to Abraham and Ismael and Isaac and Jacob and his offsprings, and that which was given to Moses and Jesus and that which was given to the Prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them and unto God we are resigned. If therefore they believe in what ye believe, then they are rightly guided; but if they turn away from the true faith, then they are divided among themselves and God will suffice to protect you against them, for He is the Hearer, the Knower.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: The 60 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1) إِنَّ الدِّينَ عِندَ اللَّهِ الْإِسْلَامُ ۗ وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا مِن بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ بَغْيًا بَيْنَهُمْ ۗ وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنزِلَ إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِّنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ۝ فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنتُم بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوا ۖ وَّإِن تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا هُمْ فِي شِقَاقٍ ۖ فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ ۚ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ۝ صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ ۖ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً ۖ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: M. Farid Wajdi law of God to which we are created, there is no better law than His! And Him do we worship [2:136-138]. These principles which show the source of religions to be one, are readily admitted by reason on mere contemplation for they are among its primary axioms. As to the source of religions being one in all times, no other fact could be more acceptable to reason, for truth is one and could never be more. As to religion being a divine institution identical with the natural instincts, it is a fact that admits of no doubt for souls are prone to seek the truth and submit to its judgment so long as they are guided by the light of pure reason.
segments.label: page

segments.text: As to the tendency to iniquity, disregard of reason and blind imitation of the practices of ancestors being the cause of differences which divide people among themselves, it is a fact that no one could gainsay and is well borne out by history. Should man rid himself of all these imperfections and appeal to reason in his search after true religion he will certainly come to Islam. The adoption of these principles in the present day has become within reach of everyone. The spread of learning among the different classes of people and the independent thinking and formulation of personal opinion inspired by wide reading have paved the way for the adoption of these Islamic principles. But they should be presented to people in a form well-worthy of the greatness of the ideals inculcated by them.
segments.label: page

segments.text: And now that Islam has allied itself with reason and science which rests on no hypothesis or conjecture, nothing stands between it and the far-flung dominion anticipated for it, save the organization of the proper introduction and the expounding of its universal principles in every language. Once this is done, no power on earth could stand in its way or stem its tide. Indeed, the religious beliefs of nations have become so interwoven with their national life that they constitute a principal element of that life. Many nations still hold to these beliefs to maintain their national existence though they no longer believe in them. But through the succession of events which gave rise to a spirit of friendly co-operation between nations and confirmed the belief that their safety lies in mutual understanding, nationalism is losing ground day by day.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Further, the economic crises brought about by trade competition have indicated to nations the necessity of setting up a universal system for agricultural and industrial production so that the world may be spared the economic dearth which induce nations to war in the same way as their early ancestors did. This method has not only become abominable, but it has also proved detrimental, for the economic relations between nations ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1) 61
segments.label: page

segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD based on the modern business system are so greatly affected by war that the victor so often loses the fruits of his so called victory by the great losses in souls which may exceed those of the vanquished nation itself. It has now become evident that economic depressions affect all nations, victors or vanquished alike. These considerations have induced the nations of today to seek fresh means of life commensurate with the present changes and the degree of cultural progress which science has brought about in every sphere of life. The efforts are calculated to save humanity from the dangerous passes that may take her back to the early days of barbarism. Every advocate of unity today brings to the tortured humanity a new remedy with which to heal its wounds.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: The call to unity is everywhere received with general approval though the beliefs of men have become an elemental part of nationalism in every country. But nationalism has been badly shaken and human communities have felt the need to reorder their time-worn systems to conform with their present and future requirements. We find today nations of different creeds and religions concluding defensive offensive alliances, a thing which could not have taken place up to the last century. The French had risen against their king Francis I for having sought the aid of the Turks against Charles V Emperor of Germany and Austria who threatened to occupy their country in the sixteenth century. The present day disregard of these considerations is a new departure in international relations and affords ample evidence to the impending overthrow of the barriers that once separated nations.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: All this and the like is fast paving the way for the golden age promised by Islam to humanity. It rests with Muslims to make public the great principles inculcated by the Qur'an and draw the attention to the study of Islam so that it may become known unto the whole world. We will show the unbelievers Our signs in distant climes, and through the wonders wrought in the creation of man till it becomes manifest unto them that the Qur'an is the truth. Doth it not suffice that thy Lord is witness over all things? (41:53).
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: Do the unbelievers seek a religion other than God's and to Him had everyone in heavens and earth submitted willingly or unwillingly, and unto Him shall they return? (3:83). 62 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1) سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ ۗ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا وَكَرْهًا وَإِلَيْهِ يُرْجَعُونَ
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI mainstream of Sufism as one of the faithful dervishes of Al-Rāḍi. Prior to his initiation, of course, Guenon became a Muslim; he changed his name to ‘Abdul-Wāḥid Yaḥyā, married and lived in Egypt until he died in 1370 AH (1951 C.E.). Shaykh Salāmah Al-Rāḍi was born in Egypt 1293 (1867) and received his general education in the public schools. Thus, like most Sufi teachers, he did not receive his religious education through formal religious schools. Upon completion of his education, Shaykh Salāmah obtained a position with the Egyptian government as an accountant. He remained in this position until his retirement in 1355 (1927) as Chief of the Government’s Properties Section, Gīza Province Administration.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: Shaykh Al-Rāḍi belonged to the modern Sufi school of ‘Ali b. ‘Abdullāh Al-Shādhilī, better known as Abul-Ḥasan Al-Shādhilī. This particular school of Sufism advocates not only full participation in this life, but also transforming the daily worldly affairs into a form of worship. Through this series of aphorisms, the readers will gain a better insight into the life and thoughts of this great Sufi leader. 1. My beloved ones: You must realize that your Master is Merciful. He looks with utmost kindness upon His servant and rejoices when he moves towards Him. He commands the angels in the heavens to welcome him, and to accompany him along the path of light. Your Master is kinder than the kindest parent. Therefore, O you who are fleeing from the mercy of your hospitable and compassionate Master, come back. Your Master is waiting eagerly for you at the gates of His mercy.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: Lest you may fall into merciless hands, He has sent His beloved messenger to guide you to the right path, and to warn you from pitfalls. Yet, He sees that you still reject His hospitality which awaits you. He sees you surrounding yourself with your enemies who took you as their captive, placed chains around your neck and your feet, and isolated you in the prison of remotion and darkness. Your Almighty Master expects you to remember Him and to call upon Him, that He may guide you out of the darkness and into the light. Your Master is close to you. If you turn to Him with all your mind, all your soul, you will find Him right by you, saying, “Welcome, welcome, my beloved one.” He is ready and willing to forgive your past rejection of His guidance, and for as long as you place your heart with Him, your Master will be with you. The door is wide open; acceptance and forgiveness appear through it. Your Master misses you. Move towards Him, even one step, and He will run towards you, happily welcoming you; fulfilling your needs; 64 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1)
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI admitting you into the abode of dignity and honor; clothing you with garments of happiness, satisfaction, and acceptance. 2. My beloved ones: If you really wish to be slaves of God, you should submit to your Master without reservations, and behave like slaves. When your Master sees this from you, and finds you consistently in His servitude, He will surely fulfill your needs and defend you. Can anyone humiliate a slave whose Master possesses all dignity and all power? 3. My beloved ones: If you want your Master to be pleased with you, you should first be pleased with Him; pleased with whatever He ordains. When you see someone dissatisfied and unhappy with your deeds, you will certainly be displeased with him. The satisfaction of your Master starts with your own satisfaction. 4.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: Dear beloved ones: If you reflect very carefully, you will realize that your Master, the possessor of all dignity and all power, actively provides for your needs while you're asleep. When you wake up, you take His provisions and employ them in the very things that displease your Master. He does not treat you with justice; He is much too kind for mere justice. He treats you with grace and compassion, that you may treat Him rightly some day. He sees you persistent in sinning, but He continues to be Clement with you, and extends to you the rope of respite and generosity; He keeps the door of repentance wide open, that you may return to Him. 5. Dear beloved ones: Your hearts are where your love is. Therefore, you shall place your love in the hands of your Master, that your hearts may be at Him. 6. My beloved ones: Instinctively, the hearts love whoever is good to them.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: But I see you not loving your Master, who created you, showered you with His bounties, and treated you with clemency and kindness. 7. Dear beloved ones: When the slave runs away from his Master, and befriends other fleeing slaves, he deprives himself from the care of his Master, and removes himself out of His sight. 8. Dear beloved ones: Have you found anyone better than your Master; a better substitute whom you can love? If you were on the right path, you would find that your Master is the only real love. ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1) 65
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI 9. Dear beloved ones: Your Lord is Benign to His slaves, and He loves those who are benign to them. Therefore, if you want Him to be kind to you, you shall have mercy upon His slaves; especially the weak and the poor among them, for they have none to help them except their Master. 10. My beloved in (the cause of) God: Whatever you feel in your hearts of hatred and envy is but the result of the devil's occupation of your hearts. Therefore, you shall purge your hearts by trusting and loving the creatures of God.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI

segments.text: Islamic Concentrates: The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 1 Islamic Concentrates The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 1 ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī, a famous Persian Sufi, was born in Herat 396 AH (1005 C.E.). It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet Muhammad (God’s blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat with ‘Aṣāf, son of Qays. Anṣārī’s father, Abu Manṣūr Muḥammad Anṣārī, became a permanent resident of Herat. These invocations, translated into English by Sir Jogendra Singh, contain true advice to guide the Pilgrim along the path of discipleship to the temple of peace. They come from a man who himself had trodden the path and found what his heart desired. When ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī departed from this world, he was 85 years old, leaving behind a wealth of Sufi knowledge.
segments.label: page - Islamic Concentrates: The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 1

segments.text: Among his well-known works are Risāla Munājāt (The Book of Prayer), Tabaqat-ul-Ṣūfiyyah (The Book of Sufis), Zād-ul-‘Arifīn (Provisions of the Sufi Teachers), and Kitāb-i-Isrār (The Book of Mysteries). In the name of God, Most Gracious, Most Merciful. O Thou Munificent One Who art the bestower Of all bounties, O Thou wise One Who overlookest our faults, O Self-existent One Who art beyond our comprehension, O Thou omnipotent One Who hast no equal in power and greatness, Who art without a second: O Thou merciful One ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1): 67-69 67
segments.label: page - Islamic Concentrates: The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 1

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 1 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 1 Who guidest stray souls to the right path, Thou art truly our God. Give purity to our minds, Aspiration to our hearts, Light to our eyes. Out of Thy grace and bounty Give us that which Thou deemest best. O Lord, Out of Thy grace give faith and light to our hearts. And with the medicine of truth and steadfastness cure the ills of our life. I know not what to ask of Thee, Thou art the Knower. Give that which Thou deemest best. O Lord! I have wasted my life, Injured my soul, And pleased the accursed Satan. My being or not being is of little worth. Accept my repentance and forgive my sins, Take me from sorrow to happiness. From the consequence of my past actions And perils of the future I see no way of escape. O Lord! I am afraid of the evil within me.

segments.text: The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 1 (Hijra / Gregorian) Islamic Concentrates The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 1 (Hijra / Gregorian) Over the first five issues of ISLAM, the Journal will publish this table for convenient conversion of dates from either of the two calendar systems. Such chronological conversion tables have been difficult to find yet most indispensible for the Western scholar of Islam. Since all great works of Islamic literature refer exclusively to Hijra dates, the Editors feel that these tables will be useful to many readers. According to the historians, the prophet Muhammad (God's blessings be upon him) arrived at Medina on the 12th day of Rabi' I, coincident with September 24, 622 CE (Christian Era). This sets the first day of the first Hijra year (Muharram 1, 1) as July 16, 622. Fifteen hundred Hijra years will be covered in these tables (622-2076 CE).

segments.text: Book Review Book Review Race and Color in Islam by Bernard Lewis. Harper & Row, New York, 1971. 104 pages, $2.25. According to Bernard Lewis, a host of people including blacks like Malcolm X and whites like Arnold Toynbee, have been deceived by the “myth” of Islamic racial equality. His purpose in this book, he says, is “to correct the false pictures drawn by the myth-makers, the picture of the total absence of such evils (of race and color prejudice) ... to refute the claims ... of exclusive virtue ... and to point to certain common failings of our common humanity.” (p. 102). Lewis’ attempt is not novel. In 1967 a black Christian preacher, the Reverend Albert Cleage, delivered a widely-published speech in which he made a similar charge with reference to the conversion of Malcolm X to Islam: “According to the myth, his pilgrimage to Mecca turned Brother Malcolm into an integrationist ...
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: I say I do not believe this myth ... He would not have been taken in by what happened in Mecca. Brother Malcolm knew that the Arab Muslims had been the backbone of the slave trade.” (Malcolm X, The Man and His Times, ed. by John Henrik Clarke, Collier Books, N.Y., 1969, pp. 14, 15.). I recall reading a piece in The Washington Post newspaper in 1969 which asserted similarly that Arab Muslims were “the most notorious slave traders in history.” The Cleage speech may be passed off as simple religious rivalry. The Post article was written in the context of questioning why so many black Americans are becoming Muslims. Lewis, however, comes in the guise of the dispassionate, objective scholar. It is strange that the book is titled Race and Color in Islam, since its primary purpose is the attempt to document racism and color prejudice as practiced by a few Muslim individuals.
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: The first flaw is that Lewis does not know what Islam is. He gives the Qur’an and the example of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) only passing mention, but spends a lot of time with The Arabian Nights. As his book develops it is clear that, for him, Islam means “not what Muslims believed or were expected to believe but what they actually did.” (p. 6). For this reason, his entire study lacks validity. His basic working premise is false; therefore, his conclusions are false. Islam is what Muslims do in obedience to the Qur’an and the example of Muhammad. That which is done contrary to the letter or spirit of Islam is not Islam, even if the doer is a Muslim, as is made clear in several Ahādīth reported by Bukhārī and Muslim. (See Mishkat al-Maṣābīḥ, vol. 1, pp. 17, 19.). Racial prejudice and slave trading do not represent Islam, even if practiced by some Muslims, because both are against the principles upon which Islam stands. ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1): 81-84 Ahādīth, Mishkat al-Maṣābīḥ
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: Secondly, to follow to its logical conclusion a train of thought and "evidence" such as Lewis presents, one would be forced to concede that genocide is the essence of Christianity merely because Hitler was a Catholic, or that Christ (peace be upon him) was a racist simply because South Africa is a "Christian" country. It is indeed possible to be scholarly absurd and this book is a prime example of scholarly absurdity. Lewis carefully picks and chooses "facts" to suit his argument, even while admitting that many of his references are questionable and not represent the complete picture, while passing over a mass of evidence which disputes his claims. No one will deny that Islam, the system of liberation, equality and freedom, had to wage a hard struggle in order to eradicate pride of tribe and race from the hearts of the people with whom it came in contact.
segments.label: page

segments.text: It is also true that some people were not cured completely of their prejudices immediately, and there were those in the dār-ul-Islām who, from time to time, slipped back into their old vices. But these are normal human failings, not failure of the system. During the time of the Prophet (peace be upon him), a certain companion taunted another by calling him "Ibn al-saudā", "son of the black woman." To Muhammad, a member of the noblest Arab tribe of Quraysh, such prejudice was nothing but pure ignorance (Jahiliyya). (Bukhari 2:21). The bulk of examples which Lewis cites of "Islamic" racism are from 900 to 1200 C.E., a period when some Muslims were influenced, not by Islam, but by racial mores of the pagans and Christians.
segments.label: page

segments.text: And it is significant that some Muslim chronologists wrote just as disparagingly of white Europeans as they did of pagan Africans: "Thus they lack keenness of understanding and clarity of intelligence, and are overcome by ignorance and dullness, lack of discernment, and stupidity. Such are the Slavs, the Bulgars, and their neighbors." (Sa'id al-Andalusi of 1029-1070 C.E., quoted on p. 36.). Lewis admits that Muslims enslaved both black and white captives of war, but insists that the trade in black slaves was evidence of Muslim racial discrimination. This non sequitur is typical of his shallow scholarship.
segments.label: page

segments.text: If racial prejudice existed to even a fraction of the extent he claims, there never would have been the great black Islamic empires of West Africa which arose from 850 C.E. on and flourished, establishing extensive diplomatic, cultural and economic relations with the Muslim east as well as Muslim North Africa. It is strange that Europeans like Lewis (and some misinformed blacks) attempt to tag Islam as worse in slave trading than European Christianity, whereas African writers themselves highlight the vast difference: "(Slave trading by Muslims) did not compare in extent with the slave trade later carried on across the Atlantic. The demand for household slaves was less than the demand for plantation slaves; nor was it possible to transport by land, across the desert, the large numbers that could be packed into ships. Their fate 82 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(1) dār-ul-Islām, Ibn al-saudā, Jahiliyya
segments.label: page

segments.text: at their destination was likely to be preferable to what met slaves in America. In Muslim society a slave could rise to a high place . . . Nor was Muslim slavery based on color. Though the slaves exported across the Sahara were all Africans, many Muslim households in North Africa also had European slaves, captured in war . . . The famous (black) king Mansa Musa of Mali, when he visited Cairo on his pilgrimage to Mecca (in 1324 C.E.), bought white Turkish slaves there to take home with him." (A Thousand Years of West African History, ed. by A. Ajaye, U. of Ibadan Press, Nigeria, 1965, p. 245.). Arab slavery on Africa's east coast was also much smaller in volume than was the European slave trade. (See Africa and Africans by Paul Bohannan, The Natural History Press, N.Y., 1964, p. 108.) Islam allowed the enslavement of war captives so long as the enemy enslaved Muslims captured in war.
segments.label: page

segments.text: However, the emphasis in the Qur'an and in the example of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was of liberating slaves as quickly as possible. Kidnapping people to enslave them, and trading in slaves for economic gain has always been forbidden in Islam. Therefore, those few Muslims who engaged in slave trading were not representative of Islam, but were following their own desires or imitating the European Christians, for whom slave trading eventually became big business. But it is clear even so that those Muslims who did engage in slaving did not do so for racial discrimination against Africans, as Lewis suggests. Under Arab and African slavery, slaves were treated as human beings with recognized rights. Nor were slaves considered inherently inferior due to their color, but merely victims of adverse circumstances.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Islam is the only system of life which not merely advocated the liberation of slaves but which also provided incentives for people to become liberators. In Qur'an [4:92], for example, the concept of tahriru raqabah "freeing the neck," i.e., libertaing a slave is mentioned three times as a ransom for one's own sins. Similarly, in Qur'an [5:92] God says: "In order to atone (or seek remission) . . . liberate a slave (tahriru raqabah)." In Qur'an [2:177] we are told: "It is righteousness . . . to spend money, despite one's love thereof . . . for the liberation of slaves." And at Qur'an [90:12, 13] God says: "And what will explain to you the exalted path (of true belief)?
segments.label: page

segments.text: It is to emancipate a slave (fakku raqabah) . . ." Furthermore, the gradual emancipation practiced by the early Muslims, in accordance with the Qur'anic instructions, was an act of social welfare which worked to ease the rigors of readjustment to the life and responsibilities of the free man. This contrasts most favorably to the example of American emancipation, during which ex-slaves were merely cast off without proper resources to provide for themselves, so that even a hundred years later, the descendants of ex-slaves in America face crushing social and economic problems. segments.text: It is held that when a Seeker gives his heart and mind to the search, and disperses the mists that arise from tumultuous passions, Truth becomes brighter and brighter and fills the Soul with its light. It is asserted that while reason is puzzling itself about mystery of consciousness, time, and space, the man of Faith is going forward from discovery to discovery, in the growing illumination of his heart. But it must be recognised that this knowledge is only available to those whose eyes are fixed, like an archer, on the arrow and the object at which he aims, and that without purity of purpose and unceasing effort deliverance cannot be obtained. In all ages and in all times men have sought and found truth. They have shown the way and means of attainment. But men have listened to the message with incredulity and continued the mad pursuit of sense objects.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Passions of body and mind govern men and kindle fires of desire, of greed, attachment, egoism and anger. These enslave and obscure the mind which must be freed, and restored to its pristine purity to reflect truth. The seekers of truth, therefore, concentrate all their strength in drawing away the mind from sense objects and to set it free from the dominations of fear and hate. Some follow the path of knowledge, and others the path of devotion, hoping to lose all sense of duality in the supreme uprising of love. (from Preface of "The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī”) ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī

segments.text: Notes to Authors Notes to Authors It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity. The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyās), consensus (Ijmā'), and personal thought (Ijtihād). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference.
segments.label: page - Notes to Authors

segments.text: Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint. Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations.
segments.label: page - Notes to Authors

segments.text: ISLAM: Its Mission in the World by Professor M. Farid Wajdi ISLAM: Its Mission in the World 2. CONDEMNATION OF THE PRINCIPLE OF BLIND IMITATION Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam. In all ages throughout the human history, reformers were never confronted with a stronger obstacle than that of blind imitation of forefathers and leaders of old religions. This inaction has been the cause of the persistence to this day of corrupted religions whose survival in our times is a slur on the human intellect.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: It was equally responsible for the continual existence of certain sects which exploited the ignorance of people who were otherwise well-fitted to take their place among the rising nations but have for this reason remained in stygian darkness down to the present day. Only one who has made a thorough study of the religions professed by the majority of contemporary nations as well as of the few hundred minor divisions derived therefrom, could appreciate the pernicious influence exercised by blind imitation over the life of people and the harm involved in the consequent antagonism to learning and reason. Next to the establishment of its principal beliefs, Islam has striven against the tendency of blind imitation into which people have long lapsed without having it examined or assayed by reason.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: Indeed, this rational idea could never have been conceived by minds in those dark and remote times when humanity was yet under age. But when humanity attained maturity in the generations that followed, this idea became an essential element of the universal religion which was ordained by the Lord in His last dispensation, not only to conform with the momentous intellectual development that took place, but also to rouse the religious sentiment in the hearts of men and inspire them to still greater and higher attainments. Those interested in the investigation of human affairs of recent times will find out that souls have discarded all moral restraints and have fallen an easy prey to unbridled passion and wickedness while the religious sentiment 85 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 85-90

segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD which constitutes the supreme moral power mitigating those excesses, has become incapable to discharge its function in many a nation. It was on account of this that other agents were sought to counteract those excesses. Some have sought such agents in science, in the power of public opinion or in some human instinct. But the investigator who goes deeply into the initial causes of things, will soon realize that, of all human instincts, the religious sentiment is best suited to counteract those excesses and to wield the most beneficial influence over the souls of men.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: If, however, it has become unequal to the task in certain nations, it is only on account of the weakness which affected their religions and which was the outcome of what was impressed on the people as being traditional matters to be followed or disregarded as a whole. But if they knew that a religion existed which severely censures imitation and imitators, and insists on reasoning and consideration, a religion whose beliefs are founded on evidence and truth, and is withal framed in a system which surpasses that of modern scientific investigation in reasoning and accuracy, their hopes in regaining the influence of religion will be roused again. For once this influence is regained the religious sentiment is awakened and its power will once more be felt in the guidance of men and in setting up a virtuous civilization for the world.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: It was for this reason that Islam has striven hard to overcome the obstacle of blind imitation and has attempted to do this by different ways of reasoning aiming thereby at three objects: 1. To spread its life-giving principles calculated to revive humanity in its later days. 2. To conserve for the religious sentiment its intrinsic power which enables it to restrain the human passions and safeguard the people from being carried away by wickedness. 3. To render the system of religious investigation more advanced and more accurate than that of scientific investigation so that the latter may not overwhelm the former and put it into insignificance.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: This is a great objective at which Islam aimed so that reason may not hold undisputed sway over souls independent of the religious sentiment which the Lord has set to mitigate the brutal tendencies attendant on the human state and which no intellectual culture could restrain. This could only come about by convincing reason, by proof, to give due regard to that sentiment and to admit the power exercised by it.

segments.text: ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) M. Farīd Wajdi By so doing, Islam has succeeded to associate reason with the religious sentiment for the first time in the history of religions. It has succeeded, on the strength of these two great principles, to raise a nation which attained to the height of human progress and took the lead in both moral and scientific culture as well as in the religious leadership of the world. Islam was thus rendered equal to establish the highest civilization on earth without the least conflict between religion and reason and without people degenerating in their morals and propensities as is the case in the present day civilization. Let us now consider how far has Islam succeeded to fulfill this great project.
segments.label: page - ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

segments.text: Islam was revealed at a time when people were the slaves of false and corrupted religions which they inherited from their forefathers and from which they could not be moved. Any one who wished to move them therefrom was regarded by them as a bitter enemy merely because he attempted to bring about a reform. The campaign was first opened by admonitions and threats thus awakening in men the instinct of reasoning and urging them to reflection and consideration of the sad end to which past nations have come. This done, Islam began to attack the main cause which prevented them to consider any reform viz. the blind imitation of their forefathers even though they were completely in the wrong.
segments.label: page - ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

segments.text: In this connection the Lord says: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوْلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ And when they are told, "You shall follow what God has sent down," they say, "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers lacked both knowledge and guidance? The allegory of those who disbelieve is like those who parrot whatever they hear without any understanding. They are deaf, dumb, and blind. Thus, they fail to understand. (2:170-171) In the preceding verses, the Lord has given a representation of the state of those who were blinded by imitation.
segments.label: page - ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

segments.text: He who calls them to righteousness is likened to one who parrots whatever he hears without any comprehension. They are deaf, dumb, blind and devoid of understanding on account of their holding fast to the practices of their forefathers and refusing to put them to the test of reason. ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 87 وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوْلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ
segments.label: page - ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)

segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD The Lord says that if those unbelievers were asked to follow what the Lord has sent down, they will say "We follow only what we found our forefathers doing," to which the Lord replies rousing the instinct of reason in them: "What if their forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?" Then the Lord gave the above representation of them which no one with a whit of pride would tolerate, provoking them thereby to seek an outlet to their sorry state. In order to move them from this inaction, the Lord then applies different reasoning.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: And when they are told, "Come to what God has sent down; come to this Messenger," they say, "Enough for us is what we found our forefathers doing." What if their forefathers had neither knowledge, nor guidance? (5:104) That is, if the unbelievers were called to follow the guidance of the Qur'an they say the knowledge which we inherited from our forefathers is sufficient for us to which the Lord says: "Will you still say so if your forefathers lacked both the knowledge and the guidance?" And in this connection the Lord demanded of the unbelievers to support their claim of the so-called knowledge of their forefathers: Have you any certain knowledge to substantiate your claim that you may produce to us? (6:148) In another verse the Lord days: Bring me a scripture before the Qur'an or some vestiges of ancient knowledge to support your claim if you are truthful. (46:4) In describing the end of those who imitate their forefathers without any knowledge or a book to guide them, the Lord says: 88 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَعَالَوْا إِلَىٰ مَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ وَإِلَى الرَّسُولِ قَالُوا حَسْبُنَا مَا وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا ۚ أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ هَلْ عِندَكُم مِّنْ عِلْمٍ فَتُخْرِجُوهُ لَنَا ائْتُونِي بِكِتَابٍ مِّن قَبْلِ هَٰذَا أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِّنْ عِلْمٍ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبَابُ وَقَالَ
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: M. Farid Wajdi That is when the leaders shall disown their followers. They shall undergo the punishment and no help shall come to them.
segments.label: page

segments.text: The followers shall then say, "If we only get a second chance, we shall disown them as they have disowned us." Thus, God will show them the consequences of their deeds; nothing but sorrow for them, and they shall never exit from the hellfire. (2:166,167) And: The Lord will say unto the unbelievers on the Judgment day: "Enter ye into Hell together with nations of jinn and of men who have preceded you;" so oft as one nation enters, it shall curse its sister, until they have all entered in succession, the last of them shall say unto the first: "O Lord, these have led us astray, deal Thou unto them a double punishment of hell-fire;" and the Lord will say: "It shall be doubled unto all, but ye know not." And the first of them shall say unto the last: "Ye have no advantage over us and we have both been in error; taste ye therefore the punishment for that which ye have done." (7:38-39) In the preceding verses, the Lord points out that the followers of disbelief are just as culpable as the leaders, for the Lord has endowed all men with reason and required them to distinguish between truth and falsehood.
segments.label: page

segments.text: They are therefore equally responsible for their deeds and none of them has an advantage over the other. And when the imitators have asked the Lord to deal a double punishment to their leaders whose example they have imitated, the Lord has adjudged them both responsible and has doubled the punishment to them all. Such was the Lord's warning against persistence in blind imitation.
segments.label: page

segments.text: In another chapter of the Qur'an the Lord says: ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 89 الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبَابُ ۝ وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُوا مِنَّا كَذَلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ حَسَرَاتٍ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا هُمْ بِخَارِجِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ ۝ قَالُوا ادْخُلُوا فِي أُمَمٍ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ مِنَ الْجِنِّ وَالْإِنْسِ فِي النَّارِ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَتْ أُمَّةٌ لَعَنَتْ أُخْتَهَا حَتَّى إِذَا ادَّارَكُوا فِيهَا جَمِيعًا قَالَتْ أُخْرَاهُمْ لِأُولَاهُمْ رَبَّنَا هَؤُلَاءِ أَضَلُّونَا فَآتِهِمْ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا مِنَ النَّارِ قَالَ لِكُلٍّ ضِعْفٌ وَلَكِنْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ ۝ وَقَالَتْ أُولَاهُمْ لِأُخْرَاهُمْ فَمَا كَانَ لَكُمْ عَلَيْنَا مِنْ فَضْلٍ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ ۝ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا فِي النَّارِ ۝ وَقَالُوا مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَى رِجَالًا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ مِنَ الْأَشْرَارِ ۝ أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سِخْرِيًّا أَمْ زَاغَتْ عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصَارُ ۝ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ ۝
segments.label: page

segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD Unto the leaders it shall be said: "This is a company which shall be plunged with you into Hell," to which they shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they shall burn in hell-fire like us." And the followers shall say unto the leaders: "But ye, too! There shall be no welcome for you.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: It was ye who brought us to this and wretched is the abode." [38:59-60] On the entry of the unbelievers into Hell, angels shall say to the leaders: "This is a company of your followers that shall be plunged with you into Hell." The leaders shall say: "No welcome is there for them, they have had minds to distinguish between truth and falsehood and their punishment is hell-fire like us." The followers will retort: "No welcome for you either, you have enticed us into this delusion and wretched indeed is our ending." The Lord (may He be praised and glorified!) has seen fit to impress on us by such variegated forms of eloquence the fact that leaders and followers will come to the one and same evil end, and it avails the latter not to be followers of others so long as they have had minds by which to distinguish between truth and falsehood.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: By these solemn admonitions, Islam has demolished the principle of blind imitation of forefathers and has awakened the consciousness of individual responsibility. It has delivered the weak from their bondage to the strong and smashed down the invulnerable walls of exclusiveness which the leaders raised for their own ends. By demolishing blind imitation Islam has aimed at abolishing a state of ignorance in which men were enslaved to certain sects that made learning and religion an exclusive right only to themselves, and arbitrarily ruled the people even as absolute masters do. They suffered no censure or criticism to be passed on their actions and declined the admission, into their exclusive body, of any outsider though he may have been a noted man of learning and genius.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: Should this state of things become established in a nation, learning and religion will be rendered the exclusive right of a sect which will exploit them in their own interest and subject them to the dictates of their passion. In course of time, they will become a collection of stereotyped forms which will check the onward march of progress and stand between nations and the realization of their objectives. Freedom from the shackles of imitation was the objective of Islam and it has led its people to a perfect state of cooperation between learning and religion as well as between sentiment and reason. Through this cooperation Muslims have attained to the height of progress which gave them the world-leadership for many a century and it is assured that they will regain that leadership once they follow faithfully, the tenets of their glorious religion. 90 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity by Yūsuf Amīn Walī, Ph.D. Treasurer, Supreme Council of the Muslim Young Men's Association, Cairo, Egypt God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity* God's finalized and completed message to man, namely, the Qur'an, was delivered in the Arabic language.** However, since it is intended for all the people, in all places, at all the times, it carries within its composition the proof of authenticity which can be understood and fully appreciated by anyone regardless of his tongue. On these pages, the reader is presented with physical, examinable, and indisputable evidence that the Qur'an is the unaltered message from the Almighty to His creation. Seekers of the truth shall find herein sure guidance towards their goal.
segments.label: page - God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

segments.text: The unfortunate souls who are afflicted with various prejudices shall be utterly blinded (Qur'an 18:57) The greatest affliction of man is the lack of identity and purpose. Once a correct identity is established, and once the purpose behind our existence is defined, such affliction can, sequentially, be removed. The vast majority of people spend their lives under the pretense that the body constitutes one's identity. Thus, they spend their lives caring for the body, the mere shell of their real self; working, laboring, fighting among themselves, hating, loving, and struggling in the service of their vanishing entity. When it is too late, i.e., when they shed the shell, they discover that their real self was left unfed, undeveloped, and miserably neglected.
segments.label: page - God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

segments.text: Their eternal existence in such a feeble state can be rightly described as "hell." On the other hand, those who are fortunate enough to overcome this identity crisis will be able to define their purpose, place the emphasis during their earthly existence on the right goal, and live and act accordingly. They will realize that developing their eternal entity requires putting the body in the service of the soul, and not the other way around. *Condensed from the book "Miracle of the Qur'an: Significance of the Mysterious Alphabets" by Rashād Khalifa, Islamic Productions International, Inc., St. Louis, Missouri, USA. 1973. **It had to be delivered in some language.
segments.label: page - God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

segments.text: The Qur'an itself states that its language is immaterial; that the believers shall grasp the full message therein, regardless of their mother tongue; and that even the Arabic-speaking people will not understand it unless they qualify therefor by sincerity and devotion (6:25, 18:57; 4:44; 56:77-79.) ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 91-104
segments.label: page - God's Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

segments.text: GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY Our Creator has informed us of the ways and means of developing and caring for the soul. His message, the one and only message, started with the creation of Adam, the first man; the first messenger. Subsequent messengers, such as Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad (may God bestow His blessings and peace upon them), delivered the same message whereby man can feed and develop his real self. With the arrival of God's final messenger, THE MESSAGE was finalized, and the Almighty Himself vowed to preserve it for all subsequent generations, and to protect it from alteration or distortion(1). Moreover, the Almighty has vowed to embed in His message such proof of authenticity that each generation can witness; leaving no excuse for anyone to disbelieve(2).
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: This article, which is but a glimpse from a vast computerized study of the Qur'an (3), offers an example of the visible miracles which are embedded in the Qur'an to prove its authenticity. Only those completely enslaved by worldly matters will deny the indisputable proof presented here. To appreciate this evidence which comes to all of humanity from their Creator, one needs no special knowledge of the Qur'an's language. The Qur'anic Initials One of the unique features of the Qur'an is the occurrence at the beginning of certain suras of alphabets which bear no apparent meanings. These alphabets, henceforth called "Qur'anic Initials," are not known in any other literary work. Of the 114 suras in the Qur'an 28 begin with one set of Qur'anic initials, and one sura is prefixed with two sets of Qur'anic initials.
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: Each set of Qur'anic initials consists of a number of letters ranging between one and five. The different sets of Qur'anic initials and the suras where they occur are listed in Table 1. As shown in that table, there are 14 different sets of Qur'anic initials, and the number of letters which participate in the make-up of these initials is also 14. The 14 letters involved in the formation of Qur'anic initials are Alif (A), Ḥā (Ḥ), Rā (R), Sīn (S), Ṣād (Ṣ), Ṭā (Ṭ), ‘Ayn (‘A), Qāf (Q), Kāf (K), Lām (L), Mīm (M), Nūn (N), Hā (H), and Yā (Y).
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: These letters are known in the Muslim literature, more specifically among the Sufi mystics, as "the illumination letters (الحروف النورانية)." The other half of the alphabet, the 14 letters not involved, are known as "the darkness letters (الحروف الظلمانية)." The suras which contain Qur'anic initials are listed in their recorded sequence in Table 2. 92 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) الحروف النورانية, الحروف الظلمانية

segments.text: The Qur'anic Initial Qāf (Q) Yūsuf Amīn Walī This article will deal with the miraculous features embedded in only two sets of these Qur'anic initials, namely, Qāf (Q) and Ṭā Sīn Mīm (ṬSM). For the complete computerized study of all 14 sets of Qur'anic initials, the reader may consult reference 3 listed below. The Qur'anic Initial Qāf (Q) There are two suras in the Qur'an which bear this initial, namely, sura Al-Shūrā (number 42) and sura Qāf (number 50). Although sura Al-Shūrā is more than twice as long as sura Qāf, these two Qāf-initialed suras contain the same number of the letter Qāf (Q), 57. At this point, we must stop and reflect on the significance of this observation. To derive correct conclusions, the following points should be borne in mind: 1. This observation is an undeniable fact; no speculation or guesswork is involved.
segments.label: page - The Qur'anic Initial Qāf (Q)

segments.text: It is a fact that anyone, anywhere in the world, can establish for himself, regardless of his language. The only prerequisite would be familiarity with one letter of the Arabic alphabet; the letter Qāf (Q). The letter looks like this: ق . When placed at the beginning of a word, it looks like this: قـ . When placed in the middle of the word, the letter Qāf (Q) looks like this: ـقـ . At the end of a word, the letter looks like this: ـق . With this minute amount of information, any person can look up the Qur'an, count the frequency of the letter Qāf in sura Al-Shūrā (No. 42) and in sura Qāf (No. 50). This person will physically establish THE FACT that the only two suras in the Qur'an which are initialed with letter Qāf contain the same number of this letter, namely 57. 2. The second fact one must bear in mind is that the Qur'an was revealed over a period of 23 years.
segments.label: page - The Qur'anic Initial Qāf (Q)

segments.text: Its verses came to us widely separated from each other both in time and place. Thus, sura Al-Shūrā, for example, contains 4 verses which were revealed in Medina, namely, verses 23, 24, 25, and 27. The other 49 verses were revealed, separately, in Mecca (300 miles from Medina). Sura Qāf consists of 44 Meccan verses and one Medinian verse (No. 38). These historical facts are significant, since they point out to us that the Author of the Qur'an knew in advance the alphabetical distribution within the Qur'an. One can readily see from the revelation system that such knowledge is beyond the ability of any human or group of humans(4). The evidence is overwhelmingly presented in this minute glimpse of the total study that the Qur'an could not be man-made. To indicate this advance knowledge to the recipients of His message, the Almighty Author placed the initial Qāf (Q) at the beginning of these two suras which contain the same number of this particular letter. segments.text: GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY 3. The fact that the two Qāf-initialed suras contain exactly the same number of the letter Qāf, provides physical evidence that the Qur'an was protected from human tampering throughout the past 14 centuries. Any alteration or distortion involving words such as Qad (قد), Qāla (قال), Qawn (قوم), etc., which are essential and very frequently used words, would have resulted in variability between these two suras with regard to their initial Qāf. The number 57 itself, being 50% of 114 (see 4(ii) below), provides a double-check that no alteration or distortion took place in the past. Of course, this is only a reflection, and undisputable confirmation, of the divine pledge that the Qur'an shall be preserved; protected from any distortion.(5) 4.
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: The computer printout, shown in Table 3, reveals that there is one more sura which also contains 57 of the letter Qāf, namely, sura Ibrāhīm (No. 14). Some readers may ask the question, "Why didn't the Qur'an's author place the initial Qāf at the beginning of sura Ibrāhīm as well?" There are numerous reasons which one can infer from the complete study: i. As mentioned above, having the same number of the letter Qāf (Q) is by no means the only characteristic of the Qāf-initialed suras. For example, the overall relative frequency of occurrence of the letter Qāf was found highest in the Qāf-initialed and Qāf-titled sura No. 50; higher than any other sura(3). Undoubtedly sura Ibrāhīm did not qualify for bearing the initial Qāf.
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: The complete study (3) revealed that the initialed suras possessed certain characteristics; certain distribution patterns of the alphabetic constituents, which qualified the sura for bearing specific initials. Thus, sura Ibrāhīm, which happens to be one of the 29 initialed suras, starts with the Qur'anic initials Alif (A), Lām (L), and Rā (R). On the other hand, the initial Qāf (Q) exists in sura Al-Shūrā in conjunction with 4 other Qur'anic initials, namely, Ḥā (Ḥ), Mīm (M), ‘Ayn (‘A), and Sīn (S). The letter Qāf is interlocked with these other 4 initials of sura Al-Shūrā, and the sura itself is interlocked with its 6 sister suras which bear the initials Ḥā Mīm (ḤM) (these are suras No. 40 through No. 46). The first verse in each one of these seven suras consists of the initials Ḥā Mīm.
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: Only sura Al-Shūrā (No. 42) has three additional initials, ‘Ayn Sīn Qāf (‘ASQ), which constitute verse No. 2 of the sura. The detailed study of the initials showed that the presence of ‘Ayn Sīn Qāf in sura Al-Shūrā serves as a specific indicator for a specific frequency distribution of these 3 letters, Ḥā Mīm-initialed suras) (see reference No. 3). These interlocking relationships point out the impossibility of composing a mathematically controlled literary work like the Qur'an(4). The presence of the initial 98 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) قد, قال, قوم

segments.text: Qāf in sura Al-Shūrā, therefore, serves a specific function. Sura Ibrāhīm, on the other hand, does not qualify as a bearer of the initial Qāf. ii. Why did the Almighty choose to place 57 Qāfs in the alphabetical structure of the two Qāf-initialed suras? Why 57, and not any other number? Does the number 57 in each of the Qāf-initialed suras represent a random choice, or a coincidental occurrence? No chance of either possibility. When we add the 57 Qāfs of sura Al-Shūrā plus the 57 Qāfs of sura Qāf, the product is 114, same as the total number of suras in the Qur'an. If the letter Qāf (Q) stands for "Qur'an", which is by no means a far-fetched assumption, then the number 57 in each of two suras would be the ONLY choice. The product, 114, tells us in clear language that the 114 suras do represent the Qur'an, the whole Qur'an, and nothing but the Qur'an.
segments.label: page

segments.text: The reader can see here another reason for restricting the initial Qāf to these two 57-Qāfed suras. These are by no means all the miraculous features of the Qur'anic initial Qāf. Presentation is made here of only a fraction of those features; a fraction which can be easily scrutinized, examined, and verified by any reader who has no access to electronic computers. For details dealing with the distribution of the letter Qāf throughout the Qur'an, the reader may consult reference 3. The Qur'anic Initials Ṭā Sīn Mīm (Ṭ.S.M.) This group of initials occurs in three suras which are consecutive both in the recording sequence and the chronological revelation sequence of Qur'an. Two suras are initialed with the three letters Ṭā Sīn Mīm. These are Al-Shu'arā' (No. 26) and Al-Qaṣaṣ (No. 28). The Qur'anic initials constitute an independent verse in these two suras.
segments.label: page

segments.text: The two letters Ṭā Sīn occur in sura Al-Naml (No. 27), and they make up only part of the first verse, rather than an independent verse. Thus, we have here three consecutive suras where the two-lettered set of Qur'anic initials separates the three-lettered sets of initials. The computer printouts of the percentage values of Ṭā Sīn Mīm, and their absolute frequency of occurrence values throughout the Qur'an are shown in Tables 4 and 5. The percentage values were calculated by dividing the total number of occurrences of the letters Ṭā (Ṭ), Sīn (S), and Mīm (M) by the total number of alphabetic letters which make up the sura. This was done for each one of the Qur'an's 114 suras. When we look at the ascending order of percentage values of Ṭā Sīn Mīm (Table 4), we note that sura Al-Qaṣaṣ (XXVIII) ranks 36, and sura Al-Shu'arā' (XXVI) ranks 79, out of the Qur'an's 114 suras. The arrangement of the three Ṭā Sīn/Ṭā Sīn Mīm suras, gives a special sense of balance. The observation that 35 suras contain a higher proportion of Ṭā Sīn Mīm than sura Al-Shu‘arā’, and the same number of suras contain a lower percentage than sura Al-Qaṣaṣ, leaves little doubt that the omission of Mīm in sura Al-Naml’s Qur’anic initials was not coincidental. The balanced distribution of the proportion of these 3 letters throughout the Qur’an, and the specific positioning of the two Ṭā Sīn Mīm-initialed suras leaves little doubt that the Author of the Qur’an had advance knowledge of the mathematical distribution of the Qur’an’s alphabetic letters.
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: The fact that this mathematical balance, manifested through the use of electronic computers, depends on the relative frequency of occurrence of Ṭā Sīn Mīm throughout the Qur’an is an undeniable evidence that the Qur’an could never be man-made, alone man-made by an illiterate man 14 centuries ago when the concepts of “percentage” and “proportion” were not known. In order to appreciate this miraculous phenomenon, let us go back in time 1400 years. A sizeable book is being constructed over a period of 23 years. The component sentences are widely separated from each other both in time and place. In advance, someone knew the exact relative frequency of the letters Ṭā (T), Sīn (S), and Mīm (M) (we have expressed this relative frequency by the ‘percent’ concept which was unknown in those days).
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: Thus, that “Someone” knew that out of 114 chapters, exactly 35 will have a higher relative frequency of Ṭā Sīn Mīm than chapter X, and exactly 35 will have a lower relative frequency than chapter Z. To indicate this fact, chapters X and Z were “tagged” with the letters Ṭā Sīn Mīm. And to convey the sense of balance inherent in this observation, chapter Y was “tagged” with the less powerful initials Ṭā Sīn (only 2 initials, and only part of the verse). Obviously, this kind of advance knowledge, and this kind of control over the distribution of individual alphabets, are unattainable by man.
segments.label: page - GOD'S MESSAGE TO HUMANITY

segments.text: Just as we did with the initial Qāf and the number 57, the reader is entitled to ask the question, “Why the number 35, and not any other number?” Why do we find exactly 35 suras containing a higher proportion of Ṭā Sīn Mīm than sura Al-Shu‘arā’, and exactly 35 suras containing a lower proportion of these letters than sura Al-Qaṣaṣ? Could this be a mere coincidence? Again, the divine proof is so overwhelming, the possibility of coincidence is eliminated. And again, the proof is physical, touchable, and examinable. Thus, if we look up the computer printout showing the simple frequency of occurrence of the letters Ṭā, Sīn, and Mīm (Table 5), we discover that sura Al-Shu‘arā’ (XXVI) contains 615 of these letters, while sura Al-Qaṣaṣ ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 102 Ṭā, Sīn, Mīm, Ṭā, Sīn, Al-Shu‘arā’, Al-Qaṣaṣ, Al-Naml, Qāf

Giving the greatest blow to all theories of racial discrimination, whether "scientific" or bigoted, God says further: O mankind. The emphatic point, 'so that you (mankind) may be mutually acquainted,' is just one expression in Arabic: lita'ārafū. ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 115 karramnā, karāmah, faḍl, āyāt, āyah, shu'ūb, lita'ārafū

segments.text: RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM In grammatical terms ta‘arafa is a Form VI verb which emphasizes the mutual application of the verb sense. The verb root itself is ‘arafa, which means ‘to be acquainted with; to approve of; to appreciate; to be positive about.’ The Qur’an, employing this expression lita‘arafū, is making the revolutionary statement that God made the different races and peoples so that the variety in mankind would lead to mutual acquaintance, mutual approval, mutual appreciation, a positive attitude.”(28) Bernard Lewis passes over this phenomenal statement, having blurred its import by translating shu‘ūb (races) as the vague term “confederacies” and asserting that the main point being made by it is “clearly social rather than racial.”(29) This assumption is incorrect. Shu‘ūb does refer to “races”. Dr. A. J.
segments.label: page - RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM

segments.text: Arberry so translates it in his The Koran Interpreted: “O mankind, We have created you male and female, and appointed you races and tribes . . .” The Muslim scholar Ḥāfiẓ Ghulām Sarwar likewise renders this verse: “O ye mankind! Surely We have made you out of male and female. And We have made into races and tribes . . .” (30) In his commentary on this verse Maulana ‘Abdul Mājid Daryabadi (Vol. 6, The Taj Co., Karachi, Pakistan, 1957, p. 818) writes: “In plain speech, all races of men, Europeans, Asiatics and Africans; white, brown and black are equally His creation . . .
segments.label: page - RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM

segments.text: This verse equally well demolishes the myth of a ‘master race,’ and completely supports the scientific finding that racial discrimination has no foundation in biological fact . . . this puts an end to the vast pseudo-science of ‘racial biology’ seeking to justify political ambitions (and) economic ends.” And, according to Dr. Muḥammad ‘Abdul-Ra‘ūf, the essential point being made here is that “all people are equal in the eyes of God, and He wants them to treat each other as equal. Distinction between people on the basis of race, color or wealth or on any other basis is artificial and should not be tolerated.”(31) Islam insists that racial variety should be a means of mutual attraction, and this has been the function of racial variety during the many millenia in which the human population interbred extensively.
segments.label: page - RACE, RACISM AND ISLAM

segments.text: English Meanings of the Qur'an : 2 English Meanings of the Qur'an : 2 by Rashad Khalifa, Ph.D. Sura Al-Baqarah (The Heifer) 2:30-98 In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful (The Creation of Man) 30 When your Lord said to the angels, “I will place on earth a viceroy,” they said, “Will you place therein one who may spread corruption and bloodshed; while we praise Your glory and hold You sacred?” He said, “I know what you know not.” 31 He taught Adam the names of all things, then presented them to the angels, saying, “Tell Me the names of these if you are right.” 32 They said, “All glory belongs to You. We have no knowledge, except that which You bestowed upon us.
segments.label: page - English Meanings of the Qur'an : 2

segments.text: Surely, You are the Omniscient, the Wise.” 33 God said, “O Adam, inform them of their names.” When he informed them of their names, God said, “Did I not tell you that I know the future of the heavens and the earth; that I know what you reveal as well as what you conceal?” 34 Then when I told the angels, “Fall prostrate before Adam,” they fell prostrate, except Iblis; he refused, due to arrogance, and thus, he became a rebel. 35 I said, “O Adam, dwell with your wife in Paradise; eat therefrom and enjoy whatever you like, but do not approach this one tree lest you become wrong-doers.” 36 However, Satan duped them, and caused their eviction therefrom. Thus, I said, “Go down as enemies of one another.

segments.text: On earth, there shall be your abode and provision for a finite period.” 120 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 120-136 وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا قَالَ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ فَقَالَ سُبْحَانَكَ لَا عِلْمَ نَادَاهُم بِأَسْمَائِهِمْ إِنِّي أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ وَإِذْ قُلْنَا رُوكَانَ مِنَ كَلَامِيهَا لِإِبْلِيسَ هَبِطُوا بَيْنَ

segments.text: A true understanding of Islam requires, as a minimum, a reasonable understanding of its message, the Qur'an. While many people acquire a distorted picture of the religion by observing some aspects of the actions, history, or personal conduct of its professed followers, the readers of this series are presented with an opportunity to grasp the basic principles of true Islam. Readers who are familiar with the various Qur'anic translations will appreciate the fact that this is the first English rendering of the Qur'an's meanings by a Muslim Arab. It is being printed for the first time.

segments.text: ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 121 وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (٣٠) وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَٰئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ (٣١) قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ (٣٢) قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ (٣٣) وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ (٣٤) وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ (٣٥) فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِۖ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۖ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍ (٣٦)
