segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:37-50 37 Then Adam received from his Lord certain commands whereby God redeemed him. Surely, He is the Redeemer, the Merciful. 38 I said, “Go down therefrom, all of you, and when My guidance comes to you, those who follow My guidance shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve. 39 As for those who disbelieve and reject My Revelations, they shall deserve the hellfire.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: They shall abide therein eternally.” (The Children of Israel) 40 O Children of Israel, be appreciative of the favors which I bestowed upon you; fulfill My covenant, that I may fulfill your covenant; you shall reverence Me; 41 You shall believe in what I reveal herein confirming what you have; do not be the first to reject it; you shall not trade away My revelations for a cheap material gain; you shall observe piety towards Me. 42 Do not confound the truth with falsehood, nor conceal the truth deliberately. 43 You shall observe the Ṣalāt prayers, pay the Zakāt charity (due alms), and bow (in prayer) with those who bow. 44 Do you order people to be righteous, while forgetting your own selves, even though you know the scripture? Have you not any understanding? 45 Seek help in perseverance and in the Ṣalāt.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Such is a difficult task, but not so for those who humble themselves; 46 who believe that they shall face their Lord; that they shall return to Him. 47 O Children of Israel, be appreciative of the favors which I bestowed upon you; I set you apart from all beings. 48 Beware of the day when no soul can avail another soul, no intercession can be accepted therefrom, no ransom can be paid, and no one can be helped. (Deliverance from Egypt) 49 Recall that I saved you from the Pharaoh’s people who inflicted severe persecution upon you; they slaughtered your sons and spared your daughters.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Such was an exacting trial from your Lord. 50 Recall that I parted the sea for you; thus, I saved you and drowned the Pharaoh’s people as you watched. 122 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) فَتَلَقَّىٰ آدَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ (37) قُلْنَا اهْبِطُوا مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّي هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَايَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (38) وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (39) يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا بِعَهْدِي أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّايَ فَارْهَبُونِ (40) وَآمِنُوا بِمَا أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوا أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍ بِهِ ۖ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا بِآيَاتِي ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَإِيَّايَ فَاتَّقُونِ (41) وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا الْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (42) وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ (43) أَتَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتَابَ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (44) وَاسْتَعِينُوا بِالصَّبْرِ وَالصَّلَاةِ ۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى الْخَاشِعِينَ (45) الَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَاقُو رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ (46) يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ (47) وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (48) وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَاكُم مِّنْ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوءَ الْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَاءَكُمْ ۚ وَفِي ذَٰلِكُمْ بَلَاءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (49) وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ (50)

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 123 الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة فَتَلَقَّىٰ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ (٣٧) قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٣٨) وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ (٣٩) يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِعَهْدِىٓ أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱرْهَبُونِ (٤٠) وَءَامِنُوا۟ بِمَآ أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍۭ بِهِۦ ۖ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِى ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱتَّقُونِ (٤١) وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (٤٢) وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرْكَعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ (٤٣) أَتَأْمُرُونَ ٱلنَّاسَ بِٱلْبِرِّ وَتَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَتْلُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ (٤٤) وَٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ۚ وَإِنَّهَا لَكَبِيرَةٌ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلْخَٰشِعِينَ (٤٥) ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُوا۟ رَبِّهِمْ وَأَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ (٤٦) يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ (٤٧) وَٱتَّقُوا۟ يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِى نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا شَفَٰعَةٌ وَلَا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (٤٨) وَإِذْ نَجَّيْنَٰكُم مِّنْ ءَالِ فِرْعَوْنَ يَسُومُونَكُمْ سُوٓءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يُذَبِّحُونَ أَبْنَآءَكُمْ وَيَسْتَحْيُونَ نِسَآءَكُمْ ۚ وَفِى ذَٰلِكُم بَلَآءٌ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ عَظِيمٌ (٤٩) وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ ٱلْبَحْرَ فَأَنجَيْنَٰكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ (٥٠)
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH 51 Recall that when I summoned Moses for forty nights, you worshiped the calf in his absence, and you turned wicked. 52 Yet, I pardoned you thereafter, that you may be appreciative. 53 Recall that I gave Moses the scripture and the statute book, that you may be guided. 54 Recall that Moses told his followers, "You have wronged your souls by worshiping the calf. Therefore, you shall repent to your Creator; you shall kill your ego. This would be best for you with your Creator." Subsequently, God absolved you.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surely, He is the Absolver, most-Merciful. 55 When you said, "O Moses, we shall not believe unless we see God in person," the lightning struck you as you looked. 56 Then, I revived you after you died, that you may be appreciative. (In Sinai) 57 I shaded you with clouds, and sent down to you manna and quails; "Eat from the good things I provide for you." Indeed, they did no harm to Me, but rather they harmed themselves. 58 When I said, "Go into this village and eat therefrom as you please; enter the gate in humbleness, and speak gently, that I may forgive your sins and reward the virtuous," 59 the evil ones distorted My commandments. Consequently, I showered the evil ones with wrath from the sky due to their wickedness. 60 Recall that when Moses sought water for his followers, I said, "Strike the rock with your staff." Whereupon, twelve springs gushed out therefrom.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Thus, each of the tribes had their own water; "Eat and drink from God's provisions, and roam not the earth in corruption." ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ ۖ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا هَٰذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ ۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رِجْزًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ ۖ فَانفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا ۖ قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ ۖ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِن رِّزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 125 الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة وَإِذْ وَاعَدْنَا مُوسَىٰ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ ﴿٥١﴾ ثُمَّ عَفَوْنَا عَنكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٥٢﴾ وَإِذْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَالْفُرْقَانَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ ﴿٥٣﴾ وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنفُسَكُم بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَىٰ بَارِئِكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوا أَنفُسَكُمْ ذَٰلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ عِندَ بَارِئِكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿٥٤﴾ وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نُّؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّىٰ نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً فَأَخَذَتْكُمُ الصَّاعِقَةُ وَأَنتُمْ تَنظُرُونَ ﴿٥٥﴾ ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاكُم مِّن بَعْدِ مَوْتِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٥٦﴾ وَظَلَّلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْغَمَامَ وَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَنَّ وَالسَّلْوَىٰ ۖ كُلُوا مِن طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ ۖ وَمَا ظَلَمُونَا وَلَٰكِن كَانُوا أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ ﴿٥٧﴾ وَإِذْ قُلْنَا ادْخُلُوا هَٰذِهِ الْقَرْيَةَ فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمْ رَغَدًا وَادْخُلُوا الْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُولُوا حِطَّةٌ نَّغْفِرْ لَكُمْ خَطَايَاكُمْ ۚ وَسَنَزِيدُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ ﴿٥٨﴾ فَبَدَّلَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا قَوْلًا غَيْرَ الَّذِي قِيلَ لَهُمْ فَأَنزَلْنَا عَلَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا رِجْزًا مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ بِمَا كَانُوا يَفْسُقُونَ ﴿٥٩﴾ وَإِذِ اسْتَسْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِب بِّعَصَاكَ الْحَجَرَ ۖ فَانفَجَرَتْ مِنْهُ اثْنَتَا عَشْرَةَ عَيْنًا ۖ قَدْ عَلِمَ كُلُّ أُنَاسٍ مَّشْرَبَهُمْ ۖ كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا مِن رِّزْقِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ ﴿٦٠﴾
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:61-68 61 When you told Moses, “We can no longer tolerate one kind of food; ask your Lord to produce for us earthly crops such as beans, cucumber, garlic, lentils, and onions,” he said, “Do you wish to substitute that which is inferior for that which is good? Go down to the countryside wherein you may find your request.” Thus, humiliation and poverty became their lot, and they incurred wrath from God.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: That, because they rejected God’s commandments and because they slew the prophets unjustly; because they rebelled and transgressed. 62 Surely, those who believe; those who were Jewish, Christian, or Sabian; any among them who did believe in God and the hereafter, and did good works, shall receive their recompense from their Lord; they shall have no fear, nor shall they grieve. (The Covenant) 63 Recall that I made a covenant with you, and raised Mount Sinai above you, saying, “You shall uphold this covenant strongly, and remember the contents thereof, that you may achieve piety.” 64 But you turned away thereafter, and were it not for God’s grace towards you and His mercy, you would have been destroyed. 65 You know what happened to those among you who desecrated the Sabbath; I said unto them, “You shall be despicable apes.” 66 Thus, I set them up as an example for their generation, as well as subsequent generations, and an admonition for the pious. (The Heifer) 67 When Moses said to his followers, “God commands you to sacrifice a heifer,” they said, “Are you kidding us?” He said, “God forbid that I may be so ignorant.” 68 They said, “Ask your Lord to show us what kind of heifer.” Moses said, “He says that she is a heifer which is neither too old, nor too young; of an average age.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: You shall carry out this command.” 126 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) حَتَّىٰ إِذَا قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ فَادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ مِن بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّائِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا ۖ قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ۚ اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ ۗ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا وَّكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ (61) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالنَّصَارَىٰ وَالصَّابِئِينَ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (62) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (63) ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنتُم مِّنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ (64) وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ (65) فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ (66) وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً ۖ قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا ۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ (67) قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ (68)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 127 الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصْبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٍ وَاحِدٍ فَادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخْرِجْ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنبِتُ الْأَرْضُ مِن بَقْلِهَا وَقِثَّائِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَا ۖ قَالَ أَتَسْتَبْدِلُونَ الَّذِي هُوَ أَدْنَىٰ بِالَّذِي هُوَ خَيْرٌ ۚ اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلْتُمْ ۗ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ وَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَوا وَّكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ ٦١ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالنَّصَارَىٰ وَالصَّابِئِينَ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ ٦٢ وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاذْكُرُوا مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ ٦٣ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَلَوْلَا فَضْلُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَتُهُ لَكُنتُم مِّنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ ٦٤ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمْتُمُ الَّذِينَ اعْتَدَوْا مِنكُمْ فِي السَّبْتِ فَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ كُونُوا قِرَدَةً خَاسِئِينَ ٦٥ فَجَعَلْنَاهَا نَكَالًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَمَا خَلْفَهَا وَمَوْعِظَةً لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ ٦٦ وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَىٰ لِقَوْمِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَن تَذْبَحُوا بَقَرَةً ۖ قَالُوا أَتَتَّخِذُنَا هُزُوًا ۖ قَالَ أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ الْجَاهِلِينَ ٦٧ قَالُوا ادْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا فَارِضٌ وَلَا بِكْرٌ عَوَانٌ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ فَافْعَلُوا مَا تُؤْمَرُونَ ٦٨
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:69-79 69 They said, “Ask your Lord to inform us of her color.” Moses said, “He says that she shall be a yellow heifer; bright-colored and pleasant looking.” 70 They said, “Ask your Lord to point her out for us. The heifers look alike; with God’s help we shall find her.” 71 Moses said, “He says that she is a heifer never humiliated in plowing the land or watering the crops; safe from any blemish.” They said, “Now you have brought the truth;” they sacrificed her, though reluctantly. 72 Then, when you committed a murder and disputed among yourselves, God decided to uncover what you tried to conceal. 73 Thus, I said, “Strike the victim with part of that heifer.” Whereupon, God revived the victim and showed you His signs, that you may understand. 74 Yet, your hearts hardened thereafter and became like rocks or even harder.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: For there are rocks from which rivers gush out; some rocks crack and gently release water; some rocks even stoop out of reverence for God. God is never unaware of anything you do. (Distortion of the Scriptures) 75 How do you expect them to believe with you? Some of them used to hear the word of God then deliberately distort it with full understanding thereof. 76 When they meet the believers, they say, “We believe in this,” but when in private with each other, they say, “Inform them not of the scripture revealed to you from God, lest they may use it to support their argument.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Do you not understand?” 77 Do they not realize that God knows whatever they hide, as well as whatever they disclose? 78 Among them there are those who have no knowledge of the scripture; they may think that they know it, but in fact they do not. 79 Therefore, woe to those who fabricate the scripture with their own hands, then claim that such writings came from God, seeking thereby a cheap material gain.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Woe to them as a consequence of their fabrications; woe to them as a consequence of their deeds. 128 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَاءُ لَوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ النَّاظِرِينَ إِنَّهُ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِيَ كَالْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً وَإِنَّ مِنَ الْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ الْأَنْهَارُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ الْمَاءُ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا لَكُمْ وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَامَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُ مِن بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ وَإِذَا لَقُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ قَالُوا أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم بِمَا فَتَحَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لِيُحَاجُّوكُم بِهِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْكِتَابَ إِلَّا أَمَانِيَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ الْكِتَابَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا فَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَآءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّـٰظِرِينَ ۝ قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ ٱلْبَقَرَ تَشَـٰبَهَ عَلَيْنَا وَإِنَّا إِن شَـٰٓءَ ٱللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ ۝ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِى ٱلْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا ۚ قَالُوا۟ ٱلْـٰـَٔنَ جِئْتَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ ۝ وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَٱدَّرَٰءْتُمْ فِيهَا ۖ وَٱللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ ۝ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْىِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ ۝ ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرُ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَاءُ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَـٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ ۝ أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟ لَكُمْ وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُۥ مِن بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ ۝ وَإِذَا لَقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ قَالُوا۟ أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم بِمَا فَتَحَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لِيُحَآجُّوكُم بِهِۦ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ ۝ أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ ۝ وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّا أَمَانِىَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ ۝ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَـٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا ۖ فَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ ۝ قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا لَوْنُهَا ۚ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ صَفْرَآءُ فَاقِعٌ لَّوْنُهَا تَسُرُّ ٱلنَّـٰظِرِينَ ۝ قَالُوا۟ ٱدْعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُبَيِّن لَّنَا مَا هِيَ إِنَّ ٱلْبَقَرَ تَشَـٰبَهَ عَلَيْنَا وَإِنَّا إِن شَـٰٓءَ ٱللَّهُ لَمُهْتَدُونَ ۝ قَالَ إِنَّهُۥ يَقُولُ إِنَّهَا بَقَرَةٌ لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ ٱلْأَرْضَ وَلَا تَسْقِى ٱلْحَرْثَ مُسَلَّمَةٌ لَّا شِيَةَ فِيهَا ۚ قَالُوا۟ ٱلْـٰـَٔنَ جِئْتَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ فَذَبَحُوهَا وَمَا كَادُوا۟ يَفْعَلُونَ ۝ وَإِذْ قَتَلْتُمْ نَفْسًا فَٱدَّرَٰءْتُمْ فِيهَا ۖ وَٱللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ ۝ فَقُلْنَا ٱضْرِبُوهُ بِبَعْضِهَا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْىِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَيُرِيكُمْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ ۝ ثُمَّ قَسَتْ قُلُوبُكُم مِّن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ فَهِىَ كَٱلْحِجَارَةِ أَوْ أَشَدُّ قَسْوَةً ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْحِجَارَةِ لَمَا يَتَفَجَّرُ مِنْهُ ٱلْأَنْهَـٰرُ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَشَّقَّقُ فَيَخْرُجُ مِنْهُ ٱلْمَاءُ ۚ وَإِنَّ مِنْهَا لَمَا يَهْبِطُ مِنْ خَشْيَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَـٰفِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ ۝ أَفَتَطْمَعُونَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟ لَكُمْ وَقَدْ كَانَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ كَلَـٰمَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُحَرِّفُونَهُۥ مِن بَعْدِ مَا عَقَلُوهُ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ ۝ وَإِذَا لَقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَا بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ قَالُوا۟ أَتُحَدِّثُونَهُم بِمَا فَتَحَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمْ لِيُحَآجُّوكُم بِهِۦ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ ۚ أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ ۝ أَوَلَا يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ ۝ وَمِنْهُمْ أُمِّيُّونَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ إِلَّا أَمَانِىَّ وَإِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ ۝ فَوَيْلٌ لِّلَّذِينَ يَكْتُبُونَ ٱلْكِتَـٰبَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ ثُمَّ يَقُولُونَ هَـٰذَا مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ لِيَشْتَرُوا۟ بِهِۦ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا ۖ فَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا كَتَبَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَوَيْلٌ لَّهُم مِّمَّا يَكْسِبُونَ ۝
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH (2:80-87) SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:80-87 (God's Chosen People?) 80 They say, “The hellfire will not touch us, save for a limited number of days.” Say, “Have you taken such a promise from God, and God never breaks His promise? Or, do you attribute to God what you know not?” 81 Yes indeed, anyone who commits sin, and becomes surrounded by his misdeeds, these shall be dwellers of the hellfire; they shall abide therein eternally. 82 As for those who believe and do good works, they shall be dwellers of Paradise; they shall abide therein eternally. (Transgressions of the Israelites) 83 Recall that I made a covenant with the Children of Israel that they shall not worship any except God; to be kind to the parents, the relatives, the orphans, and the poor; to speak with the people amicably; to observe the Salāt and pay the Zakāt.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH (2:80-87)

segments.text: But you turned away, except a few of you, and you became averse. 84 I made a covenant with you that you shall not shed your blood, nor shall you evict one another from your homes; you agreed and bore witness. 85 Yet, here you are slaying one another, and evicting some of you from their homes, banding together against them sinfully and defiantly. When they come to you as captives you demand ransom from them; evicting them was prohibited for you in the first place. Do you then believe in part of the scripture and disregard the other? What should be the requital for such deeds, except humiliation in this life and, on the Day of Resurrection, even worse retribution? God is never unaware of anything you do. 86 Such are they who traded away the hereafter for this lowly life.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH (2:80-87)

segments.text: Therefore, their retribution shall not be commuted, nor shall they receive any help. 87 I have given Moses the scripture and subsequent to him I dispatched many messengers. Similarly, I gave Jesus the son of Mary manifest signs, and I supported him with the holy spirit. Is it ever so that whenever a messenger comes to you with what you do not like, you resort to arrogance? Thus, some messengers you rejected, and some you slew.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH (2:80-87)

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah 80. And they say: The Fire shall not touch us but for a few days. Say: Have you taken a promise from Allah, then Allah will not fail to keep His promise, or do you speak against Allah what you know not? 81. Yea, whoever earns evil and his sins beset him, these are the companions of the Fire; therein they shall abide. 82. And those who believe and do good deeds, these are the companions of the Garden; therein they shall abide. 83. And when We made a covenant with the Children of Israel: You shall not worship any except God; and to parents, relatives, the orphans, and the needy, show kindness; and speak to people amicably; and observe the prayer and pay the zakat. But you turned away, except a few of you, and you are averse. 84.
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: And I made a covenant with you: You shall not shed your blood, nor shall you expel one another from your homes; you agreed and you are witnessing. 85. Then you are those who are slaying one another, and expelling a party of you from their homes, banding together against them in sin and hostility. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them; evicting them was forbidden to you in the first place. Do you then believe in a part of the Book and disregard the other? So what is the reward of those who do such deeds, except humiliation in the life of this world, and on the Day of Resurrection, even they shall be sent to the most grievous of torment. And Allah is not unaware of anything you do. 86. These are those who buy the life of this world for the hereafter, so the torment shall not be lightened for them, nor shall they be helped. 87. And indeed We gave Moses the Book and followed him with messengers, and We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs and strengthened him with the Holy Spirit. Is it that whenever a messenger comes to you with what your souls desire not, you become arrogant?
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: So a party you denied and a party you slay. وَقَالُوا لَن تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَةً ۚ قُلْ أَتَّخَذْتُمْ عِندَ اللَّهِ عَهْدًا فَلَن يُخْلِفَ اللَّهُ عَهْدَهُ ۖ أَمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (80) بَلَىٰ مَن كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً وَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ فَأُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (81) وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ أُولَٰئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَنَّةِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ (82) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ لَا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا وَذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَقُولُوا لِلنَّاسِ حُسْنًا وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا مِّنكُمْ وَأَنتُم مُّعْرِضُونَ (83) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ لَا تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَاءَكُمْ وَلَا تُخْرِجُونَ أَنفُسَكُم مِّن دِيَارِكُمْ ثُمَّ أَقْرَرْتُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ (84) ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ هَٰؤُلَاءِ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَتُخْرِجُونَ فَرِيقًا مِّنكُم مِّن دِيَارِهِمْ تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِم بِالْإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ وَإِن يَأْتُوكُمْ أُسَارَىٰ تُفَادُوهُمْ وَهُوَ مُحَرَّمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ إِخْرَاجُهُمْ ۚ أَفَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِبَعْضِ الْكِتَابِ وَتَكْفُرُونَ بِبَعْضٍ ۚ فَمَا جَزَاءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ ذَٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ إِلَّا خِزْيٌ فِي الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يُرَدُّونَ إِلَىٰ أَشَدِّ الْعَذَابِ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ (85) أُولَٰئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا بِالْآخِرَةِ ۖ فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ (86) وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَقَفَّيْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ ۖ وَآتَيْنَا عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ الْبَيِّنَاتِ وَأَيَّدْنَاهُ بِرُوحِ الْقُدُسِ ۗ أَفَكُلَّمَا جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لَا تَهْوَىٰ أَنفُسُكُمُ اسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ فَفَرِيقًا كَذَّبْتُمْ وَفَرِيقًا تَقْتُلُونَ (87)
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:88-98 88 They said, “Our hearts are saturated.” Nay, it is but a curse from God, due to their heathenism, that causes them to believe but rarely. 89 Thus, when this scripture came to them from God, confirming what they have, and though they used to predict to the disbelievers its coming, they rejected it when they realized it had come. Such is the curse of God upon the rejectors. 90 Miserable indeed is what they traded their souls for; disbelieving in these revelations of God, out of sheer jealousy that God should bestow His grace upon whomever He wills among His creatures.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Therefore, they incur wrath after wrath; the disbelievers shall suffer a humiliating punishment. 91 When they are told, “You shall believe in these revelations of God,” they say, “We believe only in what was revealed to us.” They reject subsequent scripture even though it is the truth; even though it confirms what they have. Say, “Why did you slay the prophets of God in the olden times, if you were really believers?” 92 Moses had come to you with manifest signs, but you worshiped the calf in his absence and you turned wicked. 93 Recall that I made a covenant with you, and raised Mount Sinai over you, saying, “You shall uphold this covenant strongly, and hearken.” They said, “We hearken, but we shall not obey.” Thus, their hearts were filled with adoration for the calf, due to their rebellion.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Say, “Miserable is what your convictions dictate upon you, if you do have any convictions.” 94 Say, “If the abode in the hereafter is guaranteed by God for you alone, to the exclusion of all others, then you should long for death if you are truthful.” 95 However, they never long for it, due to what their hands have committed. God is fully aware of the wrong-doers. 96 In fact, you shall find them the most covetous of life, even more so than the heathens; the one of them would wish to survive a thousand years. But this shall not move him any further from his due retribution, even if he does live long.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: God is Seer of everything they do. 97 Say to those who resent (the archangel) Gabriel that he conveyed this Qur’an into your heart, by God’s leave, confirming previous scriptures and providing guidance and good news for the believers. 98 If anyone chooses to oppose God, His angels, and His messengers, including Gabriel and Michael, then God will oppose such disbelievers. 132 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُوا مِن قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم مَّا عَرَفُوا كَفَرُوا بِهِ ۚ فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ (89) بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ أَن يَكْفُرُوا بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ بَغْيًا أَن يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ۖ فَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ عَلَىٰ غَضَبٍ ۚ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ (90) وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَيَكْفُرُونَ بِمَا وَرَاءَهُ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ ۗ قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنبِيَاءَ اللَّهِ مِن قَبْلُ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (91) وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ (92) وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاسْمَعُوا ۖ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ ۚ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ (93) قُلْ إِن كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ عِندَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً مِّن دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ (94) وَلَن يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ (95) وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَاةٍ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا ۚ يَوَدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ (96) قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ (97) مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ (98)

segments.text: Surat Al-Baqarah 2:88-98 وَقَالُوا قُلُوبُنَا غُلْفٌ ۚ بَل لَّعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِكُفْرِهِمْ فَقَلِيلًا مَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿٨٨﴾ وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُوا مِن قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَلَمَّا جَاءَهُم مَّا عَرَفُوا كَفَرُوا بِهِ ۚ فَلَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ ﴿٨٩﴾ بِئْسَمَا اشْتَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ أَن يَكْفُرُوا بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ بَغْيًا أَن يُنَزِّلَ اللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ۖ فَبَاءُوا بِغَضَبٍ عَلَىٰ غَضَبٍ ۚ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ مُّهِينٌ ﴿٩٠﴾ وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا بِمَا أَنزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا نُؤْمِنُ بِمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَيَكْفُرُونَ بِمَا وَرَاءَهُ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ ۗ قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِيَاءَ اللَّهِ مِن قَبْلُ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٩١﴾ وَلَقَدْ جَاءَكُم مُّوسَىٰ بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ ثُمَّ اتَّخَذْتُمُ الْعِجْلَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَنتُمْ ظَالِمُونَ ﴿٩٢﴾ وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا مَا آتَيْنَاكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَاسْمَعُوا ۖ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ الْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهمْ ۚ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِهِ إِيمَانُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٩٣﴾ قُلْ إِن كَانَتْ لَكُمُ الدَّارُ الْآخِرَةُ عِندَ اللَّهِ خَالِصَةً مِّن دُونِ النَّاسِ فَتَمَنَّوُا الْمَوْتَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ ﴿٩٤﴾ وَلَن يَتَمَنَّوْهُ أَبَدًا بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالظَّالِمِينَ ﴿٩٥﴾ وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ أَحْرَصَ النَّاسِ عَلَىٰ حَيَاةٍ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا ۚ يَوُدُّ أَحَدُهُمْ لَوْ يُعَمَّرُ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَ ۗ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿٩٦﴾ قُلْ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّجِبْرِيلَ فَإِنَّهُ نَزَّلَهُ عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَهُدًى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ﴿٩٧﴾ مَن كَانَ عَدُوًّا لِّلَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ ﴿٩٨﴾

segments.text: COMMENTARY COMMENTARY Predestination: In verse 30 of sura Al-Baqarah, the Almighty announces His intention to create man. A most significant statement in this verse, though invariably overlooked by most people, is the divine declaration, "I will place on earth..." Thus, the temporary abode of man on earth had been predestined, even before his creation. God knew in advance that Adam and Eve were going to break His law by eating from the forbidden tree (verse 36). He knew that they were going to sin; thereby disqualifying themselves from abiding in heaven, and deserving to be sent down to earth (verses 36 and 38). Man, on the other hand, did not possess such advance knowledge. As far as Adam and Eve were concerned, they were placed in heaven, and given a law to live by.
segments.label: page - COMMENTARY

segments.text: Therefore, in a most profound way, these verses teach us that predestination is a quality of God; Man's life, every aspect of it is indeed predestined, BUT ONLY AS FAR AS GOD IS CONCERNED. As far as we are concerned, we have the absolute freedom of thought; the absolute freedom to believe in God or disbelieve (18:29; 25:57; 39:15; 41:40; 73:19; 74:37,55; 76:29; 78:39; 80:12; 81:28). It just happens that the Almighty has foreknowledge of what course each one of us is going to choose. The dimension of "time" represents one of the limitations within which the finite man lives. But it is a nonexistent dimension with regard to the infinite God. The Almighty, therefore, exists in the past, present, and future simultaneously. Because He is in the future now, He knows the exact destiny of each one of His Creatures.
segments.label: page - COMMENTARY

segments.text: Predestination is one of the most misunderstood concepts in Islam; both by Muslims and non-Muslims. It is also one of the most abused concepts by the enemies of God; the enemies of Islam. They abuse it to project Islam as a fatalistic faith, implying the absence of freedom of choice. Consequently, such fatalistic conception of Islam is a piece of ignorance common among too many teachers and students of theology in the West. The law given to Adam and Eve is symbolized by the forbidden tree in verse 35. Since heaven is described in the Qur'an (2:25-26; 13:35; 47:15) in allegorical terms (see also the first issue of ISLAM, page 56), the tree mentioned in verse 35 must be an allegorical representation of God's law. The facts about man's creation as stated in verses 30 through 39 provide another example of finalization of God's message in the Qur'an. Thus, the exact reasons behind the fall of Iblis (= Lucifer = Satan) are presented to mankind for the first time. No record of such facts exists in any of the previous scriptures. As mentioned in verse 34, Iblis refused to fall prostrate before 134 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)
segments.label: page - COMMENTARY

segments.text: Rashād Khalifa Adam along with the other angels, due to sheer arrogance. Even such prominent Christians as evangelist Billy Graham never knew the reasons behind the fall of Lucifer. In his 1974 Arizona Crusade (aired on television June 3, 1974 in the St. Louis, Missouri area), Mr. Graham declared, "We do not know why Lucifer rebelled. It seems that he led a group of angels in rebellion against God." That Iblis is a fallen angel is abundantly clear from verse 34, "I said to the angels, 'Fall prostrate before Adam.'" Thus, the command to fall prostrate was directed to the angels. Had Iblis been other than an angel, therefore, he would not have been expected to obey such command. The fact that Iblis was held responsible for disobedience is clear evidence that he is a fallen angel. Some students of the Qur'an maintain that Iblis is a jinn; that angels do not disobey divine commands.
segments.label: page

segments.text: They base their argument on verses 12 of sura Al-A'rāf (No. 7) and 76 of sura Sād (No. 38) which state, Iblis said, "I am better than him; You created me from fire and created him from mud." verse 15 of sura Al-Rahmān (No. 55): He created jinn from blazing fire and verse 50 of sura Al-Kahf (No. 18): I said to the angels, "Fall prostrate before Adam." They fell prostrate, except Iblis; he was a jinn; he disobeyed the command of his Lord. However, the statement that Iblis was created from fire does not necessarily mean that he was different from the angels (who supposedly were created from light). The common belief that the angels were created from light is not supported by a single verse in the Qur'an; nowhere in the Qur'an are we told that the angels were created from light.
segments.label: page

segments.text: If the source of this general belief is a Hadith or a tradition of which this commentator is unaware, this still does not necessitate that Iblis was not an angel. The Qur'an commonly refers to the various stages of man's creation [dust (3:59; 18:37; 22:5; 30:20; 35:11; 40:67), mud (6:2; 7:12; 23:12; 32:7; 37:11; 38:76; 17:61), clay (15:26; 15:28; 15:33; 55:14), drop of semen (16:4; 23:13-14; 36:77; 53:46; 75:37; 76:2; 80:19), hanging clot (96:2)]. Similarly, it is not inconceivable to describe the creation of angels at any stage (fire, light). Furthermore, from ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 135 قَالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نَارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ وَخَلَقَ الْجَانَّ مِنْ مَارِجٍ مِنْ نَارٍ وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ
segments.label: page

segments.text: ENGLISH MEANINGS OF THE QUR'AN : 2 ENGLISH MEANINGS OF THE QUR'AN : 2 the verses discussed here we may infer that a jinn is a rebellious angel, and that the jinns are descendants of Iblis, just as we are descendants of Adam. As stated in the Qur'an, the jinns are subject to tests, judgment, heaven, and hell, exactly as we are (6:112,130; 7:38, 179; 11:119; 17:88; 32:13; 41:25, 29; 46:18; 51:56; sura 55; sura 72; 114:6). Another lesson we derive from verses 30-39 is the grossness of the sin of PRIDE. It is because of pride, and pride alone, that an angel was doomed, and is destined for Hell. Today, there are humans who are too proud to fall prostrate even before the Almighty Himself. Satan's pride caused his refusal to fall prostrate before a creature, Adam, and hence his condemnation.
segments.label: page - ENGLISH MEANINGS OF THE QUR'AN : 2

segments.text: Man's refusal to surrender his will to the Creator; to fall prostrate before the Creator (not a creature), must be at least equally disastrous. Original Sin!? Islam holds that each individual is solely responsible for his or her deeds (6:164; 17:15; 35:18; 39:7; 53:38). This doctrine applies of course to Adam, as stated in verse 37 of sura Al-Baqarah. Adam and Eve sinned (verse 36), and they alone were held responsible. The concept of "repentance" was taught to Adam (verse 37); he exercised this concept, and his repentance was accepted by the Almighty. Thus, Adam was completely exonerated; his sin was forgiven and erased. "Original sin" (a foreign concept introduced into "Christianity"), therefore, is an unacceptable doctrine in Islam; unacceptable to the all-encompassing justice of God.
segments.label: page - ENGLISH MEANINGS OF THE QUR'AN : 2

segments.text: Likewise, the commonly believed concept in the Judaeo-Christian world that Adam and Eve's sin of "eating the apple" refers euphemistically to sexual intercourse is unacceptable to Islam. This idea has caused millions to believe that sexual relations, even between a man and wife, are inherently sinful, and it is in part responsible for much of the sexual aberration and perversion which plagues the West. The detailed account of the Israelites' plight, deliverance, and rebellion, as stated in verses 40 through 123 need no comment.
segments.label: page - ENGLISH MEANINGS OF THE QUR'AN : 2

segments.text: Sura Al-A'raf 7:156-158 IN THE NAME OF GOD, THE COMPASSIONATE, THE MERCIFUL My mercy encompasses all things. But I will designate it for those who maintain righteousness, observe charity, and believe in My revelations; Those who follow the messenger, the illiterate prophet (Muḥammad) whom they find written in their Torah as well as the Gospel. He enjoins upon them but righteousness, and prohibits but evil; he permits for them but the good, and forbids for them but the bad; he unburdens them and breaks the chains which bind them. Indeed, those who believe in him, honor him, support him, and follow the light which was revealed through him, shall be the winners.
segments.label: page - Sura Al-A'raf 7:156-158

segments.text: Say (O Muḥammad), "O mankind, I am the messenger of God to you; all of you." (Sura Al-Aʻrāf 7:156-158) ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 137 بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَرَحْمَتِي وَسِعَتْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ ۚ فَسَأَكْتُبُهَا لِلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ وَيُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ وَالَّذِينَ هُمْ بِآيَاتِنَا يُؤْمِنُونَ ۝ الَّذِينَ يَتَّبِعُونَ الرَّسُولَ النَّبِيَّ الْأُمِّيَّ الَّذِي يَجِدُونَهُ مَكْتُوبًا عِنْدَهُمْ فِي التَّوْرَاةِ وَالْإِنْجِيلِ يَأْمُرُهُمْ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَاهُمْ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُحِلُّ لَهُمُ الطَّيِّبَاتِ وَيُحَرِّمُ عَلَيْهِمُ الْخَبَائِثَ وَيَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ الَّتِي كَانَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ ۚ فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِهِ وَعَزَّرُوهُ وَنَصَرُوهُ وَاتَّبَعُوا النُّورَ الَّذِي أُنْزِلَ مَعَهُ ۙ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ ۝ قُلْ يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللَّهِ إِلَيْكُمْ جَمِيعًا

segments.text: The Origin of Islamic Jurisprudence by Dr. ‘Abdul-Ḥalim Maḥmūd Grand Shaykh of Al-Azhar The Origin of Islamic Jurisprudence What some have erroneously termed “Islamic sects” are merely branches of one tree. There is but one school of jurisprudence in Islam, that based on the life and personal conduct of the prophet Muhammad (God’s blessings and peace be upon him). It is from the extensive record of his exemplary life that the four well-known branches of Islamic jurisprudence evolved. The very initiation of these branches was approved by the Prophet himself. Thus, when he appointed Mu‘adh b.
segments.label: page - The Origin of Islamic Jurisprudence

segments.text: Jabal as a viceroy in Yemen, the Prophet asked him, “How will you rule?” Mu‘adh replied, “According to the Qur’an.” The Prophet said, “What if you do not find a related rule in the Qur’an?” Mu‘adh replied, “Then, I will have to depend on my personal thought and reasoning (ajtahidu).” The Prophet is reported to have been pleased and approved of Mu‘adh’s line of thinking. In this article, the grand imām of Azhar reports on the origin and nature of the one tree of Islamic jurisprudence. The final messenger of God (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him) practiced Islam as the Almighty wanted it to be practiced. He applied Islam to all aspects of his life; his actions, reactions, talk, feelings, and his daily conduct were all governed by Islam. The Prophet’s companions followed his example very closely.
segments.label: page - The Origin of Islamic Jurisprudence

segments.text: This example of the Prophet was transmitted to us from his companions to their contemporaries and then onwards from generation to generation. The companions of the Prophet explained the Islamic way of life as they saw the Prophet live it. They narrated everything he did or said with regard to all kinds of circumstances. As the Muslim nation expanded, the Muslims transmitted these traditions to the new areas. Eventually, many outstanding scholars evolved who specialized in researching, collecting, and recording the Prophet’s traditions. Most of those scholars observed the highest 138 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 138-141 المذاهب الفقهية
segments.label: page - The Origin of Islamic Jurisprudence

segments.text: 'Abdul-Halim Mahmūd principles of scientific investigations to assure the accuracy and truthfulness of their sources. Their methods of collection and authentication of the Prophet's life have been highly esteemed by even the modern historians. The Prophet's example was consistent with regard to certain specific situations. In other situations, however, he deliberately varied his mode of behavior. The situations where he was consistent include all the fard (the obligatory rites of worship). These encompass such rites as the method of fasting, the recitation of Qur'an during the ṣalāt, and the kneeling for "tashuhhud" recitation.
segments.label: page

segments.text: The variability in the Prophet's example was observed only with regard to the nonobligatory functions which are designated today as "sunnah." Thus, his conduct did not follow one specific methodology in such sunnahs as reciting supplications between the initial takbīr of ṣalāt (saying, "Allāh Akbar") and the opening sura (Al-Fātiḥah), and in his supplications as he fell prostrate in ṣalāt, and in the manner of placing the arms and hands during ṣalāt, and so forth. Such variations were observed also in many situations of daily life involving commerce, crimes, loans, usury, and personal relations. it is only around these variations in sunnah that the four branches of jurisprudence evolved. No differences whatsoever exist among the opinions of the imams Al-Shāfi'ī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanifah, and ibn Ḥanbal concerning the obligatory duties.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Their differences are found only in their personal interpretation and reasoning with regard to the nonobligatory actions and behavior of the Prophet. These non-doctrinal differences of opinion among the four great imams have been grossly exaggerated by various groups who sought to create imaginary sects or divisions within Islam. Such exaggerations were intended mainly to divert the Muslims from their basic Islamic doctrines and, hence, from establishing the perfect society as inculcated by Islam. It was such groups who created, for example, the question of whether one should fold or unfold the arms while standing in ṣalāt. In the folding situation, the worshiper places the left hand on the stomach and the right hand on the back of the left hand. In the unfolding situation, the worshiper simply lets the arms hang down freely on the sides.
segments.label: page

segments.text: This minor issue was magnified by some researchers beyond reasonable proportions, and led to lengthy and hot debates in certain Muslim countries. These arguments were finally terminated when one enlightened scholar raised the following questions to those involved in the controversy: 1. If the worshiper stood in ṣalāt with his arms extended straight forward, would that nullify the prayer? 2. If the arms were lifted completely upward, would that nullify the prayer? ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 139 fard, ṣalāt, tashuhhud, sunnah, takbīr, Allāh Akbar, Al-Fātiḥah, Al-Shāfi'ī, Mālik, Abū Ḥanifah, ibn Ḥanbal
segments.label: page

segments.text: THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE 3. If the arms were folded, would the prayer be nullified? 4. If the arms hang down on the sides, would that nullify the prayer? When the debaters unanimously agreed that the answer to each of these questions was “No”, they realized the insignificance of their differences. This question of placing one’s arms during the ṣalāt prayer is a typical example of the subjects in which the great imams of jurisprudence expressed varied opinions. It is such differences of opinion, originating from the traditions of the Prophet, that became the basis of the branches in Islamic jurisprudence. Clearly, all these branches, reflecting different personal interpretations, belong to one and the same tree. All the imams of jurisprudence had but a single model from which they derived their opinions.
segments.label: page - THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE

segments.text: Only ignorance and narrow-mindedness would create separate schools of jurisprudence out of the one school, namely, the school of prophet Muḥammad (God’s peace and blessings be upon him). It is heartening to note that the era of false divisions within the school of Islamic jurisprudence has passed. It is a rarity nowadays to meet a Muslim who describes himself as a Shāfi‘i, Mālikī, Ḥanafī, or Ḥanbalī; the trend has been towards the one essential description: Muslim. Who Qualifies as a Mujtahid? By a mujtahid here is meant one who is scholarly qualified to set new rules and regulations to be followed by the Muslims everywhere. Some scholars have contended that the door of ijtihād (personal thought and reasoning which leads to new rules) has been closed; that the last mujtahids were the four well-known imams. Other scholars maintain that the door of ijtihād is always open.
segments.label: page - THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE

segments.text: Some among the latter group, however, talk about ijtihād as if it were attainable by anyone. It is inconceivable that God’s grace was limited to the four great imams with regard to ijtihād, since new circumstances are founded with each generation of humans. Therefore, any Muslim who satisfies certain exacting requirements can contribute to the rules and regulations known as Islamic jurisprudence, i.e., become a mujtahid. These requirements include: 1. Mastery of the Arabic language: The great imams of jurisprudence (e.g. Mālik and Al-Shāfi‘i) were unrivaled masters of the Arabic linguistic sciences. 2. Memorization of the Qur’an, with full awareness of the complete message and regulations therein. This includes a high degree of knowledge of the various Qur’anic sciences such as the circumstances associated with the revelation of each verse or group of verses. Although the Qur’an was revealed for the guidance of all the people in all places and at all times, knowledge of the specific circumstances of revelation does help in reaching 140 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) ṣalāt, Muḥammad, Shāfi‘i, Mālikī, Ḥanafī, Ḥanbalī, mujtahid, ijtihād, Qur’an, Mālik, Al-Shāfi‘i
segments.label: page - THE ORIGIN OF ISLAMIC JURISPRUDENCE

segments.text: ‘Abdul-Ḥalim Maḥmūd the correct interpretation. 3. Knowledge of the spoken sunnah, as well as the practical traditions of the Prophet (God’s peace and blessings be upon him). These requirements form the basic background needed by a Muslim before he or she can contribute correctly to Islamic jurisprudence. The seriousness and the awesomeness of responsibility in issuing new rules of jurisprudence can be appreciated if we reflect upon some of the Prophet’s teachings in this regard.
segments.label: page

segments.text: In Ṣaḥīḥ Al-Shaykhān (well-known record of Ḥadīth), the Prophet (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him) is reported as saying, “Whoever fabricates false rules from my teachings shall be committing a gross offense.” Abū Hurayrah reported the Prophet’s saying, “Whoever establishes a righteous tradition shall receive a reward equal to that due to all followers of such tradition, without reduction in their rewards. And whoever establishes an evil tradition shall incur sins equal to all the sins of those who follow such evil tradition, without reducing their guilt (reported in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim). The overall purpose of ijtihād can be divided into 2 areas: 1. Establishing rules of Islamic jurisprudence relating to matters which took place during the Prophet’s time. In this case, the purpose would be to find the Prophet’s judgment regarding the matter in question.
segments.label: page

segments.text: An example here would be the search for the exact manner of making ablution (wuḍū’), as performed by the Prophet (may God bestow peace and blessings upon him). 2. Establishing rules of Islamic jurisprudence dealing with current matters which did not exist during the Prophet’s time. Even here, the rule-making process must depend on the Prophet’s example through Qiyās (analogy). The Qur’an and the sunnah of the holy Prophet provide an unlimited array of situations which can be used directly or indirectly in establishing current rules of Islamic jurisprudence. Thus, the Muslim never lacks the reference materials he needs to establish a given rule. Under all circumstances, the mujtahid must be a “follower,” rather than an “initiator.” For the Prophet’s instructions to the mujtahids are, “you shall follow, not invent” when dealing with rules of Islamic jurisprudence.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Finally, it must be pointed out that ijtihād cannot succeed through knowledge alone. A mujtahid must be characterized first and foremost by a high standard of piety and righteousness. All the great imams who contributed positively to Islamic jurisprudence had in common a high level of genuine piety. Thus, the rules they have established for us represent no less than guidance from God to His sincere servants. Knowledge alone can never invoke such divine guidance, for God tells us, “only those who stand by God shall receive right guidance.” (Qur’an [3:101]). segments.text: Islamic Concentrates: The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī : 2 Islamic Concentrates The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī : 2 These aphorisms, with their esoteric connotations, are derived from the Qur'an, the sunna, teachings of the great imams, and the principles of Sufism. Published for the first time in English, these particular aphorisms are valuable pieces of advice delivered by one of the greatest Sufis of all time, Shaykh Salāmah Al-Rāḍī, to his dervishes. 11. My beloved in (the cause of) God: If anyone of you wishes God to heed his prayers, he shall first heed God's commands. When you heed Him, He heeds you. 12. My beloved ones: Whoever claims to have acquired dignity on his own, reveals but sinful pride. But whoever humbles himself before His Master, derives his dignity from his Lord.
segments.label: page - Islamic Concentrates: The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī : 2

segments.text: When The Reality sees you humbling yourself before Him, He permits no humiliation to ever touch you; He guarantees your dignity. 13. My beloved in (the cause of) God: Once your hearts are fully content with your Master, you enter the court of His grace. For as long as you are hesitant, you remain strangers to Him. He is only with those who are fully with him. 14. O you beloved ones: If your heart truly loves your Master, it will not grieve over parting with anything else. So long as you grieve over parting with other than your Master, this should be your indicator that you are not yet in His court. Rather, you would be in the court of whatever diverted you from your Master. 15. O you beloved ones: If you are saddened by the people's criticism, and rejoice when they flatter you, beware. This would indicate that your ego is still alive and thus still competing with the Master in His divine attributes. 142 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 142-144
segments.label: page - Islamic Concentrates: The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī : 2

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2 THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2 16. O you beloved ones: If you spend your lives worshiping your Master, while at the same time being dissatisfied with Him, not humbling yourselves before His dignity, staying away from His company, keeping your thoughts with the devils and the far-removed individuals, how do you expect your worship to attain any light? It would be spiritless worship; dead. 17. O you beloved ones: You care too much for feeding vanishing shells, and pay little attention to feeding your eternal entity. Consequently, you end up with great bodies, but diminished souls. 18. O you beloved ones: Your hearts are like empty containers. You strive and even pay monies to fill them with darkness, while the light is within your reach, free of charge.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2

segments.text: Instead of helping yourselves to the light, you keep pushing your hearts further and further therefrom. Would a wise person fill his eyes with darkness, until he sees but darkness? Or, would he rather fill them with light in order to become a seer? 19. O beloved ones: The love of this life has a certain sweetness which causes intoxication of the heart. Thus, it becomes distracted from the love of its Master, and adores but illusions. This world is no more than an illusion. Therefore, you shall not imbibe this particular wine; it is far more evil than the grape's wine which masks the mind from physical objects. 20. My beloved in (the path to) God: Whenever you see one who obeys the devil & does his deeds, you shall stay clear of him; he is a devil himself. Whoever befriends him shall in turn become a devil like him. 21.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2

segments.text: O you beloved ones: Whoever is filled with goodness, nothing but goodness comes out of him. Whoever is filled with evil, nothing but evil comes out of him. How could evil ever spill out of one who is filled with goodness? 22. O you beloved ones: Whoever adorns himself with virtue exhibits but virtue. Therefore, you shall strive to become virtuous people, so that only virtuous traits may be reflected from you. 23. My beloved ones: The poor, by definition, is one who is in need. Thus, if one possesses tremendous wealth but still seeks more wealth, he is poor. He continues to labor in order to acquire more riches. If he is never satisfied, his poverty will last all his life. 143 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2 THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2 24. O you beloved ones: Whoever seeks power tires himself, for power is beloved by all, and the people fight among themselves over it. Therefore, you should not seek power. It will seek you so long as you shun seeking it, and when anyone opposes you in this case, many will stand by you and support you. 25. My beloved ones: If anyone claims superiority over you, do not fight him. If you fight him over it, it will abandon both you and him. But if you allow him to claim superiority, it will abandon him and come to you. 26. My beloved ones: If anyone fights you over what belongs to God, you shall not fight him. God cares for whatever belongs to Him, & if you take the matter in your hands and fight over His belongings, you yourselves belong to God no more. 27.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2

segments.text: My beloved ones: You gain God's love if you are persecuted in His cause. Thus, you shall seek victory for His cause. You shall never seek victory for yourselves. If you do, you fall from your Master's grace. 28. My beloved ones: You shall persevere in the face of persecution, injustice, and tribulation. Do not ever execrate or curse. Instead, you shall be exemplars of mercy and pardon on earth, in order to earn the love of your Master. The Almighty is always with those whose hearts are broken in His cause. 29. My beloved ones: While the people are busy with the affairs of this life, you shall busy yourselves with your Master. While they are busy with the given, you shall be busy with the Giver. 30. My beloved ones: Habituate yourselves with doing good, & respond not to evil by evil. God loves the good-doers. 144 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀḌI : 2

segments.text: The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 2 Islamic Concentrates The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 2 ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī, a famous Persian Sufi, was born in Herat 396 AH (1005 C.E.). It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet Muhammad (God’s blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat with ‘Aṣaf, son of Qays. Anṣārī’s father, Abu Manṣūr Muhammad Anṣārī, became a permanent resident of Herat. These invocations, translated into English by Sir Jogendra Singh, contain true advice to guide the Pilgrim along the path of discipleship to the temple of peace. They come from a man who himself had trodden the path and found what his heart desired. When ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī departed from this world, he was 85 years old, leaving behind a wealth of Sufi knowledge.
segments.label: page - The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 2

segments.text: Among his well-known works are Risāla Munājāt (The Book of Prayer), Tabaqat-ul-Ṣūfiyyah (The Book of Sufis), Zād-ul-‘Ārifīn (Provisions of the Sufi Teachers), and Kitāb-i-Isrār (The Book of Mysteries). O Lord, give me a heart That I may pour it out in thanksgiving. Give me life That I may spend it in working for the salvation of the world. O Lord, give me that right discrimination That the Lure of the world may cheat me no more. Give me strength That my faith suffer no eclipse. O Lord, give me understanding, That I stray not from the path. Give me light To avoid pitfalls. O Lord, keep watch over me That I stray not. Keep me on the path of righteousness That I escape from the pangs of repentance. ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 145-150 145 ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī, Risāla Munājāt, Tabaqat-ul-Ṣūfiyyah, Zād-ul-‘Ārifīn, Kitāb-i-Isrār
segments.label: page - The Invocations of ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī : 2

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 O Lord, judge me not by my actions. Of Thy mercy, save me, And make my humble efforts fruitful. O Lord, give me a heart Free from the flames of desire. Give me a mind Free from the waves of dissimulation. O Lord, give me eyes Which see nothing but Thy glory. Give me a mind That finds delight in Thy service. Give me a soul Drunk in the wine of Thy wisdom. O Lord, to find Thee is my desire But to comprehend Thee Is beyond my strength. Remembering Thee is solace to my sorrowing heart, Thoughts of Thee are my Constant Companions I call upon Thee night and day. The flame of Thy love glows In the darkness of my night.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: O Lord, he whom Thou killest doth not smell of blood, And he whom Thou burnest doth not smell of smoke, For he whom Thou burnest is happy in The burning, And he whom Thou killest, rejoiceth In being killed. O Lord, though the blue flower be poisonous It is of Thy garden, And if ‘Abdullāh be a sinner He is of Thy people. O Lord, when I think of Thy compassion I feel like a crowned king; When I think of my sins I am as dust, nay, less than dust. (Right column text fragment): Life in my body My heart beats in If on my dust a tuft To grow Every blade would tremble For Thee. O Lord, every one desires I desire That Thou mayest cast a Let me not disgrace myse If Thy forgiveness awaits Lower not the standard Which Thou hast unfur O Lord, if Thou sendes I raise no protest.

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 Life in my body pulsates only for Thee, My heart beats in resignation to Thy will. If on my dust a tuft of grass were To grow Every blade would tremble with my devotion For Thee. O Lord, every one desires to behold Thee, I desire That Thou mayest cast a glance at me. Let me not disgrace myself. If Thy forgiveness awaits me in the end Lower not the standard of forgiveness Which Thou hast unfurled. O Lord, if Thou sendest me to Hell I raise no protest. And if Thou takest me to Paradise, I go there, but not of my own choice. If in Hell I obtain union with Thee What care I for those who dwell in Paradise? And were I called to Heaven without Thee The pleasures of Paradise would then Be worse than the fires of Hell. O Lord, prayer at Thy gate Is a mere formality: Thou knowest what Thy slave desires.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: O Lord, better for me to be dust, And my name effaced From the records of the world, Than that Thou forget me. He knoweth all our good and evil Nothing is hidden from Him. He knoweth what is best medicine To cure the pain, And to rescue the fallen. Be humble, for He exalteth the humble. I am intoxicated with love of Thee And need no fermented wine. ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) 147
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 I am Thy bird Free from need of seed And safe from the snare of the fowler. In the Ka‘ba and in the Temple Thou art the object of my search. Else I am freed From both these places of worship. O Lord, when the fire of separation was burning me Why didst Thou light the fire of Hell? Lord, when Thou wert hidden from me The fever of life possessed me. When Thou revealest Thyself This fever of life departeth. O Lord, other men are afraid of Thee But I — I am afraid of myself, From Thee flows good alone, From me flows evil. Each day I recall the day, That is left behind. Sorrowing over my misdeeds The dread of my doings drives me to despair. The thought of Thy mercy Is the only solace of my heart. Others fear what the morrow May bring. I am afraid of what happened yesterday.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: O Lord, if Thou holdest me responsible for My sins I shall cling to Thee for Thy Grace. I with my sin, am an insignificant atom. Thy Grace is resplendent as the Sun. O Lord, out of regard for Thy name, The qualities which are Thine, Out of regard for Thy greatness, Listen to my cry For Thou alone canst redeem me. 148 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ, Ka‘ba
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 O Lord, intoxicate me with the wine Of Thy love. Place the chains of Thy slavery on My feet; Make me empty of all but Thy love, And in it destroy me and bring me Back to life. The hunger Thou has awakened, culminates In fulfillment. Make my body impervious to the fires Of Hell; Vouchsafe to me a vision of Thee in heaven. The spark Thou has kindled make it Everlasting. I think of no other, And in Thy love care for none else. None has a place in my heart but Thee. My heart has become Thy abode, It has no place for another. O Lord, Thou cherishest the helpless And I am helpless, Apply Thy balm to my bleeding heart For Thou art the physician. O Lord, I, a beggar, ask of Thee More than what a thousand kings may ask of Thee; Each one has something he needs to ask of Thee, I have come to ask Thee to give me Thyself.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: If words can establish a claim I claim a crown. But if deeds are wanted, I am as helpless as The ant. Urged by desire I wandered in the streets Of good and evil, I gained nothing except feeding the fire of desire. As long as in me remains the breath of life Help me, for Thou alone canst hear my prayer. My friend, wisdom lies In abandoning heedlessness, ISLAM 1394/1974; 1(2) 149
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2 In turning the heart away from the worldly objects, And in gathering provision for the hereafter Before departure from this earth. Someone asked the Holy Prophet — “What dost thou say concerning the things of the world?” The Prophet said — “What can I say about them: Things which are acquired with hard labour, Preserved with perpetual watchfulness, And left with regret.” My friend, the world is not a place For enjoyment, But a place where humanity is on trial. The world is a mere crossing And not an abiding city of delight. O mendicant, man is doomed to death And has to leave the world. Dost thou take the world for a friend Or foe? If thou holdest it a friend, Know that it will not last, If thou holdest it to be a foe, consume it, So that it may not last. Behold what thou art, and whence thou Hast come.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: Beware what thou doest and whither Thou wouldest go, If thou treadest the path of lust and longing Thou shalt go without fruit and without good name. My friend, put not thy reliance On three things: On heart, on time and on life. The heart is easily tempted, Time is always in a state of flux, The sands of life run out. ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANṢĀRĪ : 2

segments.text: The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 2 (Hijra / Gregorian) Islamic Concentrates The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 2 (Hijra / Gregorian) Over the first five issues of ISLAM, the Journal will publish this table for convenient conversion of dates from either of the two calendar systems. Such chronological conversion tables have been difficult to find yet most indispensible for the Western scholar of Islam. Since all great works of Islamic literature refer exclusively to Hijra dates, the Editors feel that thes tables will be useful to many readers. According to the historians, the prophet Muhammad (God's blessings be upon him) arrived at Medina on the 12th day of Rabi' I, coincident with September 24, 622 CE (Christian Era). This sets the first day of the first Hijra year (Muharram 1, 1) as July 16, 622. Fifteen hundred Hijra years will be covered in these tables (622-2076 CE).
