segments.text: Book Review Book Review The Late Great Planet Earth by Hal Lindsey. Bantam Books, New York, (30th printing) 1973. 180 pages, $1.25. This fascinating book about Bible prophecies and the author's version of their modern fulfillment has gone through 30 impressions since its release in 1970 and boasts of having over 2 million copies in print. Lindsey has a pleasant, chatty style and has gathered a plethora of facts which supposedly support his major contention that Christianity is still relevant because the return of Christ is near. He makes use of the present anxiety over world affairs and points to matters as current as the daily paper as sure signs of the End. The obvious problem with Lindsey's theory is that most of the ground he covers has been covered many times before in age after age.
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: Eschatological speculation and millenialist expectation have occupied the minds of men since Jesus ended his mission. There have been untold hundreds of "prophets" who predicted doomsday for their own times. Bible scholars and Christian sects have used the very same verses quoted by Lindsey to predict the End for the years 1843, 1879 and 1914, among other dates. Some Christian sects currently warn that the End is sure to come in 1976. Lindsey himself leans toward 1988 (p. 43). However, Lindsey is confident that he has found the one necessary histoircal ingredient missing in all previous predictions about the Last Day: the establishment of the state of "Israel" in the year 1948 (p. 33). The rebirth of "Israel" is the "fuse of Armageddon", the proof that our generation is living on borrowed time.
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: But this conclusion produces in Lindsey's book the weird dogma best described as Christian Zionism. This states that Christ cannot come again and Christian hopes for the Kingdom of God cannot be fulfilled, until "Israel" is in complete control of Palestine, including Jerusalem, and the Temple of Solomon is rebuilt. "It is certain that the Temple will be rebuilt. Prophecy demands it," Lindsey argues on page 45. This puts him in the position of condoning the Israeli occupation of Palestine, the dispossession of the Arabs, Zionist terrorism against Palestinians and Zionist attempts to rebuild the Jewish Temple — which means the destruction of Qubbat al-Sakhrah. Of this he flippantly suggests, "Who knows, maybe there will be an earthquake." (p. 47) Man-made, perhaps???
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: Lindsey's Christian Zionism has uprooted the expected Christian compassion over the awful human misery of the refugee camps, the horrible napalming of Arab children by the Zionists and the terrible denial of Arab rights perpetrated by "Israel". But Christian Zionism has no basis in fact. 160 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2): 160-162
segments.label: page - Book Review

segments.text: Every one of the biblical verses which he quotes in support of it actually has reference to events a thousand years old, not to events of our day! For example, the prophet Ezekiel predicted the restoration of Israel and the reconstruction of the Temple about 598 B.C. His prophecy was fulfilled in 538 B.C., when the Jews returned from dispersal to Jerusalem and in 520 B.C., when the Temple was rebuilt. Thus, within 80 years of his prediction, Ezekiel's prophecy was completely fulfilled. To extend any part of his prophecy to our time, as Lindsey attempts to do, is idle speculation. What he calls "current history" is really ancient history! The same is true regarding the New Testament prophecies of Jesus manipulated by Lindsey.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Some of these are highly allegorical; others were fulfilled within a generation or two after Jesus' departure, such as the predictions of the destruction of the Jewish Temple and its desecration by the Romans. (Matthew, chapter 24) These things occurred between 70 and 134 C.E. After 134 C.E. the Romans made Jerusalem a colony, renamed Aelia, and forbade Jewish settlement there. The Temple site was rededicated to the Roman gods Jupiter and Zeus. Rather than foretelling a Jewish return to Palestine, Jesus instead pronounced God's rejection of the Jews as a nation and God's abandonment of the Jewish Temple: "The kingdom of God will be taken away from you, and given to a nation that yields the proper fruit . . . O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the city that murders the prophets and stones the messengers sent to her . . .
segments.label: page

segments.text: Look, look! there is your temple, forsaken by God." (Matthew 21:43 and 23:37, New English Bible) As the last prophet sent specifically to Israel, the verdict of Jesus carries infinitely more weight than Lindsey's conjectures and interpretations of the words of prior prophets. There are also serious holes in Lindsey's argument that current history supports his interpretation of events marking the End. To cite just two of many examples, he predicts a Russian attack on "Israel" and the wholesale conversion of the Arabs to Communism. This looked plausible a few years back, before Nixonian detente and Kissingerian diplomacy, but highly unlikely now. And, far from turning to Communism, the Arab world is now making overtures to the West. Lindsey appears to have a real concern for the rebuilding of the Jewish Temple. He insists on it in several passages of his book. But this is impossible.
segments.label: page

segments.text: For the Temple to be inaugurated anew, according to the Bible (Ezekiel 43:19-27), the priesthood must exist and the priesthood has not existed for 1900 years. This proves also that the Roman destruction of Jerusalem began in 70 C.E., after Jesus' warning to the Jews, was an act of Divine judgment on their nation. In previous tribulations, the priesthood had survived. But in 70 C.E. the Romans destroyed all the priestly records, in effect, destroying the priesthood. To this day, there is no priesthood in modern "Israel". There 161 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2)
segments.label: page

segments.text: can be no priesthood with the records which no longer exist. No priesthood, no Temple. There are many prophecies in the Old Testament which were fulfilled with the coming of Jesus. His manner and place of birth, lineage, message and miracles were all recorded in advance so that believers would recognize him when he came. Lindsey is correct to charge the Jews with disobedience when they rejected Jesus despite these clear prophecies. But Christians, including Lindsey are guilty of doing exactly the same thing. The New Testament as well as the Old Testament contain many prophecies which were fulfilled with the coming of Muhammad. Similarly, prominent aspects of his lineage, personality, message and achievements were all recorded in advance. (See Islam, vol.
segments.label: page

segments.text: I, no. 1, April 1974, pp. 1-13.) Christians have no more excuse for rejecting Muhammad than Jews have for rejecting Jesus (peace be upon them both), Jews and Christians are equally chargeable with persisting in the same error. Rather than fantasizing over ancient history, Christians with a real interest in prophecy should heed the prophecy of Jesus concerning the P-R-KL-TOS (periklytos, Muhammad) who would come after him (John 14 and 16) who would reveal “the whole truth” and set the record straight. As a nation, the Jews have rejected both Jesus and Muhammad (peace be upon them). What, then, is the basis for any Divine favor upon a reborn Jewish nation?
segments.label: page

segments.text: In surah Banī Isrā’īl [17:2-8] God shows that in the days of the prophet, the Jews had a last chance to return (since acceptance of Muhammad would mean acceptance of Jesus also, of whom Muhammad preached): “It may be that your Lord will yet show Mercy to you; but if you revert to your sins, We shall revert to our punishments, and We have made Hell a prison for those who reject faith.” Again the nation chose disobedience. The most insidious aspect of this book is its dogma that anyone who helps the Arab or Muslim cause against Zionism is courting the disfavor of God and sure disaster, regardless of the oppressive nature of Israeli occupation of Palestine. For Lindsey, the struggle against Zionism is tantamount to war against God! But the fatal flaw in his whole attempt to promote Christian Zionism is that he himself finally shows its utter futility.
segments.label: page

segments.text: After predicting that the Jews will be converted to belief in Christ just before the End (p. 156), he says, on the basis of his interpretation of prophecy, that only 1/3 of the Jews will be saved. The majority — 2/3 — will be lost. Therefore, according to Lindsey, even after Christ returns, even after God supposedly blesses Israeli aggression in Palestine, the majority of the Jews will go right on rejecting Jesus! What a waste of 180 pages! S. Shāhīd Mufassir 162 ISLAM 1394/1974, 1(2) Banī Isrā’īl

segments.text: IT is held that when a Seeker gives his heart and mind to the search, and disperses the mists that arise from tumultuous passions, Truth becomes brighter and brighter and fills the Soul with its light. It is asserted that while reason is puzzling itself about mystery of consciousness, time, and space, the man of Faith is going forward from discovery to discovery, in the growing illumination of his heart. But it must be recognised that this knowledge is only available to those whose eyes are fixed, like an archer, on the arrow and the object at which he aims, and that without purity of purpose and unceasing effort deliverance cannot be obtained. In all ages and in all times men have sought and found truth. They have shown the way and means of attainment. But men have listened to the message with incredulity and continued the mad pursuit of sense objects.
segments.label: page

segments.text: Passions of body and mind govern men and kindle fires of desire, of greed, attachment, egoism and anger. These enslave and obscure the mind which must be freed, and restored to its pristine purity to reflect truth. The seekers of truth, therefore, concentrate all their strength in drawing away the mind from sense objects and to set it free from the dominations of fear and hate. Some follow the path of knowledge, and others the path of devotion, hoping to lose all sense of duality in the supreme uprising of love. (from Preface of 'The Invocations of 'Abdullāh Anṣārī') ‘Abdullāh Anṣārī

segments.text: Notes to Authors Notes to Authors It the policy of this Journal to publish articles in English in all fields of ISLAM provided they are of a high caliber and contribute to the fundamental knowledge of the religion. In keeping with the universal nature of Islam, this journal is not intended to reflect any political, regional, or nationalistic bias. Articles containing unwarranted attacks, direct or implied, against any other religion, sect, belief, or ideology, shall not be accepted for publication. The journal's sole objective is to work within the framework of ISLAM towards a full appreciation of God's message to all humanity. The journal recognizes the sources of Islamic knowledge to be the Qur'an, the Sunna, analogy (Qiyās), consensus (Ijmā'), and personal thought (Ijtihād). However, THE QUR'AN shall be the ultimate reference.
segments.label: page - Notes to Authors

segments.text: Only statements in full agreement with the Qur'an shall represent the journal's official stand. All other statements, or statements subject to various interpretations shall represent only the author's personal viewpoint. Manuscripts submitted for publication should be typed, double spaced. Only one copy is required. All Qur'anic quotations must be accompanied by the number(s) of sura(s), and the number(s) of verse(s). Colons should separate the number of sura from the number(s) of verse(s) (e.g. 17:28-33). A group of verses from the same sura should be separated from each other by commas (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62). When more than one sura are involved, a semi-colon should separate the different suras (e.g. 17:28-33, 51, 60-62; 23:16; 36:9-11, 19-25, 44). The journal will undertake to add the Arabic text to all Qur'anic translations.
segments.label: page - Notes to Authors

segments.text: ERRATUM God’s Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity Yūsuf Amīn Wālī, Ph.D. ERRATUM God’s Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity In the last issue of ISLAM [1(2): 91-104], it was pointed out that the only 2 suras in the Qur’an which are initialed with the letter Qāf ق [namely, sura Al-Shūrā (No. 42) and sura Qāf (No. 50)] contain exactly the same number of this letter, i.e. 57; that the total number of occurrences of this letter in the 2 suras is 114, the same as the total number of suras in the Qur’an. It was pointed out that this deliberate design and the knowledge of the mathematical distribution of individual alphabets throughout the Qur’an are unattainable by man; that only Allah could have such capability.
segments.label: page - ERRATUM God’s Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

segments.text: Allah (the most glorified, most high) placed the initial Qāf at the beginning of the 2 suras to indicate to us His knowledge of the alphabetical distribution; that there is something special about the letter Qāf in these particular suras; that only He is the author of the Qur’an. On page 98 of that article, however, it was pointed out that sura Ibrāhīm (No. 14) is the only other sura where the letter Qāf occurs 57 times. I am writing this erratum to state that, in comparing the number of occurrences of the letter Qāf, I have overlooked the fact that while suras Al-Shūrā & Qāf have the letter Qāf prefixed to them, sura Ibrāhīm is not initialed with the letter Qāf. If the letter Qāf is prefixed as an initial in sura Ibrāhīm, for a fair and accurate comparison, then the number of occurrences of the letter Qāf will become 58, not the same as the 2 Qāf-initialed suras.
segments.label: page - ERRATUM God’s Message to Humanity: The Ultimate Proof of Authenticity

segments.text: To look at it at another way, if we remove all the Qur’anic initials from the Qur’an, we will find that sura Qāf and sura Al-Shūrā contain 56 Qāfs each, while sura Ibrāhīm contains 57 Qāfs. It was neither fair, nor accurate, therefor, to state that sura Ibrāhīm was “the only other sura which contains the same number of Qāfs as the Qāf-initialed suras.” We can easily envision that Allah (the most glorified, most high) looked at His complete message to humanity, the Qur’an, before the placement of the Qur’anic initials and knew that only two suras qualify to receive the initial Qāf so that the total number of Qāfs in them would equal the total number of suras. These two suras were Al-Shūrā (No. 42) and Qāf (No. 50). In order to give us a signal or a hint that He alone knows the alphabetical ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 163-164 ق

segments.text: THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS" THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS" According to Church historians, the Gospel of Barnabas does not exist as a complete manuscript, but survives only in fragments and certain ecclesiastical writings of the first and second centuries of the Christian Era. It was written in Greek. It is extremely difficult to find a copy of what exists, either in Greek or in translation. But there does exist another book, a complete manuscript, which calls itself the "Gospel of Barnabas". Allegedly, it was written in Hebrew when it was discovered by Pope Sixtus V (1585-1590 CE), who is said to have translated it from Hebrew into Italian. This Italian "Barnabas" later found its way into the Hofbiblyothek at Vienna, and was translated into English in 1907 by Lonsdale and Laura Ragg.
segments.label: page - THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS"

segments.text: Strangely, the Italian edition has Arabic footnotes.3 The Italian "Barnabas" could not have been written by a disciple of Jesus Christ in the first century C.E. This is the judgment of Christian scholars who have read "Barnabas" and it is one in which this Muslim reader will have to concur. To be sure, it mentions the blessed prophet Muhammad by name, but this presents the first problem. "Barnabas" mentions Muhammad by name much too often for a Christian Gospel. In fact, "Barnabas" mentions Muhammad by name more often than the Qur'an does. At the same time, it contains doctrines which are not approved by either orthodox Christian or Muslim tradition. A chief example of this is the assertion by "Barnabas" that Jesus is not the Messiah and that Jesus cursed Peter for calling him the Messiah.4 By contrast, the Qur'an makes several references to Al-Masīḥ, Īsā b.
segments.label: page - THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS"

segments.text: Maryam, "The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary." There is no disagreement between Islam and Christianity on this point. For a book supposedly written in Hebrew originally, "Barnabas" uses defective Hebrew in transliteration. Jesus reportedly raises his "eyes to heaven (saying): 'O Elohim Sabaoth, have mercy upon thy servants.'" (p. 21) This construction "Elohim Sabaoth" (God of Hosts) is Greek, not Hebrew. The correct Hebrew form would be Elohei Sabaoth or Elohei has-sabaoth.5 On page 34, "Barnabas" records that "Jesus went to Jerusalem, near unto the Senofegia, a feast of our nation." If this were originally a Hebrew book, the correct term would be Sukkoth, not Senofegia. The reference is to the Feast of Tabernacles, which is Hag has-sukkoth in the Hebrew Bible (Deuteronomy 16:13; Zachariah 14:16, etc.), and skenopegia in New Testament Greek (John 7:2).
segments.label: page - THE ITALIAN "BARNABAS"

Shāhid Mufassir Hebrew Bible.6 Many of its quotations from the Old Testament follow the Latin Bible rather than the Hebrew.7 Since the Latin (Vulgate) Bible was not published until 382 C.E., “Barnabas” could not quote from it during the time of Jesus. The dependence on the Vulgate proves that “Barnabas” could have been written not earlier than 350 years after the mission of Jesus! “Barnabas” quotes from the Old Testament apocryphal book called Susanna (p. 60) which was in the Vulgate, but not in the Hebrew canon. And if the book were written by the Barnabas of the first century, it would never have carried the serious blunder found on page 76 of the English edition. Here “Barnabas” says: “The passover drew near, wherefore Jesus, which his disciples, went up to Jerusalem. And he went to the pool called ‘Probatica’.” “Probatica” was not the name of the pool!
segments.label: page

segments.text: The name of the pool was Bethesda (“House of Mercy” in Hebrew) or Bethzatha (“House of the Olive”), according to some manuscripts. The name of the pool seems to have been connected with the miracles which were said to have taken place there, as “Barnabas” admits: “And the bath (pool) was so called because the angel of God every day troubled the water, and whosoever ever entered the water after its movement was cured of every kind of infirmity.” (p. 76, cf. John 5:2-4). However, this explanation of the name Bethesda is not included in the earliest manuscripts of the New Testament and some modern translations omit it.
segments.label: page

segments.text: It is thus the more curious that “Barnabas” includes a portion of the New Testament which is based on later manuscripts and then misinterprets its meaning!) “Probatica”, which “Barnabas” mistakes for the name of the pool, is really the name for the sheep-gate which was near the pool. “Probatica” is the Latin form of the Greek New Testament word probatika at John 5:2, meaning “Sheep Gate”. How could a book written originally in Hebrew overlook the very Hebrew name of the miraculous pool, Bethesda, and put in its place a word of Greek derivation which referred, not to the pool at all, but to its gate? The Italian “Barnabas” is full of fables. Unlike the Qur’an, which insists upon making no distinctions between the prophets, “Barnabas” portrays Muḥammad (peace be upon him) in an almost Divine light, setting him over and above all the rest to a fabulous degree.
segments.label: page

segments.text: The passage which Muslims like to quote wherein Jesus foretells the coming of Muḥammad, having denied the Messiahship to Jesus, gives it to the Prophet: “Jesus answered: ‘The name of the Messiah is Admirable (Muḥammad).’” (p. 113) But Muḥammad (peace be upon him) never claimed to be the Messiah, nor does the Qur’an say that Jesus foretold the coming of a Messiah, but of another rasūl. Therefore, even this oft-used verse of “Barnabas” has a fatal flaw. “Barnabas” could not have been written before the fourth century C.E. and there is evidence that it was written even much later, somewhere in Medieval ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 167 Muḥammad, rasūl

Second. on page 96, "Barnabas" refers to the Jewish festival of the Jubilee: "Jesus answered: 'I am indeed sent to the house of Israel as a prophet of salvation; but after me shall come the Messiah, sent of God to all the world; for whom God hath made the world (i.e., Muhammad) . . . and that year of Jubilees, which now cometh every hundred years, shall by the Messiah be reduced to every year in every place.'" Here "Barnabas" again denies the messiahship to Jesus and gives it to Muhammad, but he also speaks of the Jubilee "which now cometh every hundred years . . ." at the time of the disciple Barnabas, the Jubilee came every fifty years!

segments.text: The Jubilee which "now cometh every hundred years" could only refer to the Papal Jubilee of the Catholic Church, which was inaugurated in 1300 C.E. and reduced to 50 years in 1350 C.E. This pinpoints the writing of "Barnabas" as between 1300 and 1350 C.E., some 14 centuries after the mission of Jesus! The conclusion must be that the Italian "Barnabas" was a purposely fabricated book, written or re-written by someone familiar with Islam but outside of the orthodox (Sunni) tradition of Islam. It could not possibly be the work of the disciple Barnabas, nor is it the fragmentary Gospel of Barnabas whose existence is acknowledged by Chrisitan scholars. Because it contains dogmas and fables which conflict with the Qur'an, it is not really useful to Muslims. Nor do Muslims need it. Though some Muslims have formed a liking for the Italian "Barnabas," its lack of authenticity makes it useless.

These manuscripts in the language of Jesus say simply ". . . the P-R-KL-TOS, the spirit, whom the Father will send."9 "Spirit" carries the connotation also of "inspired person." segments.text: THE MUSLIMS AND JERUSALEM THE MUSLIMS AND JERUSALEM Heaven. This, was the place where the Prophet led the congregational prayer with all the Prophets. It is well to recall Jerusalem is regarded as the spiritual home of the Muslims next to Mecca and Medina. In the early days of Islam, it served as the first Qibla of the Muslims, for they used to pray towards Jerusalem when Muhammad still lived in Mecca. After the Prophet migrated to Medina, he continued to pray towards Jerusalem for 16 months, until he was directed to face towards Mecca.1,2 The Dome of the Rock stands on one of the most sacred spots in the world. It was built by Umayyad Caliph Abd al-Malik Ibn Marwan in 961 A.D. on the same site where Caliph ‘Umar built his mosque of wood. The monument is of such noble beauty that it stands unrivalled in the real of sacred art.
segments.label: page - THE MUSLIMS AND JERUSALEM

segments.text: It is one of the two oldest and most impressive specimens of the early Muslim architecture, the other being the Grand Mosque of Damscuss which has remained intact to this day. The temple area or the Haram al-Shar-if, as it is called by the Arabs, has always been a place of great sanctity for the Muslims all over the world. Jerusalem was captured by the Crusaders under Godfrey of Bouillon in July, 1099 A.D. who converted the mosque into a church and renamed it Templum Domini. They even built an altar on the Rock. But Sultan Salahuddin, in October, 1187 A.D., recaptured it.3,4,5 After the death of the Sultan, Jerusalem remained under Muslim rule for 731 years. It was ruled in turn by the Ayubites, Mamlukes and finally the Ottomans until 1918, when it was captured by the British forces led by General Allenby.

segments.text: Islam & The Third International Theory Islam & The Third International Theory IN THE NAME OF GOD In a world where man is confused whether capitalism or communism offers the values of life, a third path is needed. Life on earth, which was intended to be so in the beginning of the created world, is now wandering in a maze, to set aside spiritual values and to live in a whirlpool of material life, conscious or unconscious of the ultimate end. State policies, based on capitalism and materialism, have made that humans are subjected to misery and a complete loss of their identity, even for a few moments of peace. In olden days, there were no such theories. Only under the Almighty's shade, man knew the true meaning of God on earth, and there were no the veils on the truth that held sway.
segments.label: page - Islam & The Third International Theory

segments.text: Physical life was simple, even when conflict existed, such as in serfdom with the concentration of power as the main objective of men working to improve their inter-human relations, even before the pre-industrial age and the discovery of the machine. The Creator has freed mankind from true slavery and the heavy bonds for the sake of humanity. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) The "Third International Theory" is not a new theory but has been purposely called so for it, partly, screens out the drawbacks of the other two theories now in practice in the world, namely, capitalism and communism, and, partly, because it urges Mankind for a return to God by adopting a third path, different from the two existing ones. 176 الجمهورية العربية الليبية
segments.label: page - Islam & The Third International Theory

segments.text: Islam & World Governments: The Third International Theory Mu‘ammar Al-Qadhāfī Chief of State, Libyan Arab Republic Islam & World Governments: The Third International Theory IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE MOST COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL In a world where tensions and conflicts abound and in which materialism, whether capitalist or communist, is blinding human beings from the spiritual values of life, a comeback to religion is now gaining momentum. Life on earth, being as it is, a preparation for the hereafter has stopped to be so in the absence of a genuine religious drive. Man, all through the world, is now working as if he were to exist on earth forever. He has ostensibly set aside spiritual values, the result of which is that he is drifting away in a whirlpool of materialistic values. God, apparently, is being deliberately or unconsciously forgotten . . .
segments.label: page - Islam & World Governments: The Third International Theory

segments.text: State policies, in their turn, are simply inspired nowadays by mundane and materialistic objectives. Social and economic interrelations among humans are subsequently suffering. Man, today, is groping his way towards complete loss sacrificing his age-old spiritual security and happiness for some few moments of satisfaction he succeeds to snatch every now and then. In olden times when religion was supreme, there were no man-made theories. Only religion — the divine theory — predominated, and in its shade, man knew happiness and security for he duly felt he was the successor of God on earth. However, human self-conceit and other factors have put the veils on our eyes. Serfdom at one time, was institutionalized and gained sway.
segments.label: page - Islam & World Governments: The Third International Theory

segments.text: Physical force was instrumental to subdue the freeborn individual and, when conflict of interests increased among the masters, they agreed to replace serfdom with the feudal system. Riches on the earth became the instruments of power as the feudal lords possessed not only the land but also the lives of men working within the confines of this property. In the meantime inter-human exploitation spread in the cities, at first, in a limited way, during the pre-industrial Revolution Age, and, then world-wide after James Watt’s discovery of steam. The Church, too, had its part in exploiting Man, and flagrantly digressing from true Christianity in the era of the Borgias, began to sell indulgence bonds for the remission of temporal and especially purgatorial punishment. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 177-182 177 بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
segments.label: page - Islam & World Governments: The Third International Theory

segments.text: THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY Clergymen, in the Age of Decadence, were notorious feudal lords, who committed abuses of power as well as other forms of exploitation. Protestantism, a movement which caused a schism within the church, failed to reform the clergy who kept digressing from true Christianity. The Inquisition era is also a salient -digression from Christian tolerance. Islam, Judaism and even the other non-heavenly creeds have also passed through their own setbacks. But, Islam, for one, has suffered no distortions in its Holy Book though there is a general consensus that some Muslims have had their abuses which caused gross injury to Muslims at large. However, Judaism had been flagrantly distorted to suit the purposes of Zionism.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: The distortions, it is noted, occurred in the Bible and in the Gospels while, in Islam, only the misbehaviour of some Muslims is detected. (see this issue). Screening back the evolution of history, it is found that theoricians like David Ricardo and Adam Smith, began to interpret life in terms of capitalist thinking. Of course, Man tried to revolt against exploitation. Theoretically, humanitarian thinkers, philosophers and economists, like St. Simon, Owen, Lasalle and Proudhon appeared and, tried, in their own way, to establish a utopian society of their own. Practically, however, a true mass revolution took place in the year 1789 in France, calling for Liberty, Fraternity and Equality, but this outburst was short-lived as France reverted to militarism to spread its empire.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: The communist theory emerged in the year 1848 in a manifesto entirely based on dialectical materialism, which maintains that the basis of reality is constantly changing in a dialectical process giving the priority of matter over mind and metaphysics. This ideology was aimed, in fact, to be against inter-human exploitation but it appeared to be a theory that disregards spiritual values and leaves Man erring astray. Be all that as it is, the First of September Revolution in the Libyan Arab Republic feels it is its duty to remind Mankind of the necessity for a comeback to God. For humanity, as a whole, is now in dire need for a new path which is to take us back to our religions and to God who created us to be His successors on earth.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: The “Third International Theory” is not a new theory but has been purposely called so for it, partly, screens out the drawbacks of the other two theories now in practice in the world, namely, capitalism and communism, and, partly, because it urges Mankind for a return to God by adopting a third path, different from the two existing ones. From the beginning, it should be said that the Third International Theory is not a theory in the literal sense of the word, nor are its dimensions yet shaped in the Libyan Arab Republic to enable it to answer Man’s 178 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi day-to-day questions. However, it is the path of truth. It is not man-made as it is based on religion and, on the divine concept of Islam, specifically. It is not like the common theory liable to change by revocation or change. However, peoples look at the truth from different angles but, truth, in itself, remains always one, immortal and unchangeable because it is a transcendent fundamental and spiritual reality. Therefore, the “Third Theory” is not the exclusive property of any particular nation for it is not expounded for the benefit of a specific group. It is not also a kind of philosophical or ideological thinking for, unlike philosophy and ideology, it does not stop at political limits, the limits of nations and peoples. In this theory, a humanitarian concept for the seventies and the years to come is being expounded.
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: One aspect of this concept is the enunciation of a firm belief in the reality of existence and its dynamics. Many famous thinkers and philosophers sought for this reality but failed to find it. The reality of existence is not a riddle or a problem to all believers in religion who admit that they are part of that existence, and, being so, cannot transcend to comprehend the intricacies of existence which is a whole, partially closed before the eyes of individual parts. God, The Creator of the Universie, is the super-human and supra-national deity. He has revealed Himself to us through one religion, namely Islam, In fact, Prophet Muḥammad was not the bearer of Islam for Islam, in the divine concept, existed long before him. Other heavenly messages preceded Muḥammad's message, they had their prophets too also entrusted with messages calling humanity to the path of truth.
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: But, at one time, the peoples of the earth got confused and thought that Muḥammad's message was Islam. Henceforth, they distinguished themselves as Muslims, while the followers of Jesus-Christ called themselves Chrisitans and the followers of Moses Jews. That distinction bred contempt and enmity among the followers of the various heavenly messages which all emerge from Allah and are, therefore, Islam proper. To explain this, in clear-cut terms, we have to dwell on a human interpretation of the divine concept of Islam. This interpretation adopts the following logic:— 1. If all three monotheistic religions emerge from one God, is it then reasonable that these messages contradict with themselves. Of course, there should be no contradictions since the source is one. Therefore, unity exists among all three heavenly messages and this unity in truth is an indisputable reality. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 179
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY 2. However, since all three heavenly messages emerge from one source, why then did they not come all at one and the same time? — Man, being weak by nature, always succumbs to lusts and temptations, and, consequently, lacks wisdom and determination. God being all-loving for His creatures, decided to forward to them more than one prophet to guide them to the right path, the path of truth. Whenever humanity digressed, God forwarded one of his prophets to bring Mankind back to reason and to the one true religion. Moreover, Man, being unable to absorb God's teachings in one dose, needed to be reminded intermittently by God's prophets of the one and only message of truth. 3. Why did God consent to Islam being the only religion for His creatures? — Because Islam is the last heavenly religion which completes the two previous ones. 4.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: Islam is the seal of all other religions and Muhammad is the last of the prophets. This is because the Holy Qur'an came out as a detailed constitution for Man's spiritual and temporal life. Meanwhile, misinterpretation of the divine concept leads the Jews, for instance, to consider themselves God's “chosen people”. This man-made interpretation, is erroneous for it is based on an egotistic principle entitling the Jews to acquire everything for them and deprive all non-Jews from what is good. Such being the case, the Third International Theory is based on Islam, in its divine and non-fanatical concept. Religion, it is noted, is the most vital necessity for Man without which he would simply err in life. Even the atheist who seems unaware of religion has a religion of his own. The communist, outside his official work, may be a fervent or a non-fervent Orthodox.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: But, religion is humanly conceived in a dual way: a correct conception and a deviationist one. In its correct sense, religion is submission to divine guidance which organizes the relation of Man with his God, with other men and with himself. If conceived from this angle, happiness will prevail over the world and in the hereafter. on the other hand, religion, in its deviationist sense, is a mixture of feelings, including cruelty, fanaticism, materialism, selfishness and submission to natural phenomena. The Third International Theory adheres to the correct conception of religion and believes in the universality of Islam as it is a religion that provides answers to every minute question whether it is earthly or spiritual. Therefore, the Third Theory is the only path capable of uprooting falsehood as it is based on morals, ideals and values. It is also capable of 180 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi putting an end to man's slavery to materialistic objectives as it considers all men God's creatures, all being equal, gaining preference only through piety. The Libyan Arab republic is dedicating itself to the benefit of truth, freedom and peace in the world. It does not simply raise this slogan but puts it is implementation. The nationalism it practices is not at all aggressive because a quick look at its development programmes on the home front will promptly divert you from reaching such a naive conclusion. It is assiduously trying to establish bridges of confidence among members of Mankind, and towards this end, it is actively helping all its brothers in humanity to get rid of oppression and colonialism.
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: If it succeeds to base its relations on mutual confidence, and ascertain the integrity of its intentions, beliefs, initiatives, attitudes, as well as the solidity of the ground on which we stand, the 1st of September Revolution will play the role of a catalyst in promoting worldwide efforts to surmount the obstacles created by the materilistic look, by governments and by worldly politics and sophistications. The Theory it expounds is a humanitarian and not an aggressive theory because Arab nationalism, on which it rests, is not at all agressive as it does not survive at the expense of others. However, adepts of this Theory cannot trust a non-religious man because the latter is not bound to any moral value that will make him stick to a principle or an agreement. The only interpretation of history accepted by the adepts of the Third Theory is only based on both religion and nationalism.
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: God has created us and scattered us into different nations in order to get acquainted with each other and not to fight and quarrel with each other. None of us can do without these two paramount factors, which, if used properly, can help us solve our problems. True believers in God cannot attack other peoples, rob them of their freedom and enslave them, for this is inequity which cannot be committed by men who fear God. But those who went astray and, deliberately or unconsciously, abandoned religion, have no such consideration. To them might is right. Big powers attack other countries or milk their resources dry in disregard of any ethical obligations. As for the economic aspects of the Third Theory, we may say that it seeks solutions for Man's economic problems in true socialism. Socialism, in that sense, is not at all communism, nor is it, in fact, another naming for it.
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: Islam provides for the realization of social justice and equity. It does not give the right to any rich person to use his wealth as an instrument of oppression. Limitation of property means, in Islam, that whenever oppression resulting from excessive wealth arises, the State becomes entitled to curb it, whether through expropriation, nationalization, progressive income tax or any other suitable measures. However, property ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 181
segments.label: page - Mu'ammar Al-Qadhāfi

segments.text: THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY may continue to be free if it causes no harm. But wealth and property should not be allowed to co-exist in one society. In such a case, the Government is entitled to enact relevant laws which would provide for taking away from the rich to give to the poor, likewise the Third Theory stands against exploiting capitalism. The capitalists in the United States induce their government to create areas of tension so they can find an opening to market U.S. manufactured weapons and keep the warface machinery in operation. Women in both the East and West have been employed in jobs against their human nature to earn money. Many other forms of exploitation has subdued man and turned him away from God. Anxiety among the Northern societies (both East and West) leads Man to commit suicide.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: Suicide in Southern societies (majorly third World countries) is uncommon. Drugs and alcoholic drinks though harmful to Man are being increasingly used in societies which have, deliberately or unconsciously, abandoned religion. Here, in the Libyan Arab republic, a popular and cultural revolution is now under way. It is an extension of the 1st September Revolution of 1969. Three years were necessary to pave the way before the day when the masses take over genuine power in their hands. In Libya, a new and pioneering experience is being nation-wide launched. In each village, oasis, city, school, university or organization, People's Committees have been set up. These committees entitle the masses to govern themselves by themselves and start a veritable change.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: The popular revolution is, in fact, an operation which consists of destroying everything harmful and untrue, and building anew a society which adheres to the principles of the Third International Theory and to the tasks and objectives set forth by the 1st of September Revolution. All misleading and dubious thoughts, imported from both East and West, reactionary thoughts and all obstructionist elements are being wiped out. Only the thought which emerges from Islam, which is a true expression of Arabism, humanitarianism, socialism and progress, should prevail. All those who look down at the people, owing to their positions or grades, are being trampled underfoot in an unbloody purge. Freedom is being enjoyed here by the working masses; it is not monopolized by any class or group of people. Exploitation, in all its shades, is nation-wide banned.
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

segments.text: No place in this society exists for the hypocrite, opportunist, regionalist, separatist or member of a political party. In that sense, the Libyan Arab Republic is exerting every possible effort to create a model society, abiding by the precepts of Islam and humanitarian and spiritual values. 182 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE THIRD INTERNATIONAL THEORY

So many times when the city seems to be without a friendly face, A lonely place, It's nice to know that you'll be there if I need you and you'll always smile, It's all worth while, Touch me and I end up singing, Troubles seem to up and disappear, You touch me with the love you're bringing, I can't really lose when you're near, When you're near my love, If all my freidns have forgotten half their promises they're not unkind, Just hard to find.

segments.text: Propagation of Islam: The Basic Principles Khurshid Ahmad, Director of The Islamic Foundation, London, United Kingdom Propagation of Islam: The Basic Principles This is the first contribution to this journal by Professor Khurshid Ahmad. Although most readers would be familiar with Professor Ahmad's tireless efforts on behalf of Islam, a brief introduction is in order for the benefit of the general readership. Dr. Ahmad is a former professor of economy at Karachi University and, later, at Lester University (England). He has written a number of books dealing with various Islamic topics, and has served as editor for several Islamic journals. Professor Ahmad is a well-known speaker at Islamic conferences around the globe. In this article, he summarizes his long and valuable experience as propagator of Islam in non-Muslim societies. Movement is a law of nature.
segments.label: page - Propagation of Islam: The Basic Principles

segments.text: Life itself is symbolized by action, effort and movement. In a world that is ever-changing, one has to move even to remain in the same place. What is true of the world of nature is even more true for the individual and social life of man. Islam is fully cognizant of this situation and provides for the efficient operation of this life-mechanism. A number of provisions have been made to make the principle of movement operative in the socio-moral life of the Community of Islam. Da'wah is one such principle. It constitutes a built-in mechanism that keeps the community as well as the individuals who compose it, active and upright, ensures the moral health of the individual and the community, and acts as a corrective force and a blessing for the whole of mankind. Da'wah literally means call or invitation.
segments.label: page - Propagation of Islam: The Basic Principles

segments.text: In Islamic terminology it connotes the invitation addressed to mankind by Allah and his prophets to believe in Islam, the true religion, the religion of all prophets. The message of the prophets is universal and this invitation is addressed to all without any discrimination. The only valid differentiation between human beings, according to Islam, is based on their response to this Da'wah: those who believe in it or refuse to accept it. Islam: Faith, Community or Movement. All the prophets were raised to convey Islam to their People, and Muhammad 184 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 184-191
segments.label: page - Propagation of Islam: The Basic Principles

segments.text: Khurshid Ahmad Khurshid Ahmad (peace be upon him) is the last of these prophets.1 He presented this divine guidance in its complete and final form.2 He invited the entire human race to follow the path of Allah and has been a mercy and a blessing to them all.3 The mission of the prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was to provide this complete guidance to mankind and to establish a community and a movement to act as its standard-bearer. The Muslim Community has been assigned the same role vis-à-vis the rest of the world as the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was assigned to perform in respect of them. Thus we appointed you a moderate and moderating Ummah, that you may be witnesses (of Truth) to the people and that the Prophet may be a witness to you.4 The mission of the Prophet has been incorporated into the historical role of the Ummah.
segments.label: page - Khurshid Ahmad

segments.text: This has been achieved through two major factors: the preservation of the Qur'an, which embodies the divine guidance and of the example of the Prophet (peace be upon him); and the assignment of the missionary role to the Ummah as its primary function.5 This responsibility rests on each and every believer and not merely on any one class or group of people. It is the common believer who has been primarily charged with this responsibility, and this is a unique feature of Islam. 6 The moral health of the Muslim Community and of society at large depends on the continuation of these roles and responsibilities. Da'wah: The Islamic Concept Islam is the religion for man. It is the embodiment of that code of life, that guidance, which the Creator of the Universe has revealed for the benefit of mankind.
segments.label: page - Khurshid Ahmad

segments.text: Its primary concern is to build correct relationships between God and man as well as among men.7 Faith represents one's commitment to God — a commitment to think, feel and live with the awareness of the Lord, to bring his will into harmony with the Divine Will and to strive to make His will supreme in the world. Islam awakens a new consciousness in man and gives him a new outlook on life. Equipped with this new outlook, he joins a community of faith and participates in a movement, a collective effort, to reconstruct human life and society.8 Islam stands, not for life-denial, but for life-fulfillment. It presents a program for the radical transformation of man and society in ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 185 وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِّتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا
segments.label: page - Khurshid Ahmad

segments.text: PROPAGATION OF ISLAM PROPAGATION OF ISLAM the light of the basic concepts of the Unity of God (Tawḥīd) and the equality of all people. It gives an integrated view of man: moral and material, and spiritual and temporal, are welded into an indivisible whole. It refuses to divide life rigidly into the things of this world and those of the next; it regards the two as extensions of one another and invites man to enjoy the best of this world and the best of the hereafter. 9 In our own times the Islamic Da'wah has quite often been presented in ways that leave much to be desired. For a host of reasons, some historical, some otherwise, the system which Muslims had evolved for Da'wah was particularly disrupted over the last two centuries. Whatever partial efforts were made to restore some kind of a system remained of limited effectiveness.
segments.label: page - PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

segments.text: The rise of Imperialist powers and their political sway over most of the Muslim lands dealt a severe blow to the old arrangement. Christian missions, and later on Communist onslaughts provoked some reaction. However, these efforts mostly were directed to meet specific challenges. Consequently, they not only remained (basically) negative, but also became over-obsessed with the issues raised by these foreign intruders. This distorted the perspective. It is therefore, necessary that the concept of Da'wah, as it emerges from the Qur'an and Sunnah should be clearly understood. 1. Islam is not the national religion of the Muslim. It is the eternal religion. Muḥammad (peace be upon him) is not the author of Islam. Allāh has revealed essentially the same religion through all His prophets.
segments.label: page - PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

segments.text: Thus the prophets Abraham, Isaac, Ismael, David, Joseph, Moses, and Jesus (peace and blessings on them) invited man to follow the path of Islam and no other. 10 The followers of these prophets did not safeguard their teachings with the result that some of the message was lost while in the rest of it the Word of God and the word of man were mixed up. (see insert from the St. Louis Post Dispatch of January 10, 1975). Muḥammad (peace be upon him) was raised to reveal the same path in its pristine purity and to restore and finalize God's message to all humanity. The Qur'an is the superceding guardian (Muhaimin) of the doctrine revealed to all the prophets. 11 Muslims believe in all the prophets and we are not allowed to play one off against the other. We invite all people to discover their real religion.
segments.label: page - PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

segments.text: The teaching of the Qur'an is to make them eschew all national or racial prejudices and join this universal community of faith. 12 The first principle of Islamic Da'wah is to emphasize this common feature and to ignore all national antagonisms. They are not our concern at all. 186 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

segments.text: Khurshid Ahmad 2. Secondly Islam is a complete way of life, and not a scheme of partial reform. It deals with the whole of man, his spiritual, moral, personal and social existence. It offers guidance on every aspect of human life. It aims at spiritual, moral, material and social reconstruction of human society. It tries to change man from within and to enable this new man to create a just and harmonious society. It neither neglects the spiritual, nor the material dimensions of life. The moral ideal of Islam seeks realization in the shape of a God-conscious man operating in a moral society — with its social, economic, political, national and international relations emanating from the basis of truth and justice. It is this complete and integrated view of Islam as a way of life that deserves to be projected in Da'wah. 3.
segments.label: page

segments.text: The Islamic Da'wah is to be presented through word and deed at individual and social levels. It is a misconception that Da'wah would be complete or fully effective merely by spreading the knowledge of Islam. The teachings of Islam must be disseminated but this should be accompanied by setting a true Islamic example, individually as well as collectively. The Qur'an emphasizes that a prophet is the first believer;13 he lives according to what he preaches. 14 That is why his words are a source of knowledge and his actions are a model for behavior. 15 Conformity between word and deed, particularly in the context of Da'wah, has been stressed by the Qur'an. 16 It is therefore a fundamental principle that Muslims in making efforts toward Da'wah must also set a good example to the rest of the community. It follows that Da'wah is not merely for non-believers.
segments.label: page

segments.text: It is equally important for believers and non-believers; it consists in efforts to Islamise the Muslims17 and to convey Islam to the non-Muslims. 4. Another principle of Da'wah is to carefully examine the circumstances in which the message is being delivered. The message is universal but it should be presented in such a way that its relevance to the situation is fully realized. Moreover, the problems of the society are to be approached in such a way that the evil is atttacked at its roots, not merely at the level of symptoms. This becomes very clear when we try to study in the Qur'an the way in which different prophets conveyed their basic message. All of them tried to go to the root of the problem — whether a people acknowledge the sovereignty of God or not. In the last analysis everything follows from this fundamental outlook.
segments.label: page

segments.text: That is why every prophet tried to correct the relationship between God and man. But along with this he took issue with his people in the light of their situation. Prophets Solomon and Moses (peace be upon them) took up the question of magic. Prophet Lūt focused on the sexual morality of his people. Prophet Shu'aib invited them to establish economic justice. Prophet Moses concerned himself with the political and cultural servitude of the Children of Israel. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 187
segments.label: page

segments.text: PROPAGATION OF ISLAM PROPAGATION OF ISLAM Prophet Joseph looked into the management of the state and its economy. And in respect of each of their problem-areas they showed how the establishment of a proper relationship with God on the correct foundations would help them solve their problems. From this we may infer that the Da'wah should not only take note of the specific problems of the society in which it is being given but should also go deeper and show how a fundamental transformation of outlook is a precondition to the solution of these problems. 5. Da'wah is not merely a system of communication with the outside world, it also includes the evolution of a system of training — of Tarbiyah and Yazkiyah — so that the mechanism for absorption and consolidation should operate along with the machinery for contact and expansion.
segments.label: page - PROPAGATION OF ISLAM

segments.text: This is essential for the maintenance and improvement of the moral health of the community itself. 6. The ideal form for Da'wah is that the entire community should be organized on the principle of Khilafah 'ala-Minhaj-al-Nabuwwah (caliphate patterned after the Prophet's life). Under this system the Ummah can attain optimum effectiveness, within and without. The collective system would be a model of Islam. This is the most effective way. But if this is not so, as is the situation today, then on the one hand efforts should be made to establish this system, and on the other, whoever is conscious of the missionary responsibilities of the Ummah should engage in this task individually as well as through organized effort. 18 It is in pursuance of this principle that efforts at Da'wah are being made by muslims in different parts of the world. 7.

segments.text: Another principle is that Da'wah should be presented in a most carefully diplomatic way. The Qur'an says: Invite others to the way of your Lord with wisdom and gentle admonition and debate with them in the best possible manner. 19 In the Qur'an and Sunnah ample light has been thrown upon certain methodological aspects of Da'wah. Inter alia the following deserve careful consideration. (i) Those methods should not be used which may inflame the combative passions of the addressees, dim their sense of perception or provoke prejudiced retaliation. 20 (ii) If you are wronged, try to rectify the situation by resorting to good means. segments.text: Khurshid Ahmad (iii) The efforts should be made with patience and perseverance. The Qur'anic term for this mode of behaviour is Ṣabr, which implies (a) patience in the sense of being thorough and devoted; (b) constancy, perseverance, steadfastness and firmness of purpose; (c) planned and systematic effort with a realization of phases and grades involved; (d) confidence and belief in the mission itself; (e) a cheerful attitude of acceptance and understanding in sorrow, defeat or suffering and of humble restraint and thankfulness to God in happiness, success and achievement. Ṣabr is the principle of constructive dynamism and of calculated effort in the path of Da'wah. (iv) To adopt a rational and thoughtful approach and to resort to informed discussion and cool debate.
segments.label: page - Khurshid Ahmad

segments.text: In this respect it is suggested that one should make use of all available knowledge, the most reliable sources. (v) To be aware of the psychology of the people, their receptivity and responsiveness. Da'wah is not a unilateral process with one way traffic only. It should involve a meaningful dialogue, to be pursued with care, wisdom and patience. The element of time and different quantitative and qualitative consideration should be kept in view. (vi) The message should be clearly expressed in the language of the people, the crucial importance of the Arabic language not withstanding. This is essential so that they feel at home with the message and are able to follow it. (vii) Efforts should be made to benefit from the latest and most appropriate techniques of contact and communication.
segments.label: page - Khurshid Ahmad

segments.text: The best possible technology should be used in the service of the Da'wah. (viii) The process of Da'wah should be properly graduated. We must be clear about our priorities. Fundamentals must have precedence over details. Faith should be the first target. It is only through attainment of faith that the road to Islamic life can be followed. Obligatory duties should come before non-obligatory ones. The objectives and general principles of the Shari'ah should come before its minutia. Sectarian differences should be avoided at all levels and emphasis placed upon the essentials and on the areas of agreement. No effort should be made to achieve everything all at once. The wisdom behind the piece-meal revelation of the Qur'an was that society adopts Islam step by step and gets firmly rooted in it through a gradual process. segments.text: Pioneer Reform Judaism Commentary On Torah To Be Published Next Week PROPAGATION OF ISLAM Fri., Jan. 10, 1975 ST. LOUIS POST-DISPATCH Pioneer Reform Judaism Commentary On Torah To Be Published Next Week By David E. Anderson UPI Religion Writer The first volume of a new, liberal commentary on the Torah—the first five books of the Bible—which challenges the view that the Torah is the Word of God will be published next week. The commentary is the first to be produced by Reform Judaism and the only such work ever published in North America. Volume 1 of the commentary, which is being published by the Union of American Hebrew Congregations and is expected to be the standard Torah commentary for the nation's 1,100,000 Reform Jews, deals with the book of Genesis. It was written by Rabbi Gunther Plaut of Holy Blossom Temple in Toronto.
segments.label: page - Pioneer Reform Judaism Commentary On Torah To Be Published Next Week

segments.text: "Our commentary disagrees with traditional interpreters over divine origin and mosaic authorship," Plaut said, "But it does agree with them on treating the text as it is, a unified whole for it was approached this way by many generations and, in this way, it has made its impact on history" Most Orthodox Jews and Fundamentalist Christians believe the books of Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers and Deuteronomy were written by Moses through direct verbal inspiration from God.
segments.label: page - Pioneer Reform Judaism Commentary On Torah To Be Published Next Week

segments.text: Plaut, however, in his introuctory essay to the commentary, argues that the Torah "is a human book composed by men." He also argues that it is "A book about man's understanding of an experience with God" and, citing the ancient Jews' oral tradition which resulted in divergent views about God and man, said "these stand side by side in the book and tell us of our ancestors changing and developing beliefs." "In this sense, then, the book is not by God but by a people . . . it is ancient Israel's distinctive record of its search for God." 190 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) Footnotes 1. Qur'an, 42: 2. segments.text: ISLAM: Its Mission in the World Professor M. Farīd Wajdī ISLAM: Its Mission in the World 3. DECLARATION OF UNIVERSAL BROTHERHOOD OF NATIONS Of all his achievements as writer, editor of Nour-el-Islam, and Professor at Al-Azhar University, Dr. Wajdi is better known for his famous Qur'anic commentary. This series of articles, which were written by him in Arabic, promises to be a most cherished feature by ALL readers of Islam. Following the proclamation that it is the true Faith, and the inculcation of the twofold basis of human nature and pure reason on which it was founded, Islam sought to introduce a momentous social reform requisite for a great civilization which The Lord has willed Islam to establish on earth. This momentous reform was the calling of mankind to universal brotherhood.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: For though Islam did not differ, in its doctrinal principles, from the message revealed to previous Prophets, yet it was favoured by certain circumstances which anterior religions lacked. Intercourse between nations was so difficult that it was well-nigh impossible to bring them all together to one universal religion. This privilege was destined by The Lord to be granted to Islam in whose time intercourse between nations was rendered feasible. The Divine Wisdom has seen fit to afford it all the qualifications and advantages which make it a universal religion fitted for all times and climes. Was the world then at the advent of Muhammad in need of a violent blow from heaven to urge it to unity, or a wrathful cry from high to stop the misguided in their career of sin and aberration?
segments.label: page - ISLAM: Its Mission in the World

segments.text: We may well leave the answer of this question to a foreigner, the great French orientalist Monsieur Jules Le Baum. In the introduction to his index of the Holy Qur'an, he described the world's conditions prior to the advent of Muhammad in the following terms: At about the time when Muhammad was born, the world was seething with trouble and unrest. He then began to detail the generalities of this statement pointing to the animosity and contention which raged fiercely between nations: The world's atmosphere was charged with fierce vibrations. Evil was more counted upon than good and the minds of men were not at rest. The chiefs who won most of the confidence of the people, were those who raised the strong and made strong nations, cities, lords, mendicants. Had it not been for some cells of civilization from the raging sea, the apostles of progress and arrogance of the age of savagery.

Only one argument touched the hearts and made strong though passing convictions: the booty, despoiling of nations, cities, lords, men of arms, poor labourers and even simple mendicants. Had it not been for the small light which flickered in the depths of some cells of cenbites, and for some philosophic principles sheltered from the raging storms and transmitted from soul to soul by the bold apostles of progress, barbarism, accelerated in its march by the arrogance of the masters of brutal force, would have become pure savagery. After long dwelling on the condition that then prevailed, the writer said: It was during those sad circumstances, and in that heavily charged atmosphere, that Muhammad Ibn ‘Abdallāh, was born on the 29th of August 570.
segments.label: page - M. Farid Wajdi

segments.text: Indeed! the Arab nation itself was no less divided and contending than the rest of the world. Through tribal division, it formed a collection of antagonistic communities which knew no peace and were for ever on the war-path. The Arabian Peninsula was a vast battlefield on which all the dictates of love and mercy were completely ignored so much so that a man was to clout his sandal from the very skin of his enemy after having him slain and mutilated. It was in that chaotic era, in that atmosphere of stygian darkness and ruthlessness, that The Lord bade Muhammad to raise high the standard of universal brotherhood and to establish for mankind the foundation of that unity. The Lord’ saying was thus revealed to him: [Arabic text] O, mankind, We have created you all from Adam and Eve, and We have made you into peoples and tribes that you might know one another.
segments.label: page - M. Farid Wajdi

segments.text: Verily the best among you, in the sight of Allāh, is the most pious; Allāh is all-knowing and cognisant of your innermost thoughts. (49:13) The Arabs among whom this high and noble principle was preached, were most proud of lineage and boastful of forefathers. Each tribe claimed the greatest honour for itself in that respect and so much indeed had this tendency been exaggerated among them that they were wont to establish the pedigree of their camels and horses to raise them thereby above all others of their kind. The reader may well imagine their disdain for other distant peoples and tribes differing from them in colour, language and traditions. segments.text: ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD Yet the Lord had sent the last of His Prophets with this high principle to call them thereunto even though he evoked derision and was not heeded by the ignorant ones: Wherefore proclaim what you have been bidden and heed not what the polytheists say. [15:94] The mere declaration of this noble principle in a world in which everything urged to discord and disunion is in itself a mighty evidence of its divine origin, for indeed the philosopher's mind, no matter how high it soars, could never have overstepped its bounds as to conceive such a universal principle at a time in which circumstances urged to its very reverse!
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: This universal brotherhood proclaimed by Islam may well be considered a herald of a new era in the history of nations, and a prelude to further universal Qur'anic principles calculated to achieve the unification of human views and objects. We could not however leave off this subject without alluding to the beauty of the convincible style in which this great principle, like every other principle preached by the Holy Qur'an, is couched. The Lord has first called the attention of mankind. Then He reminded them of the origin from which they have come advancing thereby the proof before the facts, a procedure which is acknowledged as the highest of rhetorical and convincible styles. For indeed who could deny that all men, despite their difference in environment, color and mode of life, are the sons of Adam and Eve?
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: This reminder which overrode all the barriers raised by men and trampled over the prevailing customs and traditions which have long caused it to fall into abeyance, urges the souls to listen attentively to what is to follow, and thus prepared, the souls are apprised with the object of this reminder, namely that The Lord has made men into peoples and tribes so that they might know one another, live amicably together, cooperate in smoothing down the hardships of life and strive to attain the welfare and prosperity of the human community at large. This will put an end to contention which leads to war and can only result in destruction. War is a ceaseless strife and victory oscillates from one nation to another and should war be waged for purely material ends, it will only serve to fill the hearts with hatred and increase the desire for vengeance.

Why did it seek expansion in neighbouring countries? and why did it flood near and distant people the way it did? Why did it not content itself with evidence and proof in calling those people to its cause? And why did it not seek to win their approval by mere conviction and good example? Our answer to this objection is that Islam is primarily a religion which conforms to the laws of nature as well as to the social factors governing life. Up to the advent of Islam, those laws and factors required a certain amount of force, otherwise the mission of Islam would have been a failure and no trace would have been left of it.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: On account of the open prohibition of war ordained by Christianity it continued in a weak condition for over three hundred years. The Roman Emperors were wont to put to death all its adherents, dismember them while they still lived and hunt them down wherever they went. When Constantine, whose mother had embraced Christianity, and secretly brought him up as a Christian, came to the throne, he used force to propagate this religion and gave orders to pull down the pagan temples and forced people, under penalty of torture, to embrace it. The ascendancy of Christianity goes back to that date and for the very same reason, it is firmly established up to this day in many parts of the world. Should Islam have contented itself with preaching without having recourse to force, it would have been restricted within the Peninsula and the unbelievers would have forced its adherents to forsake it.
segments.label: page - ISLAM: ITS MISSION IN THE WORLD

segments.text: Even if it were spared annihilation, Islam would have found itself in a similar position as that of the Religion of Abraham which was preached by a few men scattered throughout Arabia of whom no trace could be found among human communities. But although Islam had prepared for war, yet it had certainly mitigated a great deal of its severity and rendered more humane the laws pertaining to it. A just code was established by Islam which definitely prohibited aggression. (See [Quran 2:190]) Indeed, the greatest merit in favour of Islam is that it did not ordain war for despoiling nations or levying tributes thereon, but it was wielded as a means for the propagation of the word of Allah among nations. Never before had any nation waged war for this reason. Wars were waged to subjugate people, appropriate their wealth and products and finally take full possession of everything in the land.

segments.text: The Falsification of Hadith: History and Development Professor Muhammad ‘Ajjāj Al-Khaṭīb, College of Sharī‘ah (Islamic Law), University of Damascus The Falsification of Hadith: History and Development While the Qur’an enjoys the Divine guarantee of God’s own protection and eternal preservation [15:9], the second source of Islamic jurisprudence, namely, the Hadith suffered disastrous human distortion, misinterpretation, falsification, and fabrication. A great number of Hadiths (the Prophet’s sayings and traditions) were rescued and verified through the life-time exertion of such scholars as Al-Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dawūd, Al-Tirmidhī, Al-Nasā’ī, Ibn Mājah, and others. However, even within the works of each of these scholars, a significant proportion of questionable Hadiths still exists.
segments.label: page - The Falsification of Hadith: History and Development

segments.text: In this article, presented in Arabic and in English, Professor Al-Khaṭīb reports on the history and development of fabricated Hadiths; with the hope that the readers may be better able to evaluate the Hadiths they come accross. The ultimate criterion for judging the authenticity of Hadith shall always be the Qur’an, the eternally-protected message of Allah. Any “Hadith” which contradicts any Qur’anic principle(s) should be deemed incorrect. The traditions of the Prophet Muhammad (Allah’s peace and blessings be upon him) remained pure and free from falsification throughout the reign of the four great caliphs. For as long as the Muslim ummah remained solidly behind their rulers, the Prophet’s sunnah remained unadulterated.
segments.label: page - The Falsification of Hadith: History and Development

segments.text: Only when people with fanatic political and or materialistic tendencies succeeded in dividing the Muslim ummah that the abuse and downright fabrication of Hadith took place. The first break in the solidarity of the ummah is traceable to the assassination of the third caliph ‘Uthmān (may Allah bestow His pleasure and grace upon him). That tragic event shook up the Muslim ummah so violently, that the damaging consequences still live with us today. Although the ummah was able to re-unite behind the fourth caliph ‘Ali b. Abū Ṭālib (Allah’s pleasure and grace upon him), the events which ensued were much too powerful to permit the continuation of sustained unity.

The Taḥkīm itself resulted in more division within the ummah: four different groups were formed: 1. The majority of Muslims remained solidly behind the caliph 'Ali, since he was the legitimate, shūra-selected Amīr-ul-Mu'minīn (the caliph selected by general consensus of the leaders and representatives of all Muslims), following the assassination of the third caliph 'Uthmān. 2. The party of Mu'āwiyah which was initially formulated to "avenge the death of 'Uthmān, but ended up demanding the caliphate for their leader Mu'āwiyah.
segments.label: page - Muhammad 'Ajjāj Al-Khaṭīb

segments.text: Following the Taḥkīm, this group did capture the caliphate. and Mu'āwiyah became the ruler of the torn ummah. 3. The Khawārij (The Rebels) who were supporters of 'Ali, but rebelled against him for accepting the Taḥkīm; they declared that only Allah had the power of Taḥkīm. At the same time, they violently opposed Mu'āwiyah for wanting to snatch the caliphate away from 'Ali. 4. Following the martyrdom of Amīr-ul-Mu'minīn 'Ali, some of his supporters formed the Shi'ah party and demanded restoration of caliphate to Ahlul Bait ('Ali's family). The Falsification Since each one of the above mentioned parties wanted to muster the allegiance of the Muslim ummah, they sought to support their political views by Qur'anic statements and sunnah traditions. Thus, some of them resorted to flagrant misinterpretations of the Qur'an; some even attempted to falsify the Qur'an itself.
segments.label: page - Muhammad 'Ajjāj Al-Khaṭīb

segments.text: With the divine guarantee of the Qur'an's integrity, those who attempted to distort the Qur'an were immediately exposed. Too many people had already committed the Qur'an to their memory, and the Qur'an distorters got nowhere. What they succeeded in, however, was the injection of false Ḥadīths into the Prophet's traditions, as well as misinterpreting the existing Ḥadīths. With the passage of time, so many false Ḥadīths were fabricated that the authentic Ḥadīths became almost completely indistinguishable from the false ones. The first falsified Ḥadīths were characterized by the praise and over-glorification of certain individuals, such as the four great caliphs, and Ahlul Bait; something they neither needed nor advocated. Then, other fabrications of Ḥadīths dealt with the establishment of certain political parties and various religious sects.
