عنه قام بعض شيعته يطالبون بحقهم في الخلافة . وهكذا نشأت الأحزاب والفرق التي اتخذت شكلا دينيا كان له أبلغ الأثر في قيام المذاهب الدينية في الإسلام (1) . وقد حاول كل حزب أن يدعى ما يدعى بالقرآن والسنة ، ومن البدهى ألا يجد كل حزب ما يؤيد دعواه في نصوص القرآن الكريم والسنة الشريفة ، فتأول بعضهم القرآن ، وفسروا بعض نصوص الحديث بما لا تحمله ، إلا أن هذا لم يُحقق ما يرمون إليه ، ولم يجد بعضهم إلى تحريف القرآن أو تأويله سبيلا ، لكثرة حفاظه ، فتناولوا السنة بالتحريف وزادوا عليها ، ووضعوا على رسول الله ما لم يقل (2) ، ونشطت حركة الوضع مع الزمن ، حتى اختلط الحديث الصحيح بالموضوع ، وظهرت أحاديث موضوعة في فضائل الخلفاء الأربعة وغيرهم من رؤساء الفرق وزعماء الأحزاب ، ثم ظهرت (۱) انظر السنة ومكانتها في التشريع الإسلامي ص ۸۹ (۲) انظر اللآلىء المصنوعة ص ٢٤٨ ج ۲
segments.label: page

segments.text: ابتداء الوضع وأسبابه IN THE NAME OF ALLAH Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon Muhammad, this script is a translation of the foreward message of the above-mentioned addresses, and to our readers who are doing good works; they are the people of Paradise, they abide therein. And it is not true that God has created a thing and set an edge thereof, and then said (it is a lie). What a lie! They are indeed liars.
segments.label: page - ابتداء الوضع وأسبابه

segments.text: ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) محمد عجاج الخطيب الأستاذ المساعد في كلية الشريعة بجامعة دمشق ابتداء الوضع وأسبابه.. أولا - ابتداء الوضع : بقي الحديث النبوي صافيا لا يعتريه الكذب، ولا يتناوله التحريف والتلفيق طوال اجتماع كلمة الأمة على الخلفاء الأربعة الراشدين، قبل أن تنقسم إلى شيع وأحزاب، وقبل أن يندس في صفوفها أهل المصالح والأهواء، وكانت البادئة الأولى التي ترتبت عليها الاضطرابات الكثيرة في القرن الهجري الأول هي فتنة عثمان رضي الله عنه واستشهاده، فقد هزت العالم الإسلامي هزة عظيمة، وأورثت الأمة عواقب وخيمة، امتدت آثارها إلى يومنا، ثم اجتمعت - بعد الفتنة - كلمة المسلمين على أمير المؤمنين علي رضي الله عنه، إلا أن الأحداث كانت أقوى من أن تفسح للهدوء والسلام سبيلهما إلى الدولة آنذاك، فحصل انقسام كبير في صفوف الأمة، تجسم في معسكر أمير المؤمنين علي الذي انطوى تحته أهل الحجاز والعراق، ومعسكر أمير الشام معاوية الذي انضم إليه أكثر أهلها وأهل مصر. وقد جر هذا الانقسام على الأمة الحروب الطاحنة، وما لبث أن انتهى بالتحكيم الذي كان سببا لظهور فرق سياسية مختلفة (1)، فالجمهور يؤيدون عليا. (1) انظر تاريخ الإسلام للدكتور حسن إبراهيم ص ٢٦٨ ج ١، والتبصير في الدين ص ٦، وفجر الإسلام ص ٢٥٦. 246
segments.label: page - ابتداء الوضع وأسبابه

segments.text: Surat al-Kahf (The Cave) IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL Praise be to Allah, who revealed to His servant (Muhammad) this scripture, and made it flawless. A straight forward message, to preach the awesome power He possesses, and to deliver good news to the believers who do good works; that they shall receive a generous recompense; they abide therein forever. And to warn those who say that God has begotten a son! They have no certain knowledge thereof, nor did their predecessors (who invented this lie). What a gross fabrication coming out of their mouths!
segments.label: page - Surat al-Kahf (The Cave)

segments.text: They indeed utter but an abominable lie. (Qur'an 18:1-5) ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 247 سورة الكهف مكية وآياتها ١١٠ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ عِوَجًا ۝ قَيِّمًا لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِنْ لَدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا ۝ مَاكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًا ۝ وَيُنْذِرَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا ۝ مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلَا لِآبَائِهِمْ كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ إِنْ يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًا ۝
segments.label: page - Surat al-Kahf (The Cave)

segments.text: English Meanings of the Qur'an : 3 Rashād Khalifa, Ph.D. English Meanings of the Qur'an : 3 A true understanding of Islam requires, as a minimum, a reasonable understanding of its message, the Qur'an. While many people acquire a distorted picture of the religion by observing some aspects of the actions, history, or personal conduct of its professed followers, the readers of this series are presented with an opportunity to grasp the basic principles of true Islam. Readers who are familiar with the various Qur'anic translations will appreciate the fact that this is the first English rendering of the Qur'an's meanings by a Muslim Arab. It is being printed for the first time.
segments.label: page - English Meanings of the Qur'an : 3

segments.text: Sura Al-Baqarah (The Heifer) 2:99-187 In the Name of Allāh, the Compassionate, most Merciful (The Distortion of Previous Scripture) 99 We reveal to you herein (O Muḥammad) clear verses; only the wicked shall reject them. 100 Is it ever so that whenever they make a covenant, some of them would disregard it? Indeed, most of them do not believe. 101 Thus, when a messenger from God came to them, though confirming their own scripture, some of those who received previous scripture rejected this scripture of God behind their backs as if they know not. 102 They followed instead what the devils have distorted for them such as the magic powers of Solomon. It was not Solomon who abused such powers; it was the devils who abused them. Thus, they taught the people sorcery as revealed through the two angels Hārūt and Mārūt.
segments.label: page - English Meanings of the Qur'an : 3

segments.text: However, these two did not teach anyone except with the admonition that such teachings were a test; that no one shall abuse them. But they use this knowledge in such evil things as breaking up marriages. They can never hurt anyone, however, except by God's leave. They learn only what harms them, not what benefits them, and they fully realize that whoever follows such distortions gets no share in the hereafter. Miserable indeed is what they sold their souls for, if they only know. 248 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4): 248-266
segments.label: page - English Meanings of the Qur'an : 3

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:99-108) ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 249 (The Heifer) 2:99-108 الجزء الأول (٢) سورة البقرة وَلَقَدْ أَنزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ وَمَا يَكْفُرُ بِهَا إِلَّا الْفَاسِقُونَ ﴿٩٩﴾ أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُوا عَهْدًا نَّبَذَهُ فَرِيقٌ مِّنْهُم ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ ﴿١٠٠﴾ وَلَمَّا جَاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ نَبَذَ فَرِيقٌ مِّنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ كِتَابَ اللَّهِ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٠١﴾ وَاتَّبَعُوا مَا تَتْلُوا الشَّيَاطِينُ عَلَىٰ مُلْكِ سُلَيْمَانَ ۖ وَمَا كَفَرَ سُلَيْمَانُ وَلَٰكِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ كَفَرُوا يُعَلِّمُونَ النَّاسَ السِّحْرَ وَمَا أُنزِلَ عَلَى الْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ ۚ وَمَا يُعَلِّمَانِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ حَتَّىٰ يَقُولَا إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلَا تَكْفُرْ ۖ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا مَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ ۚ وَمَا هُم بِضَارِّينَ بِهِ مِنْ أَحَدٍ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ ۚ وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلَا يَنفَعُهُمْ ۚ وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُوا لَمَنِ اشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلَاقٍ ۚ وَلَبِئْسَ مَا شَرَوْا بِهِ أَنفُسَهُمْ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٠٢﴾ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا وَاتَّقَوْا لَمَثُوبَةٌ مِّنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ ۖ لَّوْ كَانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٠٣﴾ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَقُولُوا رَاعِنَا وَقُولُوا انظُرْنَا وَاسْمَعُوا ۗ وَلِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ ﴿١٠٤﴾ مَّا يَوَدُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ وَلَا الْمُشْرِكِينَ أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَن يَشَاءُ ۚ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ ﴿١٠٥﴾ مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِّنْهَا أَوْ مِثْلِهَا ۗ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ﴿١٠٦﴾ أَلَمْ تَعْلَمْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ۗ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ اللَّهِ مِن وَّلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ ﴿١٠٧﴾ أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ أَن تَسْأَلُوا رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ ۗ وَمَن يَتَبَدَّلِ الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيمَانِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ سَوَاءَ السَّبِيلِ ﴿١٠٨﴾
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah (2:99-108)

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:114-125 114 Who is more evil than those who abuse the mosques of Allāh, forbid the commemoration of His name therein, and actively seek to destroy them? These ought not to enter them but fearfully. They shall have but humiliation in this life and they shall suffer in the hereafter a great punishment. 115 However, to Allāh belongs the East and the West; wherever you go, there shall be the presence of Allāh. Surely, Allāh is Omnipresent, Omniscient. (All are Subservient to Allāh; He Begets Not) 116 They said, “Allāh has begotten a son.” Glory be to Him; Nay, to Him belong all that is in the heavens and the earth; All are subservient to Him. 117 He is the Initiator of the heavens and the earth.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: To ordain any matter, He simply says, “Be,” and it is. 118 Those who have no knowledge say, “If only Allāh would speak to us, or a miracle would come to us, (we will then believe).” Others before them had said the same thing. Their hearts are alike. We do clarify the signs for those who sincerely believe. 119 We have sent you (O Muhammad) with the truth, as a bearer of good news as well as a warner, and you are not responsible for those who merit Hell. 120 Neither the Jews, nor the Christians, would accept you unless you follow their way. Say, “The guidance of Allāh is the true guidance.” If you ever follow their wishes, after this knowledge has come to you, then you shall have no protector from Allāh, nor a supporter. 121 Those to whom We have given previous scripture, and truly follow it, shall believe in this scripture.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: As for those who disbelieve in this, they shall be the losers. 122 O Children of Israel, appreciate the favors which I bestowed upon you, and that I set you apart from all peoples. 123 Beware of the day when no soul shall avail another soul, no ransom shall be accepted, intercession shall be useless, and no one can be helped. (Abraham Fulfills the Commandments) 124 Recall that Abraham was put to the test by certain commandments from his Lord, and he did fulfill them. God then said, “I will make you an imam for the people.” Abraham said, “And from among my progeny?” God said, “My covenant includes not the wrong-doers.” 125 We rendered the House (the Ka‘bah) a focal point for mankind, and a place of peace.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Thus, you shall use this station of Abraham as 252 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَهِلَّةِ ۖ قُلْ هِيَ مَوَاقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَالْحَجِّ ۗ وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقَىٰ ۗ وَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ أَبْوَابِهَا ۗ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ (189) وَقَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ يُقَاتِلُونَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ (190) وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ حَيْثُ ثَقِفْتُمُوهُمْ وَأَخْرِجُوهُمْ مِنْ حَيْثُ أَخْرَجُوكُمْ ۚ وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ ۚ وَلَا تُقَاتِلُوهُمْ عِنْدَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ حَتَّىٰ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ فِيهِ ۖ فَإِنْ قَاتَلُوكُمْ فَاقْتُلُوهُمْ ۗ كَذَٰلِكَ جَزَاءُ الْكَافِرِينَ (191) فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (192) وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ لِلَّهِ ۖ فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا فَلَا عُدْوَانَ إِلَّا عَلَى الظَّالِمِينَ (193) الشَّهْرُ الْحَرَامُ بِالشَّهْرِ الْحَرَامِ وَالْحُرُمَاتُ قِصَاصٌ ۚ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاعْتَدُوا عَلَيْهِ بِمِثْلِ مَا اعْتَدَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ (194) وَأَنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلَا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ ۛ وَأَحْسِنُوا ۛ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (195) وَأَتِمُّوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ لِلَّهِ ۚ فَإِنْ أُحْصِرْتُمْ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ ۖ وَلَا تَحْلِقُوا رُءُوسَكُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ الْهَدْيُ مَحِلَّهُ ۚ فَمَنْ كَانَ مِنْكُمْ مَرِيضًا أَوْ بِهِ أَذًى مِنْ رَأْسِهِ فَفِدْيَةٌ مِنْ صِيَامٍ أَوْ صَدَقَةٍ أَوْ نُسُكٍ ۚ فَإِذَا أَمِنْتُمْ فَمَنْ تَمَتَّعَ بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ مِنَ الْهَدْيِ ۚ فَمَنْ لَمْ يَجِدْ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْحَجِّ وَسَبْعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعْتُمْ ۗ تِلْكَ عَشَرَةٌ كَامِلَةٌ ۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ أَهْلُهُ حَاضِرِي الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۚ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ (196)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:120 - 2:129) Al-Juz' Two (2) - Surah Al-Baqarah (2:120-129) وَلَن تَرْضَى عَنكَ الْيَهُودُ وَلَا النَّصَارَى حَتَّى تَتَّبِعَ مِلَّتَهُمْ قُلْ إِنَّ هُدَى اللَّهِ هُوَ الْهُدَى وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُم بَعْدَ الَّذِي جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ مَا لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن وَلِيِّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ ﴿١٢٠﴾ الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَتْلُونَهُ حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ أُولَٰئِكَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ ۗ وَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِهِ فَأُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ ﴿١٢١﴾ يَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ اذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتِيَ الَّتِي أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّي فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿١٢٢﴾ وَاتَّقُوا يَوْمًا لَّا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَن نَّفْسٍ شَيْئًا وَلَا يُقْبَلُ مِنْهَا عَدْلٌ وَلَا تَنفَعُهَا شَفَاعَةٌ وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ ﴿١٢٣﴾ وَإِذِ ابْتَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَبُّهُ بِكَلِمَاتٍ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًا ۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِي ۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِي الظَّالِمِينَ ﴿١٢٤﴾ وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا وَاتَّخِذُوا مِن مَّقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مُصَلًّى ۖ وَعَهِدْنَا إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ أَن طَهِّرَا بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْعَاكِفِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ ﴿١٢٥﴾ وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ هَٰذَا بَلَدًا آمِنًا وَرَرْقُ أَهْلَهُ مِنَ الثَّمَرَاتِ مَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُم بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ ۖ قَالَ وَمَن كَفَرَ فَأُمَتِّعُهُ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ أَضْطَرُّهُ إِلَىٰ عَذَابِ النَّارِ ۖ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ ﴿١٢٦﴾ وَإِذْ يَرْفَعُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ الْقَوَاعِدَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَإِسْمَاعِيلُ رَبَّنَا تَقَبَّلْ مِنَّا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ﴿١٢٧﴾ رَبَّنَا وَاجْعَلْنَا مُسْلِمَيْنِ لَكَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِنَا أُمَّةً مُّسْلِمَةً لَّكَ وَأَرِنَا مَنَاسِكَنَا وَتُبْ عَلَيْنَا ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٢٨﴾ رَبَّنَا وَابْعَثْ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِّنْهُمْ يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِكَ وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ ۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ ﴿١٢٩﴾
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah (2:120 - 2:129)

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:126-136 SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:126-136 a place of worship. We appointed Abraham and Ishmael to purify My House (the Ka'bah) for those who would encircle it, those who take sanctuary therein, and those who bow down and fall prostrate. 126 Abraham said, "My Lord, make this a land of peace, and provide its people with fruits, provide for those among them who believe in Allāh and the Last Day." God said, "I will also provide for him who disbelieves; I will provide for him temporarily, then I will commit him to the agony of the hellfire and a miserable destiny." 127 As Abraham raised the foundations of the House (the Ka'bah), together with Ishmael, they prayed, "Our Lord, accept (this) from us. Surely, you are the one who is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. 128 Our Lord, make us Muslims (submitters) to You, and from our progeny let there be a nation of Muslims to You.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:126-136

segments.text: Teach us the rituals of worship, and redeem us. Surely, You are the Redeemer, most Merciful. 129 Our Lord, and raise from among them a messenger who would recite to them Your revelations, who would teach them the scripture and wisdom, and purify them. Surely, You are the Almighty, most Wise." (Islam is the One Eternal Message) 130 Who would ever forsake the religion of Abraham, except those who deceive themselves? We have chosen him in this world, and in the hereafter he shall be among the righteous. 131 When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I submit (my will) to the Lord of the universe." 132 Furthermore, Abraham enjoined the same upon his children, and did so Jacob, saying, "O my children, Allāh has pointed out the religion for you. Therefore, die not except as Muslims." 133 Were you witnesses when death came to Jacob?
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:126-136

segments.text: He asked his children, "What will you worship after I die?" They said, "We shall worship your God; the God of your fathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac; the One God. To Him we are Muslims." 134 Such is a community from the past. They have whatever they earned; against them is whatever they committed, and you are not responsible for anything the did. 135 They say, "Be you Jewish, or Christian, to be on the right guidance." Say, "Nay, it is you who should follow the religion of Abraham, the monotheist; he never advocated polytheism." 136 You (believers) shall say, "We believe in God and what was revealed to us, and what was revealed through Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Patriarchs, and what was given to Moses and Jesus, and what 254 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:126-136

segments.text: سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ الجزء الأول (٢) سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ وَمَنْ يَرْغَبُ عَنْ مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ ۚ وَلَقَدِ اصْطَفَيْنَاهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ ﴿١٣٠﴾ إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ أَسْلِمْ ۖ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿١٣١﴾ وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ يَا بَنِيَّ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ الدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿١٣٢﴾ أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ إِذْ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِلَٰهًا وَاحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿١٣٣﴾ تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٣٤﴾ وَقَالُوا كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ تَهْتَدُوا ۗ قُلْ بَلْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا ۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ ﴿١٣٥﴾ قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿١٣٦﴾ فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا ۖ وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا هُمْ فِي شِقَاقٍ ۖ فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ ۚ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ﴿١٣٧﴾ صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ ۖ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً ۖ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ ﴿١٣٨﴾ قُلْ أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ وَلَنَا أَعْمَالُنَا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُخْلِصُونَ ﴿١٣٩﴾ أَمْ تَقُولُونَ إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطَ كَانُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ ۗ قُلْ أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ ۗ وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَتَمَ شَهَادَةً عِنْدَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤٠﴾ تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤١﴾ الجزء الأول (٢) سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ وَمَنْ يَرْغَبُ عَنْ مِلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ إِلَّا مَنْ سَفِهَ نَفْسَهُ ۚ وَلَقَدِ اصْطَفَيْنَاهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا ۖ وَإِنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَةِ لَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ ﴿١٣٠﴾ إِذْ قَالَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ أَسْلِمْ ۖ قَالَ أَسْلَمْتُ لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿١٣١﴾ وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ بَنِيهِ وَيَعْقُوبُ يَا بَنِيَّ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَىٰ لَكُمُ الدِّينَ فَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿١٣٢﴾ أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ إِذْ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلَٰهَكَ وَإِلَٰهَ آبَائِكَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ إِلَٰهًا وَاحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿١٣٣﴾ تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٣٤﴾ وَقَالُوا كُونُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ تَهْتَدُوا ۗ قُلْ بَلْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفًا ۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ ﴿١٣٥﴾ قُولُوا آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰ وَمَا أُوتِيَ النَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ ﴿١٣٦﴾ فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا ۖ وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَإِنَّمَا هُمْ فِي شِقَاقٍ ۖ فَسَيَكْفِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ ۚ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ ﴿١٣٧﴾ صِبْغَةَ اللَّهِ ۖ وَمَنْ أَحْسَنُ مِنَ اللَّهِ صِبْغَةً ۖ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ ﴿١٣٨﴾ قُلْ أَتُحَاجُّونَنَا فِي اللَّهِ وَهُوَ رَبُّنَا وَرَبُّكُمْ وَلَنَا أَعْمَالُنَا وَلَكُمْ أَعْمَالُكُمْ وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُخْلِصُونَ ﴿١٣٩﴾ أَمْ تَقُولُونَ إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطَ كَانُوا هُودًا أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ ۗ قُلْ أَأَنْتُمْ أَعْلَمُ أَمِ اللَّهُ ۗ وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَتَمَ شَهَادَةً عِنْدَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤٠﴾ تِلْكَ أُمَّةٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ ۖ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَلَكُمْ مَا كَسَبْتُمْ ۖ وَلَا تُسْأَلُونَ عَمَّا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤١﴾
segments.label: page - سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:137-146 was given to all the prophets from their Lord; we make no discrimination against any of them, and to Him we are Muslims. 137 If they believe in the same things you believe in, then they shall be rightly guided. But if they turn away, then they are in oppostion. Allah will spare you their opposition; He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. 138 Such is the methodology of Allah, and who has a better methodology than Allah; Him alone do we worship. 139 Say, "Do you argue with us concerning Allah, though He is our Lord as well as your Lord? You have your works and we have our works, and to Him we shall remain sincere. 140 You claim that Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Patriarchs were Jews or Christians; are you more knowledgeable than Allah? Who is more evil than one who conceals a testimony from Allah?
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Allah is never unaware of anything you do. 141 Such is a community from the past. They have whatever they earned; against them is whatever they committed, and you are not responsible for ahything they did. (The Direction of Qiblah as a Test) 142 The unwitting among the people may ask, "Why did they change the Qiblah which they used to face?" Say, "To God belong the East and the West; He directs whomever He wills to the right path." 143 We have thus made you an objective community, that you may bear witness for mankind, just as the messenger bore witness for you. We have set up for you the initial direction of Qiblah only to distinguish those who would still follow the messenger from those who would turn back on their heels. Such was an exacting trial, except for those whom Allah had guided. Allah wastes not your works of faith.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surely, Allah is most Benevolent to mankind, most Merciful. 144 We have seen you turn your face to the heaven (in anticipation of the Qiblah you really desire). Therefore, We herein turn you towards a Qiblah which is pleasing to you, You shall henceforth turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque (mecca), and wherever you may be (O believers) you shall turn your faces towards it. Surely, those who received previous scripture realize that this is the truth from their Lord. Allah is never unaware of anything they do. 145 However, even if you show those who received previous scripture every possible miracle, they will not follow your Qiblah; you shall not follow their Qiblah. They do not even follow each other's Qiblah. Surely, if you ever follow their wishes, after this knowledge has come to you, you would be among the wrong-doers. 256 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) فإن آمنوا بمثل ما آمنتم به فقد اهتدوا ۖ وإن تولوا فإنما هم في شقاق ۖ فسيكفيكهم الله ۚ وهو السميع العليم ... (إلى آخره)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَا وَلَّهُمْ عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا ۚ قُلْ لِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ ۚ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ ﴿١٤٢﴾ وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا ۗ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ ۚ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ ۗ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ ﴿١٤٣﴾ قَدْ نَرَى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ ۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا ۚ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ ۗ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤٤﴾ وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ بِكُلِّ آيَةٍ مَا تَبِعُوا قِبْلَتَكَ ۚ وَمَا أَنْتَ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَتَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا بَعْضُهُمْ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَةَ بَعْضٍ ۚ وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ ۙ إِنَّكَ إِذًا لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ ﴿١٤٥﴾ الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ ۖ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنْهُمْ لَيَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٤٦﴾ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ ۖ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ ﴿١٤٧﴾ وَلِكُلِّ وِجْهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا ۖ فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ ۚ أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ﴿١٤٨﴾ وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۖ وَإِنَّهُ لَلْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤٩﴾ سَيَقُولُ السُّفَهَاءُ مِنَ النَّاسِ مَا وَلَّهُمْ عَنْ قِبْلَتِهِمُ الَّتِي كَانُوا عَلَيْهَا ۚ قُلْ لِلَّهِ الْمَشْرِقُ وَالْمَغْرِبُ ۚ يَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ ﴿١٤٢﴾ وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطًا لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًا ۗ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا الْقِبْلَةَ الَّتِي كُنْتَ عَلَيْهَا إِلَّا لِنَعْلَمَ مَنْ يَتَّبِعُ الرَّسُولَ مِمَّنْ يَنْقَلِبُ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ ۚ وَإِنْ كَانَتْ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ ۗ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَانَكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ ﴿١٤٣﴾ قَدْ نَرَى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّمَاءِ ۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبْلَةً تَرْضَاهَا ۚ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۚ وَحَيْثُ مَا كُنْتُمْ فَوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ شَطْرَهُ ۗ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤٤﴾ وَلَئِنْ أَتَيْتَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ بِكُلِّ آيَةٍ مَا تَبِعُوا قِبْلَتَكَ ۚ وَمَا أَنْتَ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَتَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا بَعْضُهُمْ بِتَابِعٍ قِبْلَةَ بَعْضٍ ۚ وَلَئِنِ اتَّبَعْتَ أَهْوَاءَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ ۙ إِنَّكَ إِذًا لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ ﴿١٤٥﴾ الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ ۖ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنْهُمْ لَيَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٤٦﴾ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ ۖ فَلَا تَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ ﴿١٤٧﴾ وَلِكُلِّ وِجْهَةٌ هُوَ مُوَلِّيهَا ۖ فَاسْتَبِقُوا الْخَيْرَاتِ ۚ أَيْنَ مَا تَكُونُوا يَأْتِ بِكُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ﴿١٤٨﴾ وَمِنْ حَيْثُ خَرَجْتَ فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ شَطْرَ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ ۖ وَإِنَّهُ لَلْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ ۗ وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ ﴿١٤٩﴾

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:147-159 146 Those to whom We have given previous scripture recognize the truth herein just as they recognize their own children. But, surely, some of them conceal the truth knowingly. 147 This is the truth from your Lord; you shall not have any doubts about it. 148 To each is a direction to which he turns, you shall turn eagerly towards the good works. Wherever you might be, Allāh will bring you all. Surely, Allāh is Omnipotent. 149 Wherever you may go (O Muḥammad) you shall turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. This is the truth from your Lord, and Allāh is never unaware of anything you do. 150 Wherever you may go (O Muḥammad) you shall turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you might be (O believers), you shall turn your faces towards it.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Thus, other people will have no argument against you, except those among them who are unjust; do not fear them, and fear Me. Thus do I complete My favors to you, and to render you rightly guided. 151 Other favors included Our raising of a messenger from amongst you to recite for you Our revelations, and to teach you the scripture and the wisdom, and to teach you things you never knew. 152 Therefore, you shall commemorate Me; I will then commemorate you; you shall be thankful to Me; do not be unappreciative. (The Believers Must be Put to the Test) 153 O you who believe, you shall resort to steadfastness and the ṣalāt prayers. Surely, Allāh is with those who steadfastly persevere. 154 Do not consider those who are killed in the cause of Allāh to be dead.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Nay, they are alive, but you perceive not. 155 We will put you to the test by means of some fear, hunger, and loss of monies and lives and crops. Give the good news to those who steadfastly persevere. 156 When a disaster befalls them they say, “We belong to Allāh, and to Him we shall return.” 157 These shall receive exaltations from their Lord, and mercy; these are the rightly guided ones. (Rituals of Ḥajj) 158 The knolls of Ṣafā and Marwah are among the sacred altars of God. Thus, whoever observes the pilgrimage to Mecca, or observe the ‘Umrah visitation, shall encircle them. Whoever volunteers more good works, surely, Allāh is appreciative thereof, fully aware. 159 Surely, those who conceal what We sent down of clear revelations 258 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 259 ٱلۡجُزۡءُ ٱلثَّانِي (٢) سُورَةُ ٱلۡبَقَرَةِ وَمِنۡ حَيۡثُ خَرَجۡتَ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥ لِئَلَّا يَكُونَ لِلنَّاسِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حُجَّةٌ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ مِنۡهُمۡ فَلَا تَخۡشَوُهُمۡ وَٱخۡشَوۡنِي وَلِأُتِمَّ نِعۡمَتِي عَلَيۡكُمۡ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ (١٥٠) كَمَا أَرۡسَلۡنَا فِيكُمۡ رَسُولاً مِّنۡكُمۡ يَتْلُواْ عَلَيۡكُمۡ ءَايَاتِنَا وَيُزَكِّيكُمۡ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمُ ٱلۡكِتَابَ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةَ وَيُعَلِّمُكُمۡ مَّا لَمۡ تَكُونُواْ تَعۡلَمُونَ (١٥١) فَاذۡكُرُونِي أَذۡكُرۡكُمۡ وَٱشۡكُرُواْ لِي وَلَا تَكۡفُرُونِ (١٥٢) يَٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱسۡتَعِينُواْ بِٱلصَّبۡرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّهَ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ (١٥٣) وَلَا تَقُولُواْ لِمَن يُقۡتَلُ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللهِ أَمۡوَٰتٌۢۚ بَلۡ أَحۡيَاءٌ وَلَٰكِن لَّا تَشۡعُرُونَ (١٥٤) وَلَنَبۡلُوَنَّكُم بِشَيۡءٍ مِّنَ ٱلۡخَوۡفِ وَٱلۡجُوعِ وَنَقۡصٍ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَمۡوَٰلِ وَٱلۡأَنفُسِ وَٱلثَّمَرَٰتِۗ وَبَشِّرِ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ (١٥٥) ٱلَّذِينَ إِذَآ أَصَابَتۡهُم مُّصِيبَةٌ قَالُواْ إِنَّا لِلهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيۡهِ رَٰجِعُونَ (١٥٦) أُولُوۡنَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَلَوَٰتٌ مِّن رَّبِّهِمۡ وَرَحۡمَةٌۖ وَأُولُوۡكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُهۡتَدُونَ (١٥٧) إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللهِۖ فَمَن حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡراً فَإِنَّ ٱللهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ (١٥٨) إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡتُمُونَ مَآ أَنزَلۡنَا مِنَ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلۡهُدَىٰ مِن بَعۡدِ مَا بَيَّنَّاهُ لِلنَّاسِ فِي ٱلۡكِتَابِ أُولُوۡكَ يَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللهُ وَيَلۡعَنُهُمُ ٱللَّٰعِنُونَ (١٥٩)
segments.label: page - Surah Al-Baqarah

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:160-171 and guidance, after We have clarified them for mankind in this scripture, these shall be cursed by Allāh; they shall be cursed by all who curse. 160 Only those who repent, reform, and declare this scripture, I will redeem them; for I am the Redeemer, most Merciful. 161 As for those who disbelieve, and die as disbelievers, they merit but the curse of Allāh, the angels, and all mankind. 162 Eternally they abide therein; neither their punishment can be commuted, nor shall they be granted respite. 163 Your God is One God.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: There is no good except He, the most Compassionate, most Merciful. (The Overwhelming Evidence of God) 164 Certainly, the creation of the heavens and the earth; the alternation of night and day; the ships which roam the sea for the benefit of mankind; the water which Allāh sends down from the sky to revive dead land therwith and spread in it all kinds of creatures; the manipulation of the winds; the clouds which are placed between the sky and the earth; all these are signs for the people who understand. 165 Yet, some people set up rivals to rank with Allāh, and even love them as if they were Allāh. But those who believe are much more sincere in their love of Allāh. If only the wrong-doers could envision the pun- ishment which awaits them?
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: They shall then realize that all power belongs to Allāh, and that Allāh is strict in retribution. 166 Those who followed shall then disown their followers; they shall see the punishment, and all their ties shall be severed. 167 Those who had followed shall say, “If only we could go back, we would disown them as they now disown us.” Thus does Allāh show them the consequences of their works; nothing but regrets. They shall never get out of the hellfire. (All Good Food is Lawful) 168 O mankind, eat from the earth that which is lawful and good.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Do not follow the steps of Satan, for surely he is your ardent enemy. 169 He only enjoins upon you evil and vice, and to say about Allāh what you know not. 170 Thus, when it is said to them, “Follow what Allāh sent down,” they say, “Nay, we follow only what we found our parents doing.” What if their parents lacked any understanding, and were never guided? 171 The similitude of those who disbelieve is like one who parrots whatever he hears without comprehension. They are deaf, dumb, and blind; they can never understand. 260 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) أولئك أهون عليهم... (partial right margin Quranic text)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Al-Baqarah [2:160-167] إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَأَصْلَحُوا وَبَيَّنُوا فَأُولَئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنَا التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٦٠﴾ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ ﴿١٦١﴾ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ ﴿١٦٢﴾ وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٦٣﴾ إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ ﴿١٦٤﴾ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْدَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ ﴿١٦٥﴾ إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبَابُ ﴿١٦٦﴾ وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُوا مِنَّا كَذَلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ حَسَرَاتٍ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا هُمْ بِخَارِجِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ ﴿١٦٧﴾ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا وَأَصْلَحُوا وَبَيَّنُوا فَأُولَئِكَ أَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنَا التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٦٠﴾ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ ﴿١٦١﴾ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ ﴿١٦٢﴾ وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ ﴿١٦٣﴾ إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَاخْتِلَافِ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ وَالْفُلْكِ الَّتِي تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِمَا يَنْفَعُ النَّاسَ وَمَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَا وَبَثَّ فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ دَابَّةٍ وَتَصْرِيفِ الرِّيَاحِ وَالسَّحَابِ الْمُسَخَّرِ بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَآيَاتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَعْقِلُونَ ﴿١٦٤﴾ وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْدَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَشَدُّ حُبًّا لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا إِذْ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ أَنَّ الْقُوَّةَ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعًا وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعَذَابِ ﴿١٦٥﴾ إِذْ تَبَرَّأَ الَّذِينَ اتُّبِعُوا مِنَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا وَرَأَوُا الْعَذَابَ وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبَابُ ﴿١٦٦﴾ وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوا لَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْهُمْ كَمَا تَبَرَّءُوا مِنَّا كَذَلِكَ يُرِيهِمُ اللَّهُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ حَسَرَاتٍ عَلَيْهِمْ وَمَا هُمْ بِخَارِجِينَ مِنَ النَّارِ ﴿١٦٧﴾
segments.label: page - Al-Baqarah [2:160-167]

segments.text: SURA AL-BAQARAH SURA AL-BAQARAH 2:172-180 (Prohibited Meats) 172 O you who believe, eat from the good things We provided for you, and be thankful to Allāh if you sincerely worship Him. 173 He only prohibits for you the meat of dead animals, the blood, the meat of swine, and the meat which is dedicated to other than Allāh. However, if one is forced to eat these, without being malicious or deliberate, commits no sin. Surely, Allāh is Forgiver, most Merciful. 174 Those who conceal what Allāh has revealed in this scripture, and trade it away for a cheap material gain, they eat into their bellies but fire; Allāh will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they shall suffer a painful punishment. 175 It is they who chose the straying over the guidance, and the punishment over the forgiveness.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Therefore, they will have to endure the hellfire. 176 That, because Allāh sent down this scripture bearing the Truth; those who dispute this scripture are in extreme error. (The Definition of Righteousness) 177 Righteousness is not simply turning your faces towards the East or the West (in ṣalāt); but righteousness is to believe in Allāh, the Last Day, the angels, the scripture, and the prophets, and to donate the money, despite one's love thereof, to the relatives, the poor, the alien, the beggars, and for the liberation of slaves, and to observe the ṣalāt prayers and the Zakāt charity, and to fufill the promises whenever they are made, and to steadfastly persevere in the face of adversity, hardship, and war.
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: These are the truthful; these are the pious. (The Punishment for Murder) 178 O you who believe, ordained for you herein is commensuration when imposing the maximum punishment for murder; the free person for the free person, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. However, if the guilty is pardoned by the victim's kin, then he shall pay an equitable compensation. This is an alleviation from your Lord and mercy. Whoever transgresses these limits shall suffer a painful retribution. 179 Commensuration shall be a life-saving law for you, O you who possess understanding, that you may achieve piety. (A Will Shall be Written Before Death) 180 It is ordained for you herein that when death approaches the one of you, if he is to leave any wealth behind, a will shall be made for the sake of the parents and relatives equitably. This is an obligation on those who are pious. 262 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - SURA AL-BAQARAH

segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah [2:168-176] الجزء الثاني (٢) سورة البقرة يَأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ (١٦٨) إِنَّمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوءِ وَالْفَحْشَاءِ وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٦٩) وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ (١٧٠) وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ (١٧١) يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِلَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ (١٧٢) إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغِ وَلَا عَادٍ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٧٣) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَشْتَرُونَ بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُولَئِكَ مَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ إِلَّا النَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٤) أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى وَالْعَذَابَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ (١٧٥) ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِي الْكِتَابِ لَفِي شِقَاقٍ بَعِيدٍ (١٧٦) ٢٠ ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 263 يَأَيُّهَا النَّاسُ كُلُوا مِمَّا فِي الْأَرْضِ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا خُطُوَاتِ الشَّيْطَانِ إِنَّهُ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ مُّبِينٌ (١٦٨) إِنَّمَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالسُّوءِ وَالْفَحْشَاءِ وَأَنْ تَقُولُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ (١٦٩) وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اتَّبِعُوا مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ قَالُوا بَلْ نَتَّبِعُ مَا أَلْفَيْنَا عَلَيْهِ آبَاءَنَا أَوَلَوْ كَانَ آبَاؤُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ (١٧٠) وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي يَنْعِقُ بِمَا لَا يَسْمَعُ إِلَّا دُعَاءً وَنِدَاءً صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ فَهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ (١٧١) يَأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُلُوا مِنْ طَيِّبَاتِ مَا رَزَقْنَاكُمْ وَاشْكُرُوا لِلَّهِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ (١٧٢) إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْمَيْتَةَ وَالدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ وَمَا أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغِ وَلَا عَادٍ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٧٣) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْتُمُونَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَشْتَرُونَ بِهِ ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا أُولَئِكَ مَا يَأْكُلُونَ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ إِلَّا النَّارَ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٤) أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الضَّلَالَةَ بِالْهُدَى وَالْعَذَابَ بِالْمَغْفِرَةِ فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ (١٧٥) ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّ الَّذِينَ اخْتَلَفُوا فِي الْكِتَابِ لَفِي شِقَاقٍ بَعِيدٍ (١٧٦)

segments.text: Surat Al-Baqarah الجزء الثاني (٢) سُورَةُ البَقَرَةِ لَيْسَ الْبِرَّ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا وُجُوهَكُمْ قِبَلَ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَلَكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنْ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالْكِتَابِ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ وَآتَى الْمَالَ عَلَى حُبِّهِ ذَوِي الْقُرْبَى وَالْيَتَامَى وَالْمَسَاكِينَ وَابْنَ السَّبِيلِ وَالسَّائِلِينَ وَفِي الرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَى الزَّكَاةَ وَالْمُوفُونَ بِعَهْدِهِمْ إِذَا عَاهَدُوا وَالصَّابِرِينَ فِي الْبَأْسَاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ وَحِينَ الْبَأْسِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ (١٧٧) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِصَاصُ فِي الْقَتْلَى الْحُرُّ بِالْحُرِّ وَالْعَبْدُ بِالْعَبْدِ وَالْأُنْثَى بِالْأُنْثَى فَمَنْ عُفِيَ لَهُ مِنْ أَخِيهِ شَيْءٌ فَاتِّبَاعٌ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَأَدَاءٌ إِلَيْهِ بِإِحْسَانٍ ذَلِكَ تَخْفِيفٌ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَرَحْمَةٌ فَمَنِ اعْتَدَى بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ فَلَهُ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ (١٧٨) وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصَاصِ حَيَاةٌ يَا أُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ (١٧٩) كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِذَا حَضَرَ أَحَدَكُمُ الْمَوْتُ إِنْ تَرَكَ خَيْراً الْوَصِيَّةُ لِلْوَالِدَيْنِ وَالْأَقْرَبِينَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ حَقّاً عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ (١٨٠) فَمَنْ بَدَّلَهُ بَعْدَمَا سَمِعَهُ فَإِنَّمَا إِثْمُهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ يُبَدِّلُونَهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١٨١) فَمَنْ خَافَ مِنْ مُوصٍ جَنَفاً أَوْ إِثْماً فَأَصْلَحَ بَيْنَهُمْ فَلَا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٨٢) يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ segments.text: Surah Al-Baqarah (2):184-187 Al-Baqarah (2): 184-187 أَيَّامًا مَّعْدُودَاتٍ ۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكم مَّرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۚ وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيْرًا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّهُ ۚ وَأَن تَصُومُوا خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿١٨٤﴾ شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ هُدًى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَاتٍ مِّنَ الْهُدَىٰ وَالْفُرْقَانِ ۚ فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ الشَّهْرَ فَلْيَصُمْهُ ۖ وَمَن كَانَ مَرِيضًا أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ فَعِدَّةٌ مِّنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ ۗ يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ بِكُمُ الْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ الْعُسْرَ وَلِتُكْمِلُوا الْعِدَّةَ وَلِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا هَدَاكُمْ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿١٨٥﴾ وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا لِي وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا بِي لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ ﴿١٨٦﴾ أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ الصِّيَامِ الرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَائِكُمْ ۚ هُنَّ لِبَاسٌ لَّكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ لِبَاسٌ لَّهُنَّ ۗ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ أَنَّكُمْ كُنتُمْ تَخْتَانُونَ أَنفُسَكُمْ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَعَفَا عَنكُمْ ۖ فَالْآنَ بَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَابْتَغُوا مَا كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۚ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ مِنَ الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ مِنَ الْفَجْرِ ۖ ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيَامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ ۚ وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ ۗ تِلْكَ حُدُودُ اللَّهِ فَلَا تَقْرَبُوهَا ۗ كَذَلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ لِلنَّاسِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ ﴿١٨٧﴾

segments.text: 1395/1975: An Historical Year 1395/1975: An Historical Year Praise be to Allāh, Lord of the Universe; the most Compassionate, most Merciful, and may Allāh bestow peace and blessings on His beloved messenger Muḥammad. The journal ISLAM will not be published during the year 1395/1975 in order to devote all our editorial efforts and full resources and capabilities to the final stage in the production of an historical first, namely, THE FIRST QUR’ANIC TRANSLATION BY A MUSLIM SCHOLAR WHOSE MOTHER TONGUE IS ARABIC. This final stage represents the culmination of many years of painstaking effort and dedicated exertion to produce an English rendering of the Qur’an’s meanings as accurately as humanly possible; a rendering which is worthy of God’s finalized and completed message to all mankind.
segments.label: page - 1395/1975: An Historical Year

segments.text: Realizing the awesome responsibility inherent in translating and/or interpreting God’s message, the Arab Muslim scholars of the past 1400 years have shied away from this great undertaking. Thus, though it is the ruling constitution in the lives of millions of English-speaking Muslims, the Qur’an was never previously translated into English by a Muslim Arab. The evident errors, inaccuracies, deficiencies, and inconsistencies common to the presently available translations have been a source of frustration and disappointment for the English-speaking students of the Qur’an. In spite of the admirable life-time efforts of such great Muslim scholars as ‘Abdullah Yūsuf ‘Ali and Muḥammad Marmaduke Pickthall, it is no secret that their renderings did not capture the spirit of the ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 267

segments.text: My beloved: Do not argue with others in defense of the truth. All you need to do is declare it. You are not responsible for their rejection of the truth; if they accept it, then Allah has blessed them; if they reject it, you are not liable. Salāmah b. Ḥasan Al-Rāḍī Faith is necessary for religions, but it ceases to be so for those who go further and who achieve self-realization in God. Then one no longer believes because one sees. There is no longer any need to believe, when one sees the Truth. Ahmad b. Muṣṭafā Al-‘Alawī 270 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)

segments.text: The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī: 3 Islamic Concentrates The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī: 3 These aphorisms, with their esoteric connotations, are derived from the Qur'an, the sunna, teachings of the great imams, and the principles of Sufism. Published for the first time in English, these particular aphorisms are valuable pieces of advice delivered by one of the greatest Sufis of all time, Shaykh Salāmah Al-Rāḍī, to his dervishes. 31. My beloved: Once you achieve absolute slavery to Allah, you become masters of your surroundings; you say to anything, "Be," and it is. Once you eliminate your ego, and live totally devoted to your Lord, everything obeys you. 32. My beloved: If you become filled with the love of Allah, all things will go your way: you simply wish for anything, and it comes true. 33.
segments.label: page - The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī: 3

segments.text: My beloved: Your Master treats you in the like of your treatment of Him; If you remember Him, He remembers you; If you long for Him, He longs for you; If you hasten to please Him, He hastens to please you. Accorkingly, judge your position with Him for yourselves. 34. My beloved: If you care only for your own desires, and fail to control them, you may not be admitted into the court of your Master. Moses had said, "My Lord, how can I reach you?" God said, "Abandon your ego and come." 35. My beloved: Your monies and your children are favors from Allah to you for as long as they do not divert you away from your Master; If you abandon your Master in their favor, they become but a disastrous curse. 36. My beloved: If your hearts are purged from loving anything besides your Master, He grants you a restful worldly life; only a minimum of worldly work will sustain you. Otherwise, you will have a life of hard labor. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) : 271-275
segments.label: page - The Aphorisms of Salāmah Al-Rāḍī: 3

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 37. My beloved: So long as the ego remains alive, the heart remains dead. Therefore, you shall revive your hearts by killing your egos; the heart is the abode of the Lord, most Glorified, most High. 38. My beloved: If you wish to avoid the opposition of anyone, you shall not compete with him for the things he loves. 39. My beloved: If you wish to achieve a high rank, do not claim for yourselves any rank. And, if anyone claims for himself a rank above you, do not dispute him, and allow him such a claim. As a consequence, you will taste the genuine sweetness of Īmān and Allah will fill your hearts with light. 40. My beloved: Whenever anyone transgresses against you, you shall attribute your troubles to your sinful deeds, and see that Allah is the One who punishes you.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: Do not seek revenge, nor shall you pray to Allah against your enemy. You shall be pardoners, for the beloved Prophet (blessings of Allah and peace be upon him) said, "The pardoners shall be the winners." 41. My beloved: You shall avoid all forms of show-off for it renders your efforts a servitude to other than Allah. Your Master needs not any of your deeds, and when you do anything for the show-off, He will not accept your works, saying, "Take your recompense from whomever you showed off your works." 42. My beloved: Our works are filled with deficiencies and insincerity; they are not worthy of the Almighty. How then can we pride ourselves with that which is defective? We can only turn to Allah in hopeful anticipation that out of His abundant grace, He might accept our works despite the defects therein. 43.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: My beloved: Directing your attention to the purgation of your hearts is much more important than preoccupying yourselves with the collection of knowledge; Purging your hearts will open the doors of Divine knowledge for you, and the knowledge will come to you in its pristine purity, unadulterated. 44. My beloved: Whenever you speak of anything, you shall speak of the good qualities, rather than the bad qualities thereof. The mentioning of bad qualities is itself a bad quality, and you may become so accustomed to seeing bad qualities that you end up believing that everthing must have bad qualities. 272 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 45. My beloved: Your bodies are vehicles, while your souls are the drivers thereof; Let not the vehicles take you to what angers your Master; they are driven only by your souls. 46. My beloved: The real affliction is to turn away from Allah, and the real disease is that of skeptic hearts. Thus whenever you see such afflictions in others, you shall ask Allah to grant you health, and to alleviate their afflictions. 47. My beloved: Seeking the materials of this world, as a sole objective, leads away from Allah, and results ultimately in spiritual death. Thus, regretting the loss of worldly materials would be like regretting the loss of a poisonous snake. 48. My beloved: Turning away from materialism and towards Allah is the key you need for opening your hearts; when one lacks this key, his heart remains locked. 49.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: My beloved: This worldly life is an attractive illusion; who ever rejoices over material gains therefrom actually rejoices over that which diverts his heart and takes him away from his Lord. 50. My beloved: When you turn on your physical senses, you simultaneously turn off your spiritual senses; this leads to blindness of the soul. Therefore, you shall strive to open your spiritual eye which sees the Divine dominion, by keeping the physical eye from preoccupation with the worldly dominion. 51. My beloved: The people are of varied qualities, and when you associate yourselves with the evil ones, your souls become adulterated; this in turn leads to spiritual sickness and misery for you. 52. My beloved: If you find sweetness in the taste of everything which emanates from your beloved Master, then you have achieved genuine steadfastness.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: But if you find some of His givings to be sweet and some to be sour, then this indicates a deficiency in your love. When you taste sourness from the beloved Master, this reflects your objection, and the lack of total submission to Him. 53. My beloved: If you love two entities, your heart would be divided in two; each half would compete with the other for complete dominance. This will at least dim the brightness of your love, and the beloved Master requires pure, undivided, attention. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 273
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 54. My beloved: The human being is an animal by his body; an angel or a devil by his soul. The wise among you would reflect and judge whether he wants to be an animal, a devil, or a pure angel. 55. My beloved: The capital of each one of you is right here in this world; whoever wastes away his capital, how could he make any profit? 56. My beloved: This worldly life is like the Suq market (operates only on a specific day of the week); if one misses the market, where will he sell his goods? 57. My beloved: However you live in this world, so will be your life in the Hereafter; you shall reflect and determine for yourselves whether your life here is in the blessings and pleasure of Allah, or are you incurring His anger (God forbid)? 58.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: My beloved: The character of the human being is the garment of his soul; you shall reflect and note whether your soul's garment is clean, pure, and lighted, or dirty, dark, and vile. 59. My beloved: If the one of you is told that a scorpion got into his garment, he would immediately take it off or tear it off to get rid of the scorpion. Inside each one of us we have the various lusts which continue to sting our hearts without invoking a reaction from us. 60. My beloved: The grave is your inevitable abode; you shall strive to make it a spacious, and well-lighted abode. If your present spiritual abode is spacious and well-lighted, so will your graves. 61. My beloved: If you are impressed by good deeds, you should first fetch the sincerity therein; if you do not find it, then discount them as good deeds. 62. My beloved: Your works are but ghosts; their real life and light are in the hearts.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: If the heart accompanies your good works, they would be of value; otherwise, they will be life-less, light-less. 63. My beloved; If you become too impatient with humbleness, then you should realize that your ego is trying to take you out from the courtship of Allah. Beware lest it succeeds in dismissing you from the Divine courtship. 64. My beloved: Once you become fully content with your Lord, your command becomes His command, and your deeds become solely in His name; nothing will disobey you. If your "self" expresses its own wishes, this 274 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3 would reflect a defective heart; then nothing will obey you or go your way. 65. My beloved: If you wish to progress along the path of humbleness, you shall keep company with the people of humbleness until you are genuinely humble on your own. Afterwards, you may mix with all kinds of people. Those who keep company with other than the people of humbleness, before being genuinely humble on their own, will be like one who tries to light a feeble candle in the midst of a violent storm. 66. My beloved: The breath of the human being who is in a state of obedience to Allah is but light, and the light is accompanied by angels; if he is in a sinful state, every breath is but darkness, and the darkness is accompanied by devils. The light emanating from each of you, or the darkness, surrounds you.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: Thus, look around you and find out whether you are surrounded by light and angels, or darkness and devils. 67. My beloved: As you like the people to treat you, so shall be your treatment of them; what you dislike from the people, let them not see coming from you. He who expects the people to treat him better than he treats them is utterly unjust; he who does what others dislike deserves mal-treatment; he who does things for which he later apologizes may not someday find a valid excuse, and if he does, his excuse may not be accepted. 68. My beloved: Do not argue with others in defense of the truth. All you need to do is declare it. You are not responsible for their rejection of the truth; if they accept it, then Allah has blessed them; if they reject it, you are not liable. 69. My beloved: So long as your hearts are totally devoted to your Master, you continue to reside in His courtship.
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: Once they become fond of anything else, they become deprived of His courtship. You shall watch your hearts very carefully lest they love other than your Master. 70. My beloved: Once you taste the sweetness of Īmān (unshakeable faith), you lose the taste for this worldly life. Any heart which actually enjoys the taste of this life is forbidden from tasting the sweetness of Īmān. 275 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE APHORISMS OF SALĀMAH AL-RĀDĪ : 3

segments.text: Sūrat Muḥammad سورة محمد (٤٧) سُورَةُ مُحَمَّدٍ مَدَنِيَّةٌ الآية ١٣ نزلت في الطريق أثناء الهجرة وآياتها ٣٨ نزلت بعد الحديد بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ ﴿١﴾ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَآمَنُوا بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ ﴿٢﴾ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْبَاطِلَ وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثَالَهُمْ ﴿٣﴾ IN THE NAME OF GOD, THE COMPASSIONATE, THE MERCIFUL Those who disbelieve and divert others from the path of Allah, God will render their work but vain. As for those who believe and do good works; those who believe in what was revealed through Muḥammad (for it is the truth from their Lord), God will remit their sins and care for them. That, because those who disbelieve follow but falsehood, while those who believe follow the truth from their Lord.
segments.label: page - Sūrat Muḥammad

segments.text: Thus does God set the examples for mankind. (Qur'an 47:1-3) 276 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) سورة محمد (٤٧) سُورَةُ مُحَمَّدٍ مَدَنِيَّةٌ الآية ١٣ نزلت في الطريق أثناء الهجرة وآياتها ٣٨ نزلت بعد الحديد بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَصَدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أَضَلَّ أَعْمَالَهُمْ ﴿١﴾ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَآمَنُوا بِمَا نُزِّلَ عَلَى مُحَمَّدٍ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَفَّرَ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ وَأَصْلَحَ بَالَهُمْ ﴿٢﴾ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْبَاطِلَ وَأَنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّبَعُوا الْحَقَّ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ كَذَلِكَ يَضْرِبُ اللَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ أَمْثَالَهُمْ ﴿٣﴾
segments.label: page - Sūrat Muḥammad

segments.text: The Invocations of ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī : 3 Islamic Concentrates The Invocations of ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī : 3 ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī, a famous Persian Sufi, was born in Herat 396 AH (1005 C.E.). It is said that one of his ancestors was a companion of the prophet Muhammad (God's blessings and peace be upon him) who moved to Herat with ʿAṣāf, son of Qays. Anṣārī's father, Abu Manṣūr Muḥammad Anṣārī, became a permanent resident of Herat. These invocations, translated into English by Sir Jogendra Singh, contain true advice to guide the Pilgrim along the path of discipleship to the temple of peace. They come from a man who himself had trodden the path and found what his heart desired. When ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī departed from this world, he was 85 years old, leaving behind a wealth of Sufi knowledge.
segments.label: page - The Invocations of ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī : 3

segments.text: Among his well-known works are Risāla Munājāt (The Book of Prayer), Tabaqat-ul-Ṣūfiyyah (The Book of Sufis), Zād-ul-ʿĀrifīn (Provisions of the Sufi Teachers), and Kitāb-i-Isrār (The Book of Mysteries). My friend, make an effort, That thou mayest become a man, And gather treasures Of feeling for others, So that with the favour of saints And by the blessings of waiting on them Thy cheeks may grow pale, And love of the world grow Cold in thy heart. If thou wishest to become a man In the world, In the path of religion Learn to feel for others, Night and day attend on holy men. When thou hast become like dust Of their feet Thou shalt become a man. 277 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) : 277-282
segments.label: page - The Invocations of ʿAbdullāh Anṣārī : 3

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 O man, remember death at all times; Renounce all discord and tyranny; Deem what has not been done as done, And what has been done as not done. Watch vigilantly the state of Thine own mind. Love of God begins in Harmlessness. Know that the Prophet built an external Kaba Of clay and water, And an inner Kaba in life and heart. The outer Kaba was built by Abraham, The Holy; The inner is sanctified by the glory of God Himself. On the path of God Two places of worship mark the stages. The material temple, And the temple of the heart. Make your best endeavour To worship at the temple of the heart. O mendicant, paradise is only an Allurement; The real objective is The house of God Himself.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: Fasting only means the saving of bread, Formal prayer is the business Of old men and women, Pilgrimage is a pleasure of the world. Conquer the heart, Its subjection is conquest indeed. If thou canst walk on water Thou art no better than a straw. If thou canst fly in air Thou art no better than a fly. Conquer thy heart That thou mayest become somebody. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 278
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 One man spends seventy years in learning And fails to kindle the light. Another, all his life learns nothing But hears one word And is consumed by that word. On this path argument is of no avail; Seek, and thou mayest find the truth. Helpless in childhood, Intoxicated in youth, And decrepit in old age; Then, O helpless one, when couldst thou Worship God? Alas! alas, for the master-craftman's ways: From the same iron he forges a horse-shoe As well as a mirror for the Emperor. My friend, see thine own faults; The faults of others, For thee they are not. Make thy heart forgiving; Nor sell thy soul for the fruits of the world. It is wrong to consider oneself above all others And to exalt one's self. Learn from the pupil of thine eye To see others, but to thyself be blind.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: Know friend, Human sorrow springs from three things: To want before it is due, To want more than the destined share, To want for oneself What belongs to others. When Providence has provided thy share Separately from others Then why art thou jealous, And hungering for that which is not for thee? Desire for knowledge is the path Of honour; Desire for wealth, that of dishonour. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 279
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 Wealth is the chain which slaves wear Knowledge the kingly crown. The path is narrow and beset by Yawning chasms. Woe to him who is heavily laden with sin And walks without the light of faith. He with whom virtue has become a habit, Hath accomplished his work here, And hereafter. The law of life requires: 1. Sincerity to God. 2. Severity to self. 3. Justice to all people. 4. Service to elders. 5. Kindness to the young. 6. Generosity to the poor. 7. Good counsel to friends. 8. Forbearance with enemies. 9. Indifference to fools. 10. Respect to the learned. Know that four things are symbols of Ill luck: Ingratitude in good fortune, Impatience in ill fortune, Discontent with what fate ordains, Hesitation in serving fellow-men. In this path, be a man With a heart full of compassion.
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: Engage not in vain doing, Make not thy home in the street of lust and desire. If thou wouldst become a pilgrim on the path Of love The first condition is That thou become as humble as dust And ashes. Remove “A” from “Murad” (desire) it becomes Murd (man); He who renounceth desire becometh a man. 280 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF 'ABDULLAH ANSĀRĪ : 3 THE INVOCATIONS OF 'ABDULLAH ANSĀRĪ : 3 Know that he who desires the things of the World Is haunted by sorrow. He who desires Heaven Is a labourer working for wages. But, he who desires God, Is on the path of glory. O thou who covetest the world How long wilt thou follow the path of sorrow? Even if thou seekest the pleasures of Heaven Thy quest is on the wrong trail. But if thou seekest God and receivest His seal, Thou art victorious in both the worlds. Know, that when thou learnest to lose thyself Thou wilt reach the Beloved. There is no other secret to be revealed, And more than this is not known to me. Be humble and cultivate silence. If thou hast received, rejoice, And fill thyself with ecstasy And if not, continue the demand. Be a rose and not a thorn! Be a friend and not an enemy!
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF 'ABDULLAH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: To exalt the Beloved is to practise religion; To exalt the self is to practise paganism. If the seeker is worthy Attainment is easy. The company of a good friend Is the light of the soul. The company of an ungodly person Is the poison of life. A snake is preferable to a faithless friend. Were I to abide in fire a hundred Years That scorching flame would be easier to bear Than the company of Godless men; Death is preferable to such company. ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4) 281
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF 'ABDULLAH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3 What is worship? To realise reality. What is the sacred law? To do no evil. What is reality? Selflessness. The heart enquired of the soul What is the beginning of this business? What its end, and what its fruit? The soul answered: The beginning of it is The annihilation of self, Its end faithfulness, And its fruit immortality. The heart asked what is annihilation? What is faithfulness? What is immortality? The soul answered: Freedom from self is annihilation; Faithfulness is Fulfilment of love; Immortality is union of immortal With mortal. O Devotee, if thou lovest God truly Why dost thou cast longing eyes On things other than Him? In this path the eye must cease to see, And the ear to hear. Save unto Him, and about Him. Be as dust on His path, Even the kings of this earth Make the dust of His feet. The balm of their eyes. 282 ISLAM 1395/1975 1(3-4)
segments.label: page - THE INVOCATIONS OF ‘ABDULLĀH ANSĀRĪ : 3

segments.text: The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 3 (Hijra / Gregorian) Islamic Concentrates The Islamic Calendar Conversion Table : 3 (Hijra / Gregorian) Over the first five issues of ISLAM, the Journal will publish this table for convenient conversion of dates from either of the two calendar systems. Such chronological conversion tables have been difficult to find yet most indispensible for the Western scholar of Islam. Since all great works of Islamic literature refer exclusively to Hijra dates, the Editors feel that these tables will be useful to many readers. According to the historians, the prophet Muḥammad (God's blessings be upon him) arrived at Medina on the 12th day of Rabi‘ I, coincident with September 24, 622 CE (Christian Era). This sets the first day of the first Hijra year (Muharram 1, 1) as July 16, 622. Fifteen hundred Hijra years will be covered in these tables (622-2076 CE).

segments.text: IN THE NAME OF ALLAH, THE MOST COMPASSIONATE, MOST MERCIFUL They say, “The Almighty has begotten a son!” Indeed, you have committed a gross error. The heavens almost disintegrate, the earth almost shatters, and the mountains almost crumble, because they attribute a son unto the Almighty. It never befits the Almighty that He begets a son. Everyone in the heavens and the earth is no more than a slave of the Almighty. He has counted as such each and everyone. All shall come to Him on the Day of Resurrection as helpless individuals. As for those who believe and do good works, the Almighty will bestow on them love.

segments.text: About the Author About the Author Dr. Rashād Khalifa was born in the midst of the highly spiritual and mystical world of Egyptian Sufism. His spiritual teacher, ‘Abdul-Ḥalīm Khalifa, grand Shaykh of Tarīqat Al-Rashād Al-Shāziliyya, is also his physical father. From his early childhood right through young manhood, the author was a constant companion of his father during his evangelistic missions across Egypt. He was also a constant participant in the nightly “Zikr” sessions led by his teacher/father. The climax of his Sufi indoctrination took place in Mecca (1391 AH; 1971 AD), where he was officially initiated into the chain of Sufi deputies. The first link in this chain is acknowledged by all Sufis to be the initiation of ‘Ali ibn Abī-Ṭālib by the Prophet Muḥammad (May God exalt him and bless him). From that initial indoctrination, the present schools of Sufism have evolved. Dr.
segments.label: page - About the Author

segments.text: Khalifa belongs to the school of Sufism which advocates not only full participation in the worldly life, but also transforming the daily worldly affairs into a form of worship. This concept was first adopted by the great imam of Sufism ‘Ali ibn ‘Abdillah, better known as Abul-Ḥasan Al-Shāzily (593-656 AH; ca 1195-1257 AD). In keeping with this concept, Shaykh ‘Abdul-Ḥalīm Khalifa is a retired engineer who spent 40 years in the employ of the Egyptian government. His spiritual teacher, the famed Shaykh Salāma Al-Rāḍy (1284-1357 AH; 1867-1939 AD) also served the Egyptian government as an accountant. These two great Sufi leaders, and many vii
segments.label: page - About the Author

segments.text: others who belong to Al-Shāzily's school, were dedicated, efficient, workers at their jobs. The only complaint by their worldly “superiors” had to do with the crowds of students and dervishes who waited by the government buildings' entrances every morning and afternoon. The author of this book followed the footsteps of his spiritual teachers. After going to the Qur'an school commonly known in Egypt as “Kuttāb,” Dr. Khalifa attended the public primary and secondary schools of his home town, Ṭanṭā. He went to Cairo for his college education, and when he graduated from the University of ‘Ain Shams’ Faculty of Agriculture in 1957, he ranked the first of his graduating class. This qualified him for a scholarship to study in the USA.
segments.label: page

segments.text: He attended the University of Arizona (1959-1961), where he obtained the M.Sc. degree, and the University of California, Riverside (1962-1964), where he earned the Ph.D. His major field of study was Plant Biochemistry. He worked for the University of California (1964-1966), the Egyptian government (1966-1968), and Monsanto Company (1968-1970). Since 1970, he has been a research scientist with the Food Biochemistry group at Anheuser-Busch, Inc. As a senior member of the Central Research Department, he is searching for new sources of foods and food ingredients as part of the universal effort to feed the world's growing populations. During the past ten years, Dr. Khalifa has been an active member of the Muslim Students Association of the United States and Canada, the Federation of Islamic viii

segments.text: Associations, and the Muslim community of greater St. Louis. He founded the first Muslim Students Association at the University of Arizona in 1960, and participated in establishing the first Islamic Society of Riverside, California. He served as secretary for the Association of Muslim Scientists and Engineers in North America during 1972 and 1973. In May 1972, he founded Islamic Productions International, Inc., aiming at “delivering the Message” to the English-speaking world. By means of these activities, Dr. Khalifa is maintaining the modern Sufi traditions of his spiritual teachers ‘Abdul-Ḥalīm Khalīfa, Salāma Al-Rāḍy, and Abul-Ḥasan Al-Shāzily.

segments.text: Introduction Introduction Many people find themselves today in a position similar to that of the prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) some 4,000 years ago: believing, but in need of reassurance. This is so especially in an age when science has been employed almost exclusively for materialistic and faith-shattering purposes. Such science has allegedly discovered a plethora of evidence "proving" that there is no God, no Revelation, no afterlife, and that therefore man and the world are but the result of purposeless chance and mindless evolution. When scientific substantiation appears to be overwhelmingly on the side of the materialists, atheists, and agnostics, it is not unusual for the rational man of faith to feel the need for reassurance.
segments.label: page - Introduction

segments.text: Abraham asked God for proof of a certain disputed matter and God inquired: "Do you not then believe?" Abraham responded: "Yes, but I seek to reassure my heart." (Qur'an 2:260) Further, this request was not rebuffed by the Almighty; rather, God provided Abraham with demonstrable evidence which made more firm the belief he possessed already. The conclusions based on Dr. Khalifa's astounding research provide similar faith-strengthening evidence. They make it evident that for all eternity no one will be able to meet the challenge to write a book like the Qur'an or to write so much as a sura (chapter) like its suras. Nothing as magnificent as the Qur'an exists in ancient history, and if any man or group of men could live for a thousand years with just one task: to create
segments.label: page - Introduction

segments.text: a book like the Qur'an, it is unlikely even then that they would succeed. Instead, science confirms that the Qur'an is beyond human capacity to compose or duplicate. God tells us in sura Al-Qiyāmat, verse 17, that the responsibility to compose the Qur'an and determine its method of recitation is His alone. Now, for the first time, as a result of this painstaking research, the world can appreciate how impressive and intricate a matter composing the Qur'an was, and how balanced and beautiful a composition it is! Those who believe in the Qur'an will have their belief intensified with this proof of the Qur'an's unique arrangement. Those not possessing such faith already will nevertheless have objective, tangible evidence which demonstrates to them the miracle of the Qur'an. The Qur'an is God's word, His Revelation to all mankind, the Book par excellence for guiding and developing the human family into a progressive unit. It behooves all mankind to pay attention to this Guidance. Sulayman Shahid Mufassir
segments.label: page

The references which offered some explanation unanimously declared that their tafseers were purely speculative. No definite tafseer was found. In relaxed determination not to pass up a single word without a reasonable understanding of its tafseer, research was launched to find out the significance of Alif Lām Mīm.
